**EVE-M**

Records your skin under light that is the same every time, and measures pigment, redness, pores and moisture. That way progress can be seen.

The EVE-M maps the condition of your skin and shows what is not always visible to the naked eye: early pigmentation, moisture shortage, pore structure and signs of skin ageing. Different layers of skin are analysed, and by repeating the measurement, progress becomes objectively visible.

- Consultation with EVE-M skin analysis € 50

The therapist chooses the settings based on your skin, your health, the treatment area and the goal of the treatment.

**What this device actually does**

The EVE-M records your skin and measures. Your face goes into a fixed rest, so that the distance and the angle are the same at every capture, and the lighting comes from the device itself and not from the room.

A phone photo under different light and from a different distance cannot be compared with a previous one. After eight weeks you still do not know whether anything has changed.

Besides ordinary light it also records under UV. Pigment sitting deeper in the skin is barely visible in ordinary light and is visible under UV, and it is exactly that depth that decides what is possible.

**Where this device is meant for**

On the left what this device was made for, on the right when something else does more for you.

- Recording what is there now, in a way that is still comparable months later

- Seeing what sits beneath the surface before it becomes visible

- Checking the progress of a programme rather than estimating it

- Treating. Nothing happens to your skin

- Making a diagnosis. A doctor does that

- Predicting what a treatment is going to give

**Frequently asked questions**

What does this device do to my skin?

Your face goes into a fixed rest and the lighting comes from the device itself. It takes images and measures; nothing touches your skin.

Why not simply a photo on a phone?

Because it cannot be compared with a previous one. A different distance, different light, a different angle – and then after eight weeks you still do not know whether anything has changed or whether the sun was in a different place.

What do I see under UV that I otherwise do not?

Pigment sitting deeper in the skin. In ordinary light that is barely visible, and it is exactly that depth that decides what is possible.

Do I get a diagnosis?

No. A measurement is not a diagnosis; that is a doctor's work. What you get is what has been measured and what that means for what is possible.

**The difference is in the hand that operates it**

The same EVE-M gives a different result in two clinics. What counts is the measurement beforehand, the setting that belongs with it and the therapist who judges what suits your skin.

**What this device actually does**

The TimeWalker carries two lasers in one cabinet. An Er:YAG at 2940 nanometres, which is absorbed almost entirely by water and so stays at the surface. And an Nd:YAG at 1064 nanometres, which is held back far less by water and so reaches deeper.

What is special is the way Fotona drives the Er:YAG. In SMOOTH mode the energy comes as a series of slow pulses instead of one hard one, so that the tissue heats up without the epidermis being removed. That is the difference between vaporising and heating, and it is why this mode leaves no open skin.

The same SMOOTH mode sits behind NightLase, where the soft palate is treated instead of the skin of your face. The laser is the same; only the place and the setting differ.

**Where this device is meant for**

On the left what this device was made for, on the right when something else does more for you.

- Laser peel and fractional treatment of the skin

- Treating snoring with NightLase, the one use in which this device works on the palate

- Hair growth. A different device stands for that

- Working on tanned skin

- One session with a lasting result; it is always a series

**What is different from the other devices here**

Several devices here do the same thing to the eye. Which one you get depends on your skin and on what was measured. Below is how they differ from one another.

- COMPARED WITH GentleMax Pro Aims at melanin and so at the hair root. The Fotona aims at water and so at tissue: a different target with a different effect. TO THE GENTLEMAX PRO ›

**Frequently asked questions**

Why are there two lasers in one device?

Because they do different things. The Er:YAG at 2940 nanometres is almost entirely absorbed by water and so stays at the surface; the Nd:YAG at 1064 nanometres goes much deeper. Together they cover a range one laser does not reach.

What is SMOOTH mode?

A way of driving the Er:YAG in which the energy comes in a series of slow pulses rather than one hard one. So the tissue warms up without the epidermis being removed: it is heated and not vaporised.

Is this the same device as with NightLase?

Yes, and the same mode. Only the place differs: with NightLase it is the soft palate and not the skin of your face.

You feel warmth that rises slowly. During the session the therapist asks about it and adjusts the device to your answer.

### /en/equipment/gentlemax-pro

**Tabbladtitel:** GentleMax Pro: the device | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** The laser for hair removal. It aims at the pigment in the hair root and cools the skin around it, with two wavelengths for every skin type.

**GENTLEMAX PRO**

The laser for hair removal. It aims at the pigment in the hair root and cools the skin around it, with two wavelengths for every skin type.

A laser that tackles unwanted hair growth at its core, reduces ingrown hairs and irritation and gives lastingly smooth, calm skin. Whatever absorbs the energy heats up, the rest does not.

- Laser hair removal € 20

The therapist chooses the settings based on your skin, your health, the treatment area and the goal of the treatment.

GENTLEMAX PRO, CANDELA

**Which concerns we treat with it**

Per concern it says which treatment is used for it. Which one suits you is established by the skin therapist at the intake.

- Ingrown hairs Laser hair removal € 20 ABOUT INGROWN HAIRS

**What this device actually does**

Candela's Gentle series works with an alexandrite laser at 755 nanometres. That wavelength is strongly absorbed by melanin, the pigment that gives a hair its colour. So the energy travels down the hair shaft to the root and the skin around it stays relatively untouched.

The pulse duration is adjustable from a quarter of a millisecond to a hundred milliseconds, and the spot size from 6 to 18 millimetres. Those are the two dials that matter: a thick, dark hair asks for something other than a fine one, and a large spot reaches deeper than a small one.

What sets this device apart is the cooling. With the Dynamic Cooling Device, Candela sprays a burst of cryogen onto the skin, milliseconds before and after the pulse. The epidermis cools back down while the hair root holds the heat. That is why higher energy is possible with this laser than would be responsible without that cooling.

**Where this device is meant for**

On the left what this device was made for, on the right when something else does more for you.

- Hair growth on almost any area of the body

- Reducing ingrown hairs and irritation from shaving

- Adjustable to different skin types

- Pigment spots or texture. Those are other devices

- Grey or very light hair, because there is too little pigment in it

- Tanned skin

**What is different from the other devices here**

Several devices here do the same thing to the eye. Which one you get depends on your skin and on what was measured. Below is how they differ from one another.

- COMPARED WITH Fotona TimeWalker Aims at water and works on tissue. This laser aims at melanin, and that is why it hits the hair root and not the skin around it. TO THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER ›

- COMPARED WITH Nordlys Is not a laser but a lamp with a bundle of wavelengths. That works less precisely on the hair root and goes less deep. TO THE NORDLYS ›

- COMPARED WITH Precision Photonic System Works with light on the skin itself. This laser works on the hair root: two different targets. TO THE PRECISION PHOTONIC SYSTEM ›

**The concerns this device fits.**

Every page below also says what this device is not for, and whether we treat that concern at all.

**Frequently asked questions**

Why this laser and not the Nordlys?

The alexandrite at 755 nanometres is strongly absorbed by the pigment in a hair, and that makes it precise on the hair root. The Nordlys works with a band instead of a single wavelength and is therefore broader but less precise on hair. Which one you get depends on your skin type and the area.

What exactly does the cooling do?

Just before and after every pulse the device sprays a burst of cryogen onto your skin. That cools the top layer back down while the heat stays in the hair root. You feel it as a cold tap around the warm pulse.

Why does it feel different on my upper lip than on my legs?

The spot size and the pulse duration are chosen per area, and the skin is not equally thick or equally sensitive everywhere. On a small, sensitive area the therapist works with a different setting than on a large one.

Is this possible on darker skin?

That depends on the setting. With more pigment in the skin the margin is smaller, so the therapist judges it beforehand. If it is not safe, we do not do it.

**The difference is in the hand that operates it**

The same GentleMax Pro gives a different result in two clinics. What counts is the measurement beforehand, the setting that belongs with it and the therapist who judges what suits your skin.

**What this device actually does**

The working part is the tip, not the cabinet. Inside the tip is a spiral channel under suction with fluid running through it at the same time. Those two together make a swirling movement across the skin: loosened cells and pore contents are carried out, through a side channel into a collection jar, while serum goes in via the same channel.

That is called Vortex-Fusion: cleansing, loosening, suctioning away and delivering happen in the same pass, with one hand.

The tips are single-use and there are different kinds, with a coarser or finer spiral. Which one is used depends on your skin and on the goal of the treatment.

### /en/equipment/nordlys-ipl

**Tabbladtitel:** Nordlys: the device | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** IPL works with a range of wavelengths rather than one. So it is broadly usable and goes less deep than a laser.

**NORDLYS**

IPL works with a range of wavelengths rather than one. So it is broadly usable and goes less deep than a laser.

IPL sends not a single wavelength into the skin but a range, with a filter that takes out the coarsest part. So it hits several targets at once: redness, visible vessels and surface pigment. On average it goes less deep than a laser.

- Nordlys IPL for pigmentation € 75

- Nordlys IPL for redness and vessels € 75

The therapist chooses the settings based on your skin, your health, the treatment area and the goal of the treatment.

NORDLYS, CANDELA

**Which concerns we treat with it**

Per concern it says which treatment is used for it. Which one suits you is established by the skin therapist at the intake.

- Pigmentation Nordlys IPL for pigmentation € 75 ABOUT PIGMENTATION

- Age spots Nordlys IPL for pigmentation € 75 ABOUT AGE SPOTS

- Skin discolouration Nordlys IPL for pigmentation € 75 ABOUT SKIN DISCOLOURATION

- Rosacea Nordlys IPL for redness and vessels € 75 ABOUT ROSACEA

- Couperose Nordlys IPL for redness and vessels € 75 ABOUT COUPEROSE

**What this device actually does**

Candela's Nordlys is not a laser but IPL: intense pulsed light. A laser emits one wavelength, IPL a band. Candela calls its variant Selective Waveband Technology: two filters cut the top and bottom off the spectrum, leaving a narrower band than ordinary IPL, with pulses shorter than a millisecond.

Which band comes out depends on the applicator. The manufacturer supplies several, from 530 to 750 nanometres for pigment to 645 to 950 nanometres for hair growth. Every band is chosen around what it has to hit: haemoglobin in a vessel, melanin in a spot.

The same device can also work with an Nd:YAG at 1064 nanometres, and with fractional lasers at 1550 and 1940 nanometres. Those go deeper than the IPL light and do different work.

**Where this device is meant for**

On the left what this device was made for, on the right when something else does more for you.

- Redness and visible vessels on the face

- Surface pigment across a large area

- Working fast where reach counts for more than precision

- Anything deep. The light does not reach there

- One specific spot; a laser is more precise for that

- Every skin type

**What is different from the other devices here**

Several devices here do the same thing to the eye. Which one you get depends on your skin and on what was measured. Below is how they differ from one another.

- COMPARED WITH Fotona TimeWalker One wavelength per mode, right down into the dermis. The Nordlys works more broadly and more superficially, and that suits vessels and pigment sitting just under the skin. TO THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER ›

- COMPARED WITH GentleMax Pro One wavelength, aimed at the hair root. The Nordlys is less suited to that, and better suited to redness. TO THE GENTLEMAX PRO ›

- COMPARED WITH Precision Photonic System Works with light that calms the skin. The Nordlys aims at the red in blood and uses heat for that. TO THE PRECISION PHOTONIC SYSTEM ›

**Frequently asked questions**

Is IPL the same as laser?

No. A laser emits one wavelength, IPL a band. So that band hits several things at once – redness, vessels and surface pigment – and on average goes less deep.

Why does a spot get darker first?

That is part of it. The pigment comes to the surface before it fades, and that takes a number of days. It does not mean it is getting worse.

What decides which applicator I get?

What the treatment is aimed at. For pigment the therapist chooses a different band than for hair growth; that is why there are several.

Can this be done on my legs or back too?

IPL works across a large area and that is exactly its strength. Whether it suits your concern depends on what is there and how deep.

**What this product line actually does**

A peel is not a device but a liquid, and what it does depends on three things: which acid is in it, how concentrated it is and how acidic the mixture is as a whole. Those three together decide how deep it goes.

Fruit acids stay in the horny layer and are washed off again after a few minutes. Salicylic acid dissolves in oil and so gets into the pore, where water-soluble acids do not reach. Stronger mixtures go into the epidermis and sometimes below it, and those ask for preparation and recovery time.

Which range and which strength suits you depends on your skin type, on what you are using at the moment and on the season.

**Where this product line is meant for**

On the left what this product line was made for, on the right when something else does more for you.

- Lightening surface discolouration

- Roughness and a dull texture

- Blocked pores, because the top layer renews faster

- Scars deeper than the epidermis

- Pregnancy and breastfeeding

- Just before a lot of sun

**What is different from the other devices here**

Several devices here do the same thing to the eye. Which one you get depends on your skin and on what was measured. Below is how they differ from one another.

- COMPARED WITH Dermaplane pro Scrapes the top layer off with a blade. A peel dissolves it, and depending on the range can go deeper. TO THE DERMAPLANE PRO ›

- COMPARED WITH Hydrafacial syndeo Works with a mild combination of acid and suction with no recovery time. A peel goes further and so asks more in return. TO THE HYDRAFACIAL SYNDEO ›

**Frequently asked questions**

Why is there no device here?

Because a peel is not one. This is a liquid, and what it does depends on the acid, the concentration and the acidity of the mixture.

What decides how deep a peel goes?

Those three together. Fruit acids stay in the horny layer, salicylic acid dissolves in oil and so reaches into the pore, and stronger mixtures go into the epidermis.

Will I peel?

With a light peel usually not, with a stronger one yes. You hear that beforehand, because it decides when best to schedule this.

Is this possible in summer?

With pigment preferably not, and with the stronger ranges not either. Sun after a peel is exactly the combination that costs you the result.

Per concern it says which treatment is used for it. Which one suits you is established by the skin therapist at the intake.

- Rosacea LED therapy € 30 ABOUT ROSACEA

- Redness LED therapy € 30 ABOUT REDNESS

- Sensitive skin LED therapy € 30 ABOUT SENSITIVE SKIN

**What this device actually does**

LED works differently from a laser or IPL. Those heat a target in the skin, pigment or a vessel or water, and the result comes from the healing that follows. LED heats nothing: the light is absorbed by the skin and does its work in the cell itself.

In every cell are mitochondria, the parts that supply energy. Light of certain wavelengths is absorbed there, after which the cell has more energy available for repair and production. That effect is called photobiomodulation.

The colours most studied in the professional literature sit around 415 nanometres (blue), 633 nanometres (red) and 830 nanometres (near-infrared). Blue stays in the upper layers and is used for blemishes. Red reaches into the dermis, where the connective tissue sits. Near-infrared goes furthest, because that wavelength is held back least by the skin.

The skin stays intact, so there is nothing that has to heal: no redness, no waiting time and no instructions for home. That is exactly why it fits straight after a treatment that does prompt the skin, such as microneedling or a peel.

It works cumulatively. One session is one prompt; the difference builds across a series, with a few days to a week in between. The therapist chooses the wavelength and the time based on what came out of the skin analysis.

**Where this device is meant for**

On the left what this device was made for, on the right when something else does more for you.

- Calming redness and rosacea

- Supporting recovery after needling or a peel

- Adding to a treatment without extra recovery time

- For pigment or hair growth you choose laser or IPL

- For texture and scars, microneedling works deeper

- Light works through repetition, so you plan a series

**What is different from the other devices here**

Several devices here do the same thing to the eye. Which one you get depends on your skin and on what was measured. Below is how they differ from one another.

- COMPARED WITH Nordlys Aims at the vessels themselves and works with heat. The Precision Photonic System works with light the skin absorbs, and so has no recovery time. TO THE NORDLYS ›

- COMPARED WITH Fotona TimeWalker Breaks tissue down to provoke repair. LED works more gently: light that calms the skin and supports the repair. TO THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER ›

**The concerns this device fits.**

Every page below also says what this device is not for, and whether we treat that concern at all.

**Frequently asked questions**

Do I feel anything of this?

Little. Light comes at a low strength and at most you notice mild warmth. Most people find it the calmest quarter of an hour of their week.

Why different colours?

Every wavelength reaches a different depth. Blue stays in the upper layers, red reaches into the dermis and near-infrared goes furthest, because that colour is held back least by the skin.

Does this work on its own?

With redness and rosacea people book it as a separate series. Otherwise we use it alongside another treatment, where it calms the skin and supports the recovery.

Is there recovery time?

No. You walk straight out with it and carry on with your day.

How often do I need to come?

Light works cumulatively, so the difference builds across a series with a few days to a week in between. How many sessions that is you hear after the skin analysis.

**The difference is in the hand that operates it**

The same Precision Photonic System gives a different result in two clinics. What counts is the measurement beforehand, the setting that belongs with it and the therapist who judges what suits your skin.

> knop: WHAT HAPPENS IN A SKIN CONSULTATION

> knop: ALL EQUIPMENT

- THE MEASUREMENT Under UV and in normal light, so that you know what is there and how deep.

- THE SETTING Strength, depth and pulse duration are chosen for your skin, not to a standard.

- THE HONEST NO If this does not fit what is going on with you, we say so.

### /en/equipment/skinpen-cit

**Tabbladtitel:** SkinPen CIT: the device | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Medically certified microneedling: controlled pricks at a set depth that prompt the skin to repair.

**SKINPEN CIT**

Medically certified microneedling: controlled pricks at a set depth that prompt the skin to repair.

With fine needles, channels are made down into the upper dermis. The skin answers with repair and collagen production; that repair is the goal, the pricks are the occasion for it. So it takes weeks before you see anything.

- Microneedling with the SkinPen € 180

The therapist chooses the settings based on your skin, your health, the treatment area and the goal of the treatment.

SKINPEN CIT, SKINPEN

**Which concerns we treat with it**

Per concern it says which treatment is used for it. Which one suits you is established by the skin therapist at the intake.

- Scars and stretch marks Microneedling with the SkinPen € 180 ABOUT SCARS AND STRETCH MARKS

- Skin ageing Microneedling with the SkinPen € 180 ABOUT SKIN AGEING

- Pores Microneedling with the SkinPen € 180 ABOUT PORES

- Pigmentation Microneedling with the SkinPen € 180 ABOUT PIGMENTATION

- Dull skin Microneedling with the SkinPen € 180 ABOUT DULL SKIN

- Acne scars Microneedling with the SkinPen € 180 ABOUT ACNE SCARS

- Stretch marks Microneedling with the SkinPen € 180 ABOUT STRETCH MARKS

- Lines and wrinkles Microneedling with the SkinPen € 180 ABOUT LINES AND WRINKLES

**What this device actually does**

A microneedling pen drives a cartridge of needles in a fast up-and-down motion. The SkinPen has fourteen, and the depth is adjustable from a quarter of a millimetre to three millimetres. That range runs from just through the horny layer to into the connective tissue.

The depth is the only setting that really matters, because it decides in which layer the channel ends. Shallow reaches the epidermis and heals within a day; three millimetres reaches the layer where connective tissue is made and takes longer.

The cartridges are sterile and single-use. With microneedling the needles go through the skin barrier, so that matters.

**Where this device is meant for**

On the left what this device was made for, on the right when something else does more for you.

- Scars formed by loss of structure

- Fine lines and uneven texture

- Reaching the layer a peel does not get to

- Colour on its own

- One session with a result

- Skin with active inflammation

**What is different from the other devices here**

Several devices here do the same thing to the eye. Which one you get depends on your skin and on what was measured. Below is how they differ from one another.

- COMPARED WITH Dermapen 4 Does the same thing: making channels so that your skin repairs itself. The difference is in the device and not in the principle, and which of the two fits depends on your skin and the area. TO THE DERMAPEN 4 ›

- COMPARED WITH U225 intradermal injector Also pricks, but to leave something behind. The SkinPen leaves nothing behind and works with the prompt alone. TO THE U225 INTRADERMAL INJECTOR ›

**Frequently asked questions**

What is the difference from the Dermapen?

The motor design and the number of needles. The SkinPen has fourteen and works a little more calmly; the Dermapen reaches more pricks per second. The depth range on both is 0.25 to 3 millimetres.

Why does the depth matter so much?

Because it decides in which layer the channel ends. Shallow reaches the epidermis and heals within a day; three millimetres reaches the connective tissue and takes longer.

Are the needles per person?

Yes. The cartridges are sterile and single-use. With microneedling that is not a detail: the needles go through the skin barrier, and that is what the barrier was for.

Does it hurt?

Beforehand a numbing cream goes on that takes half an hour to work. What you feel after that is vibration and pressure, strongest where the skin lies thin over bone.

### /en/equipment/u225

**Tabbladtitel:** U225 intradermal injector: the device | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Delivers active ingredients into the skin rather than onto it. The injector works automatically, so every injection lands at the same depth.

**U225 INTRADERMAL INJECTOR**

Delivers active ingredients into the skin rather than onto it. The injector works automatically, so every injection lands at the same depth.

In mesotherapy active ingredients are brought directly into the skin. The U225 does that automatically and evenly; the needle is mounted separately from the syringe, which improves the precision of the delivery. There are various skin boosters, including a depigmentation booster for face, neck and décolleté.

- Skin boosters and mesotherapy € 175

- XL Hair € 800

The therapist chooses the settings based on your skin, your health, the treatment area and the goal of the treatment.

U225 INTRADERMAL INJECTOR, U225

**Which concerns we treat with it**

Per concern it says which treatment is used for it. Which one suits you is established by the skin therapist at the intake.

- Skin ageing Skin boosters and mesotherapy € 175 ABOUT SKIN AGEING

- Melasma Skin boosters and mesotherapy € 175 ABOUT MELASMA

- Dark circles Skin boosters and mesotherapy € 175 ABOUT DARK CIRCLES

- Lines and wrinkles Skin boosters and mesotherapy € 175 ABOUT LINES AND WRINKLES

**What this device actually does**

The U225 is an injector, not a laser and not a device that works on the skin. An air-pressure system pushes an adjustable amount of liquid through a fine needle, at a depth between one and ten millimetres, up to eight times per second.

What sets it apart from injecting by hand is that only the needle moves and the syringe stays still. So there is less vibration and the depth is the same from injection to injection, even when a few hundred follow one another.

What is in the syringe decides the treatment, not the device. That can be a skin booster or a mesotherapy mixture, and that choice belongs with the therapist.

What exactly does this device do?

It delivers liquid into the skin at a set depth, between one and ten millimetres, up to eight times per second. It is an injector and not a device that works on the skin.

Why not simply inject by hand?

Because only the needle moves and the syringe stays still. So there is less vibration and the depth is the same from injection to injection, even when a few hundred follow one another.

### /en/gentlemax-pro

**Tabbladtitel:** Which laser suits your skin type | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Two lasers in one device: 755 nm and 1064 nm. Which of the two you get depends on your skin type, and that is a safety choice and not a detail.

**TWO LASERS IN ONE DEVICE.**

Everywhere you read that this device works on skin types I to VI. What is rarely added is why: there are two different wavelengths in it, and your skin type decides which of the two you get.

That is not a detail for technicians. It is the difference between a good treatment and a burn.

How do you hit a hair root without hitting the skin around it?

The laser aims at pigment: it absorbs the light, heats up and damages the root. That only works if the root absorbs more than the skin around it. If there is pigment in the top layer too, it absorbs along, and then the whole set-up no longer holds.

That is what the second wavelength is for.

**Which laser do you get?**

Choose your skin type and you see which of the two is used, how deep it goes and why it is the right one for you.

CHOOSE YOUR SKIN TYPE

The Fitzpatrick scale is about how your skin responds to sun, not about how it looks. If you are not sure, it is established at the intake.

> knop: II

> knop: III

> knop: IV

Light to medium

There is little pigment in the top layer to absorb on the way, so the 755 reaches the root. That is also why it is the stronger of the two here.

Schematic. The proportions are not accurate to the millimetre.

WITH SKIN TYPE III WE WORK WITH

755 nm

Alexandrite

Still enough difference between skin and hair root. The setting is more cautious than with type I, though, and the test patch is not a formality here.

- 755 nm Alexandrite Very strongly absorbed by pigment On light skin this is the stronger of the two. The hair root absorbs almost everything and the skin around it barely anything, so less energy is needed for the same effect. THE OTHER SIDE If there is pigment in the top layer of the skin as well, it absorbs along. So this wavelength is not the right choice on dark skin.

- 1064 nm Nd:YAG Absorbed far less by pigment The light largely passes the top layer and goes deeper. So this is the safe choice on skin with a lot of its own pigment, and also the better one for deep-lying hair roots. THE OTHER SIDE Less absorption means less yield per pulse. More energy is needed, and that feels firmer than the alexandrite.

**The cooling belongs with the pulse.**

Just before every laser pulse a coolant goes onto the skin. That protects the top layer at the moment the energy passes through it, and it makes the treatment more bearable.

So laser hair removal feels like a short tap with something cold around it and not like a burning point. Without that cooling, the energy the root needs would put too much strain on the skin above it.

> knop: Read on

WHAT YOU WILL FEEL

A short tap with something cold around it, repeated across the area. Exactly how it feels differs per place: on a shin it is sharper than on a thigh, because there is less in between.

**What it costs you.**

This page is about the device. Which areas there are, what a session costs and how many sessions go into a programme is on the treatment page. There you work it out yourself, per area, without an amount being held back until the desk.

**Google-omschrijving:** If there is a medical reason for your concern, there is a route to insurance cover. Three questions in order, and with each one where you stand.

**COVER FROM YOUR HEALTH INSURER**

If there is a medical reason for your concern, there is a route. With most insurers skin therapy sits in the supplementary package, and from there it is about your policy: which package you have, which maximum comes with it and whether your GP has to write a referral.

Conditions and maximums change per year and per package. So your current amount is in your own policy, and there it is actually right. What is here is how it works, and that stays the same from year to year.

> knop: Read on

- Contracted with all health insurers You do not have to work out whether we are contracted with your insurer. We are, with all of them.

- Dutch Quality Register for Paramedics Our skin therapists are listed. Many supplementary packages set that as a condition for cover.

- Dutch Association of Skin Therapists Our skin therapists are members of the professional association. For members, registration in the Dutch Quality Register for Paramedics is mandatory.

- Member of ANBOS The trade association for beauty therapists, with requirements on training, hygiene and complaints handling.

- SKIN Register The quality register for beauty therapists. Our beauty therapists are listed in it by name.

**Choose your insurer, see where to look**

Per insurer it says where in the policy to look and which condition sits in it most often. What exactly is in your package, you only see there.

- CZ

- VGZ

- Menzis

- Zilveren Kruis

- ONVZ

- a.s.r.

- DSW (Stad Holland, inTwente)

- Zorg en Zekerheid

- Salland (HollandZorg)

- Aevitae (EUCARE)

> knop: START YOUR INTAKE

AT THE DESK, AFTERWARDS

**This is how the route to yes runs.**

With every question it says where you stand, including when the answer falls the other way. Most sites leave that half out, and it is exactly the half that is useful to you.

- FIRST QUESTION Is there a medical reason? This is the only question that really matters, and it is not about the treatment but about the concern. The same laser can be medical in one case and cosmetic in another. IF YES Then it falls under cosmetic care and you pay for it yourself. That holds at every clinic and every insurer, because that is how the system is set up. IF NO Then you move on to the second question. Whether there is a medical reason is decided by a doctor.

- SECOND QUESTION Is it in your supplementary insurance? With most insurers skin therapy sits in the supplementary package and not in the basic one. What exactly is in it differs per insurer and per package, and it changes yearly. IF YES Then you pay for it yourself, and that can be a perfectly good choice. You just know it beforehand, with the price attached. IF NO Then look straight away at the annual maximum and at whether a referral from your GP is needed. The latter is the most often overlooked.

- THIRD QUESTION Is a referral needed? Many packages only cover with a referral from your GP, and it has to be in place before the treatment starts. IF YES Then you can come directly. Do mention at the intake that you expect cover, so that we check straight away whether everything is in order. IF NO Then arrange it first, before your appointment. Insurers rarely accept a referral sent in afterwards, and that bill then stays with you.

**Together you get it sorted.**

Cover comes through when both sides do their part. Here is which part is ours and which is yours, so that you know beforehand and not only when the bill arrives.

THIS IS WHAT WE DO

- Telling you what a treatment costs, beforehand and in full

- Putting on your invoice exactly what was done, so that you can submit it

- Saying at the intake if we think there is a medical route you have not yet taken

THIS IS WHAT YOU DO

- Checking your policy conditions for skin therapy, or asking us where to look

- Getting a referral from your GP if your package requires one

- Submitting the invoice to your insurer afterwards

**The first one saves money.**

People put treatment off on the strength of something that is not true. So that one comes first.

- WHAT PEOPLE THINK This comes out of my excess With cover from your supplementary insurance, no. The excess belongs to the basic insurance. Many people put treatment off because they think they will first be hundreds of euros out of pocket, and that is not true here.

- WHAT PEOPLE THINK My insurer covers skin therapy, so it covers this too Cover hangs on the concern and on who carries out the treatment, not on the name of the treatment. Two people with the same appointment can get a different answer.

- WHAT PEOPLE THINK The clinic will sort that out for me We put on your invoice exactly what was done, so that you can submit it. What your policy covers is only in your policy, and that conversation you have with your insurer. If you do not know where to look, ask us at the intake.

- WHAT PEOPLE THINK I will hear about it later A referral or an approval only counts if it is in place before the treatment starts. Arrange it in advance and it is usually a matter of one call to your GP.

### /en/intake

**Tabbladtitel:** The skin consultation: what happens | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** What happens in the skin consultation, how long it takes and what it costs. If you are treated in the same appointment, the intake fee is waived.

**WHAT HAPPENS IN AN INTAKE**

The therapist looks at your skin and measures with the EVE-M under fixed lighting. You watch along on the screen and hear what is possible for you, in which order and over how many sessions.

If you are treated in the same appointment, the intake fee is waived. You decide in your own time what you do next.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

*RESERVED*

Max. 30 minutes

*COST*

€ 50

*COMMITMENT*

None

*TREATMENT THIS APPOINTMENT*

THE SAME SCREEN, TOGETHER

Both start with the same measurement.

The skin consultation

We reserve at most 30 minutes for it: the conversation, the assessment of your skin and advice you take home with you. Nothing happens to your skin in this appointment.

It costs 50 euros. If you choose the appointment in which treatment is also possible, that amount is waived as soon as we treat.

Measure and start straight away

Book your first appointment

If we treat, you pay only the price of the treatment. The intake is then not charged separately. If no treatment is carried out, you pay 50 euros for the intake.

Whether that is possible depends on what the measurement shows, on any contraindications, on the time available that day and on what you want. If treating turns out not to be sensible at that moment, we do not do it.

This appointment is called treatment on advice. If you are already a client the intake is not needed again and it takes 60 minutes.

Of those 120 minutes, at least 60 minutes is treatment time.

Bring your skin profile

In 9 steps record what you want to change and what your skin can take. Retinol, pregnancy, tanned skin, medication: with those answers your treatment is ready before you walk in.

> knop: BUILD YOUR SKIN PROFILE

**What happens in that hour**

Most hesitation before an intake is about whether you will walk out with a package. So it is stated at every step, and not once in the small print.

**Frequently asked questions**

Will I be called afterwards to buy something after all?

No. You hear from us when you arrange something yourself or ask a question. There is no call round and there is no offer that expires.

What if the outcome is that I should do nothing?

Then we say so and it stops there. That happens more often than you think, and it is why the measurement stands apart from the treatment.

Can I have a treatment straight away?

Yes. Book your intake with treatment and we reserve time for it and the intake fee is waived. We measure first, so that later you can check what it did.

Do I have to come separately for every concern?

No. In one appointment we look at your whole skin, including things you did not come for. Often what bothers you and what is going on turn out not to be the same.

What happens to my photos?

They stay in your own file as a starting point. They are not used on our site or in advertising unless you give separate written permission, and you can always withdraw that.

I do not even know what I would come for.

That is a perfectly good reason to come. The symptom finder helps you find a direction, and otherwise the conversation simply starts with looking.

**One appointment, with no commitment**

You leave with a measurement that is yours and advice that is allowed to be no. What you do next, you decide at home.

### /en/knowledge/chemical-peel-rotterdam

**Tabbladtitel:** Chemical peel Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Chemical peel in Rotterdam at Diba Clinics. Four brands in three strengths, from € 140. For acne, pigment and dull skin.

**CHEMICAL PEEL IN ROTTERDAM**

A chemical peel is a treatment in which an acid loosens the bond between the outermost skin cells, so that this layer is replaced faster. At Diba Clinics in Rotterdam we work with four brands in three strengths. A peel costs from € 140 and takes 60 minutes; depending on the strength you are dry and flaky for two to five days afterwards.

> knop: BOOK AN APPOINTMENT

> knop: SEE THE PRICES

*DURATION*

*RATE*

From € 140

*RECOVERY TIME*

2 to 5 days

*STRENGTHS*

Three levels

**What a peel does to your skin**

A peel speeds up something your skin already does on its own: replacing the top layer. How far that goes depends on the agent.

Your skin replaces its top layer constantly, but not always at the same speed. If the old cells stay too long, your skin feels rough, looks dull, pores get blocked and surface discolouration stays longer than it needs to.

A peel loosens the bond between those outer cells, so that the layer is replaced faster. What the agent does depends on three things together: which acid is in it, how concentrated it is and how acidic the mixture is as a whole. Fruit acids stay in the horny layer, salicylic acid dissolves in sebum and so reaches into the pore, and stronger mixtures go into the epidermis.

On the site and in the calendar this is called a medical peel. Chemical peel is the same treatment, under the name most people search for.

It is worked out separately per concern: a peel for acne, for pigment spots and for skin rejuvenation. What the sun does around a peel is on sun and your skin, and what is possible during pregnancy on pregnancy or breastfeeding.

**Four brands in three strengths**

A peel is not a device but a liquid. Which one suits you depends on your skin at that moment and on the season.

We work with peels from Skin Tech Pharma, Dermaceutic, ADO and Mesoestetic, in three levels. The lightest work on the top layer and usually do not make you peel visibly. The strongest, such as Dermaceutic's TCA peel at 12 to 20 per cent, go deeper and ask for preparation and recovery time.

The working time is measured against your skin. Leaving it on longer gives no better result but more damage, which is why the therapist stays with you as long as the peel is on your skin.

For skin with inflamed acne an acid is sometimes too much. For that there is the herbal peel from ADO: finely ground herbs without acid, which are anti-inflammatory and antibacterial. Afterwards the skin is red and peeling for three to five days.

> knop: ABOUT THE TREATMENT

**What a peel costs with us**

The amount depends on the peel, the area and whether you book a course. With some courses the products for home use are included.

- Mesoestetic peel € 140

- TCA Dermaceutic 12 to 20% € 180

- Mesoestetic peel, back € 160

- Mesoestetic back course of three € 399

- TCA course of three with three products € 650

- TCA course of three with K-ceutic € 540

- Herbal peel, face € 150

- Herbal peel, back € 200

- Herbal peel, back course of three € 499

Peels usually work in a series of four to six, with two to four weeks in between. How many that becomes for you, you hear after the measurement.

**Is this your first visit**

Then you book a treatment on advice. We reserve at most two hours for that: the intake, and then at least an hour to treat. If treating is safe at that moment and you want it, we do the first peel in the same appointment.

**What the intake costs**

If you are treated in the same appointment, the intake fee is waived and you pay only for the treatment. If the treatment does not go ahead, the intake costs € 50. A separate intake without treatment lasts at most 30 minutes and always costs € 50.

**Have you been here before**

Then you book the peel directly in the calendar. Count on 60 minutes. If anything has changed since your last visit in your skin, your medication or your expectation, say so when you arrive.

**What helps and what we advise against**

A peel works on the upper layers. For scars that sit deeper and for stubborn pigment there is a heavier route.

**THIS WORKS**

- Surface discolouration, and pigment left behind after a spot

- Rough skin and a dull texture

- Blocked pores, because the top layer renews faster

- Inflamed acne, with the herbal peel or a peel tuned to it

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Scars that sit deeper than the epidermis. For those you choose microneedling

- Stubborn pigment or melasma. There Cosmelan and Dermamelan are the heavier programmes

- Peeling just before a lot of sun, or with pigment in the summer months

- During pregnancy or while you are breastfeeding

**The peel alongside the alternatives**

For better skin texture there are several routes. This is what they do, what you notice afterwards and what they cost.

*WHERE IT DIFFERS*

*FROM*

*Medical peels*

An acid loosens the top layer. Three strengths, from barely peeling to a few days of flaking.

Two to five days dry and flaky, depending on the strength.

Three to five days.

*HydraFacial*

Cleanses and empties pores, without acid and without peeling. Less effect on discolouration, and you see the result straight away.

There is usually no recovery time and you can carry on with your day after the appointment.

Works with needles in the dermis, deeper than a peel. For scars and texture.

One to three days red, like a strong sun flush.

A six-month programme against stubborn pigment, with a mask in the clinic and products at home.

**Frequently asked questions**

What does a chemical peel cost in Rotterdam?

At Diba Clinics a Mesoestetic peel costs € 140 and a TCA peel from Dermaceutic € 180. A herbal peel costs € 150 for the face. There are also courses of three, some with products for home use. If it is your first visit, your appointment starts with a € 50 intake, which is waived if we treat in the same appointment.

What is the difference between a chemical and a medical peel?

There is no difference; they are two names for the same treatment. We call it a medical peel, because these are agents chosen per skin and measured against your skin. Chemical peel is the name most people search for.

Will I peel after a peel?

With a light peel usually not, with a stronger one yes. With the stronger versions count on two to five days dry and flaky. You hear that beforehand, because it decides when best to schedule the treatment.

Can I have a peel in summer?

With pigment, preferably not, and with the stronger peels not either. Sun on freshly peeled skin is exactly the combination that costs you the result. A light peel for texture is sometimes possible, with strict sun protection.

How many peels do I need?

Usually a series of four to six, with two to four weeks in between. How many that becomes for you depends on your skin and on how it reacts; we measure that along the way.

Does a chemical peel help against acne?

Yes, peels are one of the most important tools for acne. With inflamed acne we work with chemical peels and with the herbal peel, which is antibacterial as well. We only tackle scars once the skin is calm.

Does a peel help against pigmentation?

With surface discolouration yes, such as the marks left after a spot. If the pigment sits deeper or it is melasma, a programme like Cosmelan or Dermamelan is the fitter answer. Which of the two it is, we establish with a measurement.

Is a peel possible on darker skin?

Yes, and it asks for a different approach. With skin types IV to VI the chance of new pigment spots from the treatment is higher, so we choose the strength more carefully and build up more slowly. We discuss that beforehand.

Where in Rotterdam are you?

At Weissenbruchlaan 166 in Rotterdam, on the north side of the city in a residential area. You park in the street. The route and the opening hours are on our contact page.

**Not sure which peel you need**

You do not have to know that before you come. We measure your skin, look at what is going on and choose the strength that fits. If a peel is not the right answer, you hear so.

If you know what you are after but are unsure about the timing or the combination with something else, ask via WhatsApp. There is a therapist on the other end and not a form.

### /en/knowledge/choosing-a-skin-clinic

**Tabbladtitel:** How to choose a skin clinic | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** What to look for in a skin clinic: which registers you can check yourself, what an intake should give you and how to read a before-and-after photo.

**HOW TO CHOOSE A SKIN CLINIC**

When choosing a skin clinic, four things can be checked without having been there: whether your therapist is in a public register, whether measuring comes before treating, whether the prices are on the site in advance, and whether it is explained when something is not sensible. The rest you only notice in the treatment room.

> knop: BOOK AN APPOINTMENT

> knop: SEE THE PRICES

*CAN BE CHECKED*

Public registers

*PROTECTED TITLE*

Skin therapist

*BEFOREHAND*

A measurement

*INDEPENDENT*

ZorgkaartNederland

**What you can check in advance**

Four things are online and can be checked in ten minutes. They do not say everything, but they say more than an impression of a website.

Skin therapist is a legally protected training title, set down in article 34 of the Dutch Individual Healthcare Professions Act. A four-year bachelor's degree in skin therapy belongs with it, and that programme exists in two places in the Netherlands. Beauty therapist is not a protected title; that says nothing about anyone's craft, but it does mean the title itself carries no guarantee.

The title says someone has done the training. The Dutch Quality Register for Paramedics says something else: that someone also practises the profession and keeps it current. Re-registration requires at least 1600 working hours over three years plus 160 points of continuing education. That register is public and you search it by name, including the name of your therapist at another clinic.

For the non-paramedical part of the work there are ANBOS and the SKIN Register. The first is the trade association with a code of conduct, hygiene guidelines and a complaints procedure; the second registers beauty therapists by name. Those can be looked up too.

And then there are the ratings. A score on the site itself is there because someone put it there. A rating kept outside the clinic, such as on ZorgkaartNederland run by the Dutch Patients Federation, cannot be placed or removed by the clinic, and so says more.

Which registers we belong to and how to check that is on quality and registrations. Who works here and with which title is on the team.

**What a first appointment gives you**

The second part you only see once you are inside, and it is the part that separates a treatment from a plan.

A first appointment should start with looking and measuring, and not with treating. Without a starting point there is no way to establish afterwards whether anything has changed, and then all that remains is the feeling that it was probably fine. So ask whether measuring happens, with what, and whether you get that image back.

Then a plan should follow setting out what is needed, how many times that is and what it costs. An amount that only lands in the treatment room is not a price agreement but a surprise. All rates should be findable in advance, and ours are on the price page.

The third is the hardest to ask and the most telling: what happens when treating is not sensible at that moment. Inflamed skin, tanned skin just before a laser treatment, a spot that has to be assessed by a doctor first. A no belongs with those, with a reason and an alternative.

Finally the photos. A before-and-after can only be compared if the light, the angle, the distance and the make-up are the same. If any of those differ, you are comparing two images and not a result. Ask how the images are taken, and whether you get to see your own side by side.

> knop: WHAT A SKIN CONSULTATION INVOLVES

**What helps and what we advise against**

These points say something about the way of working. About the outcome of your treatment they say less than people hope.

**THIS WORKS**

- Whether your therapist's title is protected, and whether the registration is in order

- Whether measuring happens before treating

- Whether the rate is findable in advance, versions and all

- Whether it is explained when something had better not happen

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Whether a treatment suits your skin. That only follows from the measurement

- How many sessions you need. A number beforehand is about someone else's skin

- Whether a more expensive device gives a better result. What counts is the choice behind it

- What it feels like to sit there. For that you have to have been once

**Seven things to ask about**

What you can check, how you do it, and how it is arranged here. The middle column works at any clinic, even if you do not come here.

Working here are five skin therapists, beauty therapists and orthomolecular skin specialists. Which title belongs with which treatment is listed per person on the team page, and who does your appointment you hear when you book it.

Who works here, with what title and what that title means exactly, is on the team page with photos and all.

**Frequently asked questions**

What should I look at in a before-and-after photo?

At light, angle, distance and make-up. If those four are the same, you are comparing a skin with the same skin. If any of them differ, you are comparing two images and the difference says nothing about the treatment. Ask too whether the photos come from a fixed device or from a phone.

Is a more expensive treatment better?

Not automatically. The price says something about the device, the time and the products, and nothing about whether that treatment suits your concern. A cheaper treatment that does the right thing gives more than an expensive one doing the wrong thing. That difference comes from the measurement and not from the price list.

Should I get a treatment plan on paper?

You should at least be told what is needed, how many sessions that is and what it costs, before you agree to anything. Here that conversation happens after the measurement, and you take the outcome with you. You are not committed to anything afterwards.

May I ask who will treat me?

Yes, and it is a normal question. Here the team page lists who works here and with which title, and when you book you hear who will do it. If you change therapist, your file with the measurements simply stays in place.

What if a clinic wants to treat straight away?

Then ask what that choice is based on. Treating without a measurement can turn out perfectly well, but afterwards there is no way to establish what has changed, and with a concern that does not respond you do not know where it went wrong. So here a first appointment starts with looking and measuring.

How do I know whether a clinic is contracted with my insurer?

That is in your insurer's provider finder and usually on the clinic's site too. A contract does not mean everything is reimbursed: that depends on your supplementary policy and on the indication. We are contracted with all Dutch health insurers.

Does a device certificate mean anything?

It says the device is what it is called, and that is useful. It says nothing about the settings it is used with, and that is exactly where the difference between a good and a mediocre treatment sits. So ask instead who operates the device and how the setting is chosen.

What is a reasonable outcome of a first appointment?

That you know what you have, what can be done about it, how many times that takes and what it costs. And that you hear what cannot be done about it. If the measurement turns up nothing that needs treating, that is an outcome too, and you have paid for a consultation instead of a programme.

Can I go somewhere with a complaint about a treatment?

Yes. For the paramedical part that goes through the professional association and the Dutch Quality Register for Paramedics; for the beauty part through the ANBOS complaints procedure. Those routes stand apart from the clinic itself, and that is exactly the point of them.

Where in Rotterdam are you?

### /en/knowledge/cosmelan-dermamelan-rotterdam

**Tabbladtitel:** Cosmelan and Dermamelan Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Cosmelan and Dermamelan in Rotterdam: six months, a mask in the clinic and products at home. For the face € 720 to € 920, products included.

**COSMELAN AND DERMAMELAN**

Cosmelan and Dermamelan are programmes of about six months against stubborn pigment: a mask in the clinic, and after that a fixed routine with products at home. Dermamelan is the stronger of the two and is used more often for melasma. At Diba Clinics in Rotterdam Cosmelan costs € 720 and Dermamelan € 920, products included.

> knop: BOOK AN APPOINTMENT

> knop: SEE THE PRICES

*DURATION*

Six months

*RATE*

€ 720 to € 920

*RECOVERY TIME*

Days of peeling

*BRAND*

Mesoestetic

**What the programme does with pigment**

Most treatments remove what is there. This programme also slows what is still being made, and that is why it takes months.

Pigment is made by cells in the bottom layer of the epidermis. With stubborn pigment those cells are, so to speak, turned up higher than they need to be, by sun, hormones and predisposition. Remove only what is there and in the months that follow they simply make it again.

Cosmelan and Dermamelan work on two fronts. The mask in the clinic slows production and makes the top layer with the pigment peel away. The products at home then keep that brake on, for months. That second part is not a side issue: it is the largest part of the programme, and it decides the outcome more than what happens in the clinic.

The programme starts with two weeks of preparation at home. Then the mask goes on in the clinic; you take it home and remove it yourself after the agreed number of hours. After a few days you start peeling, and from then on the routine follows, with check-ups along the way.

What pigment is and which type you have is on pigment spots and on melasma. The two treatments are set out separately at Cosmelan and Dermamelan. Why a programme does not start in summer is on sun and your skin.

**Cosmelan or Dermamelan**

The same set-up, a different strength and a different goal. Which one suits you is established by the therapist with a measurement.

Cosmelan is the lighter of the two. It is chosen more often for sun damage and separate pigment spots: sharply defined marks in the places the sun reaches. For that kind of pigment it is strong enough.

Dermamelan is more intensive and is used more often for melasma: symmetrical, cloud-like areas that react to hormones and heat and can come back after every summer. The schedule at home is stricter, because melasma returns as soon as the approach loosens. With melasma the goal is control rather than removal, and you hear that beforehand.

There is also a version for the intimate area, Dermamelan Intimate, for dark discolouration in the groin and bikini area. It follows the same set-up, happens in a closed room and with a therapist of your own choosing.

> knop: ABOUT COSMELAN

Preferably in autumn, so that you have months of little sun ahead of you. Between May and August we do not start a pigment programme. Do not schedule the start just before a holiday or a busy week either, because after a few days you start peeling.

**During the programme**

Two weeks of preparation at home, then the mask in the clinic, and after that the routine with products. Along the way there are check-ups, where we measure rather than estimate, so that you see whether the schedule is working.

**What helps and what we advise against**

This programme is for stubborn pigment. For pigment that sits near the surface, and for anyone not up for the work at home, there is a lighter route.

**Frequently asked questions**

What does Cosmelan cost in Rotterdam?

At Diba Clinics the Cosmelan programme costs € 720 and Dermamelan € 920, both including the products for home use. Dermamelan Intimate costs € 550. The programme starts with a € 50 intake.

What is the difference between Cosmelan and Dermamelan?

The same set-up, a different strength and a different goal. Cosmelan is the lighter one and is chosen more often for sun damage and separate pigment spots; Dermamelan is more intensive and is used more often for melasma. Which one suits you is established by the therapist at the intake.

How long does a Cosmelan programme take?

About six months. It starts with two weeks of preparation at home, then the mask goes on in the clinic, and after that a routine with products and check-ups follows.

Will I peel from Cosmelan?

Yes. After a few days your skin peels and is red. So do not schedule the start just before a holiday or an important date.

Why can I not start in summer?

Because then you spend months working against the sun. Pigment cells that have just been tackled react especially sharply to UV, and then you pay for a result you lose in September. So between May and August we do not start a pigment programme.

Does melasma go away with Dermamelan?

Not for good. Melasma remains something that can come back, especially after summer. Dermamelan can settle it, and with sun protection and the schedule at home you keep it that way. With melasma, control is the honest goal.

Is Cosmelan possible on darker skin?

Often yes, and it asks for a different approach. With skin types IV to VI the chance of new pigment spots is higher, so we look extra carefully beforehand and build up cautiously. We discuss that at the intake.

Can I have Cosmelan while pregnant?

No; during pregnancy and while you are breastfeeding we do not start it. Pigment often changes on its own in that period anyway, and then waiting is the best choice.

### /en/knowledge/dermaplaning-rotterdam

**Tabbladtitel:** Dermaplaning Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Dermaplaning in Rotterdam at Diba Clinics. € 150, sixty minutes and no recovery time. Without acids, so also for sensitive skin.

**DERMAPLANING IN ROTTERDAM**

Dermaplaning is a treatment in which a surgical blade, held at a fixed angle, removes dead skin cells and fine hairs from your face. No acids are involved. At Diba Clinics in Rotterdam a treatment takes 60 minutes and costs € 150; your skin is smooth straight away and you have no recovery time.

> knop: BOOK AN APPOINTMENT

> knop: SEE THE PRICES

*DURATION*

*RATE*

*RECOVERY TIME*

None

*METHOD*

Blade, no acid

**What dermaplaning does to your skin**

It is the simplest treatment in the clinic: a sterile blade, skin pulled taut and a fixed angle. No current, light or heat is involved.

The outer layer of your skin consists of dead cells that come away on their own, but not always smoothly. Among them sit the fine, light hairs almost everyone has on their face. Together they make the surface rougher than it needs to be, and make-up catches in it rather than going on smoothly.

In dermaplaning the therapist pulls your skin taut and the blade passes over it in short strokes, at an angle of 45 degrees. It does not cut into the skin but scrapes across the surface. What comes off are dead cells from the horny layer and the fine hairs caught in them; what stays is living skin.

Because no acid is involved, it also suits sensitive, dry or allergy-prone skin, and pregnancy. It does not hurt. The strangest part is the sound: a soft scraping you feel in your jaw more than on your skin.

How the blade and the angle work exactly is on the Dermaplane Pro. The treatment itself, apart from the place, is on the treatment page.

**Does the hair grow back thicker**

It is the question almost everyone asks, and the answer is no. Below is why.

Shaving and dermaplaning do not change the hair shaft, only the end. A hair that has never been cut has a thin, soft tip. After cutting, that tip is flat, and a flat end feels coarser for the first few days. That is what people mistake for thicker hair.

The hair grows back as it was: just as fine and just as light. It does not get darker and it does not come back faster. Those who like it come back roughly monthly, because in that time the layer of dead cells has built up again and the hairs are back.

If you want rid of the hairs instead of keeping them in check, this is the wrong treatment. For dark hair that is laser hair removal; for light, grey or white hair the laser cannot see, that is electrolysis.

**What helps and what we advise against**

Dermaplaning works on the outer layer. For what sits deeper, and for hair that should stay gone, there is a different treatment.

**THIS WORKS**

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

### /en/knowledge/electrolysis-rotterdam

**Tabbladtitel:** Electrolysis Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Electrolysis in Rotterdam: hair by hair, including grey, white and very light blond hair the laser cannot see. € 60 per half hour.

**ELECTROLYSIS HAIR REMOVAL**

Electrolysis is a hair removal method in which a fine needle follows the hair down to the root and switches it off with a short pulse of current, hair by hair. Because colour does not matter, it also works on grey, white and light blond hair that the laser does not respond to. At Diba Clinics in Rotterdam it costs € 60 per half hour of treatment time.

> knop: BOOK AN APPOINTMENT

> knop: SEE THE PRICES

*RATE*

*HAIR COLOUR*

Any colour

*AREA*

Small, hair by hair

*RECOVERY TIME*

A few hours red

**What electrolysis does**

Where the laser needs a colour to aim at, this goes straight to the root. That is why the colour of the hair does not matter here.

The laser aims at the pigment in the hair root. If there is no pigment left, as with grey, white and very light blond hair, there is nothing to aim at. That is not down to the device or the setting; that is how laser hair removal works.

In electrolysis a fine needle goes alongside the hair into the follicle, down to the root. That gets a short pulse of current, so it is the root itself that is dealt with and not the colour. Per hair you feel a short prick.

It goes hair by hair, which makes it slower than laser. So it is meant for small areas, such as the chin, the upper lip and around the eyebrow, and for the odd hairs left standing after a laser course. A hair only responds in its growth phase, so you come in a series, with a few weeks in between.

If your hair does have colour, laser hair removal is faster and better value. For hair growth caused by PCOS there is more on the PCOS page. The treatment itself is on the treatment page.

**Laser and electrolysis together**

The two do not rule each other out. In most cases it is an order of steps, and that saves you time and money.

If some of your hair still has colour, you start with a laser course. In one flash the laser covers a whole area and so works much faster than hair by hair. What is left afterwards, usually the light or grey hairs, goes with electrolysis. That way you do not pay per hair for what can be done faster.

If all your hair is grey, white or very light, electrolysis is the method meant for those hairs. That is not a second choice but the right treatment for that hair.

For large areas, such as legs or back, it is not suitable: hair by hair costs too much time and too many sessions there. You hear that at the intake too, along with what is possible in your case.

> knop: ABOUT LASER HAIR REMOVAL

The rate goes per half hour of treatment time, because it depends on how many hairs there are. The intake arrangement is set out in full.

How much time you need depends on the area and on the number of hairs. We estimate that at the intake, and after the first appointment you know better.

Then you book a treatment on advice. We reserve at most two hours for that: the intake, and then at least an hour to treat. If treating is safe at that moment and you want it, we do the first electrolysis in the same appointment.

**What the intake costs**

If you are treated in the same appointment, the intake fee is waived and you pay only for the treatment. If the treatment does not go ahead, the intake costs € 50. A separate intake without treatment lasts at most 30 minutes and always costs € 50.

**Have you been here before**

Then you book the electrolysis directly in the calendar. Count on 30 minutes. If anything has changed since your last visit in your skin, your medication or your expectation, say so when you arrive.

**What helps and what we advise against**

Electrolysis is precision work for small areas. For large areas with dark hair the laser is the better answer.

**THIS WORKS**

- The odd hairs left standing after a laser course

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

**Frequently asked questions**

What does electrolysis cost in Rotterdam?

Why does the laser not work on grey hair?

Because the laser seeks out the pigment in the hair root and the heat does its work there. Grey and white hair no longer has that pigment, so there is nothing to aim at. That is not down to the device or the setting.

Does electrolysis hurt?

Per hair you feel a short prick, and then a warm feeling in that spot. It is manageable, but because it goes hair by hair, a longer session is noticeable.

Is electrolysis permanent?

A hair whose root has been properly switched off does not come back. Because hairs are not all in their growth phase at the same time, you do need a series of appointments to settle an area. How many differs per person.

Can I combine it with laser hair removal?

That is the usual order. First the laser course for everything with pigment, and then electrolysis for the hairs left standing. That way you do not pay per hair for what can be done faster.

Which areas can you treat with electrolysis?

Small areas where precision matters more than speed: the chin, the upper lip and around the eyebrow. It is not meant for large areas such as legs or back; laser is faster and better value there.

How do I look after electrolysis?

The treated spots are red for a few hours and can swell slightly, much like after waxing. In most people that is gone the same day.

Does electrolysis help with hair growth from PCOS?

For the light hairs the laser cannot see, yes. With PCOS your body keeps making new hairs, so maintenance belongs with laser and with electrolysis alike. There is more about that on our page about PCOS.

### /en/knowledge/fitzpatrick-skin-type

**Tabbladtitel:** Fitzpatrick skin type: which type do you have | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** The six Fitzpatrick skin types, what yours says about laser, IPL and peels, and how to work it out yourself. Explained by the skin therapists at Diba Clinics.

**WHICH SKIN TYPE DO YOU HAVE**

The Fitzpatrick skin type is a scale of six types saying how your skin responds to sun: type I almost always burns and hardly tans, type VI rarely burns. For laser, IPL and peels your type decides not whether something is possible, but with which wavelength, which energy and how carefully it is built up. At Diba Clinics in Rotterdam we establish your type at the intake.

> knop: BOOK AN APPOINTMENT

> knop: SEE THE PRICES

*SCALE*

Six types, I to VI

*ABOUT*

Response to sun

*DECIDES*

The setting

*ESTABLISHED*

At the intake

**What a skin type actually says**

It is not about the colour you see in the mirror, but about what your skin does with sun. Do you burn quickly, do you tan, or a bit of both: that is where the scale lies.

The scale was devised in 1975 by the American dermatologist Thomas Fitzpatrick, and it came about because a treatment with light turns out differently on one skin than on another. So the question was not how someone looks, but how much light their skin absorbs and what happens afterwards.

Your type follows from two things: how quickly you burn in the first sun of the year, and how easily you tan afterwards. Someone who is red after half an hour and never tans sits at the start of the scale; someone who rarely burns and tans deeply at the end. Most people in the Netherlands sit somewhere in between.

It is a rough scale and it is meant as one. Two people of the same type can react differently, and your own skin reacts differently in March than in August. So for us it is a starting point and not a final verdict: what your skin really does shows in a test patch and in how the first treatment goes.

What the type does not say: how dry or sensitive your skin is, whether you break out easily and how thick your skin is. Those are other properties, and we measure them separately at the skin analysis.

You can record which type you have yourself in your skin profile, so that it is known before you come in. Which of the two wavelengths belongs with your type you can check at the laser chooser. What else comes up during a measurement is on the skin analysis.

**Why your type steers the laser**

Laser and IPL aim at pigment. If there is a lot of pigment in your upper skin, it catches part of the light, and that is exactly what the setting has to allow for.

A hair removal laser looks for the pigment in the hair root. The light has to get there without being absorbed too much on the way by the skin above it. On light skin that difference is large and almost all the energy goes to the root; on dark skin the difference is smaller and the wavelength has to be chosen differently.

That is why there are two wavelengths in one device. The alexandrite at 755 nanometres is strongly absorbed by pigment and works efficiently on types I to III. The Nd:YAG at 1064 nanometres is absorbed far less, largely passes the top layer and is therefore the choice for types V and VI.

Type IV sits on the border, and that is not a weak compromise but the honest state of affairs. If your skin responds calmly to the test patch, the alexandrite is possible at a lower energy; if there is doubt, it goes to the Nd:YAG. That choice is made in the treatment room and not beforehand on a website.

With IPL it is different, because that is not a laser but a bundle of wavelengths at once. There is less room there to work around your own pigment, so on dark skin we more often choose something else.

> knop: ABOUT LASER HAIR REMOVAL

**What helps and what we advise against**

Your type is one of the facts a treatment is set with. It is one of several, and it decides less than people think.

**THIS WORKS**

- Which wavelength is the safe and the efficient choice for hair removal

- How carefully the strength of a peel is built up

- How likely it is that pigment is left behind after a treatment

- Whether a test patch belongs beforehand, and how long we leave it

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Whether a treatment is possible. Every type is treated here, with a different setting

- How sensitive, dry or oily your skin is. That is something else and we measure it separately

- How many sessions you need. That depends mostly on the area and on your hair

- What your skin can take today. Tanned type II skin counts differently at that moment

**The six types side by side**

What each type does with sun, which wavelength belongs with it for hair removal and what else we watch. The middle column comes from the same table used in the treatment room.

*SKIN TYPE*

*FOR HAIR REMOVAL*

*WHAT WE WATCH*

**Frequently asked questions**

How do I work out my own Fitzpatrick type?

By answering two questions about the first sun of the year: do you burn, and do you tan afterwards? If you always burn and never tan, you are at type I or II. If you rarely burn and tan easily, at type IV or higher. If you are unsure, that is no problem: at the intake we establish it together.

Is laser hair removal possible on every skin type?

Yes, the GentleMax Pro works on types I to VI. Your type decides not whether it is possible, but with which wavelength, which energy and which cooling it is done. With the darker types that is with the Nd:YAG and with a test patch beforehand.

Why do you ask about my skin type before I come?

Because it decides what is possible on the day itself. If your type is already in your skin profile, that conversation does not have to start at the desk and the intake is shorter. It remains a starting point: what your skin really does shows in the test patch.

Does my skin type change in summer?

Your type itself does not, your skin at that moment does. Tanned skin holds fresh colour that absorbs light, and then the setting changes or we wait a while. How many weeks that takes you hear at the intake, because it differs per skin.

What does my type mean for a peel?

With types IV to VI the chance of pigment being left behind after a peel is higher. So we choose the strength more carefully, build up more slowly and discuss beforehand what your skin did previously after an inflammation or a small wound.

Is IPL suitable for darker skin?

Often not. IPL sends a bundle of wavelengths at once, and skin with a lot of its own pigment absorbs too much of it. So on dark skin we usually choose a different treatment, and what that is depends on what you come for.

What is the difference between skin type and skin condition?

Your type is fixed and is about your response to sun. Your condition changes and is about how your skin is doing today: dry, oily, sensitive, inflamed. For the choice of a treatment the condition often counts for more than the type.

Why a test patch if my type is already known?

Because the scale is a classification and not a measurement of your skin. Two people of the same type can react differently to the same energy. A test patch shows what your skin does, and that counts for more than the number.

Does establishing my skin type cost anything separately?

No. It belongs with the intake, along with the measurement of your skin. A separate intake costs € 50 and lasts at most thirty minutes. If treatment goes ahead in the same appointment, that amount is waived and you pay only for the treatment.

Where in Rotterdam are you?

At Weissenbruchlaan 166 in Rotterdam, on the north side of the city in a residential area. You park in the street. The route and the opening hours are on our contact page.

**Not sure of your type**

You do not have to be, before you come. We establish it at the intake, along with the measurement, and from that follows what is possible in your case and with which setting. If treating turns out not to be sensible at that moment, you hear so and we do not do it.

If you know what you are after but are unsure about the timing or the combination with something else, ask via WhatsApp. There is a therapist on the other end and not a form.

### /en/knowledge/fotona-4d-rotterdam

**Tabbladtitel:** Fotona 4D Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Fotona 4D in Rotterdam: four laser steps in one session of 90 minutes, without needles. € 370 per treatment, € 995 for a course of three.

**FOTONA 4D IN ROTTERDAM**

Fotona 4D is a laser treatment in four steps in one session: first from the inside through the cheek, then at depth in the skin, and finally a light laser peel. Together they work on laxity, texture and colour, without needles. At Diba Clinics in Rotterdam a treatment takes 90 minutes and costs € 370.

> knop: BOOK AN APPOINTMENT

> knop: SEE THE PRICES

*DURATION*

*RATE*
