*DEVICE*

Fotona TimeWalker

**What Fotona 4D does to your skin**

Four treatments following one another in the same session, each at a different depth. Together they reach what one step alone does not.

Over the years your skin makes less collagen, the connective tissue that keeps it firm. You see that as slackening along the jawline, fine lines and less even skin. Those changes sit at different depths, and that is why Fotona 4D works at different depths too.

It starts from the inside with SmoothLiftin: a handpiece against the inside of your cheek, heating the tissue you cannot reach from outside. Then FRAC3 works at depth on irregularities, and PIANO heats the tissue flatly and evenly. SupErficial finishes with a light laser peel of the top layer.

Straight after the session the skin looks fuller from the heat, but that is not a result yet. Making collagen takes weeks, and the difference builds across the series: as a one-off or as a course of three, with four to six weeks in between.

The treatment itself is on the treatment page, and which other treatments run on this device on the Fotona TimeWalker. What a course asks in time is on the number of sessions.

**Two lasers in one device**

The Fotona TimeWalker is not a treatment but a platform. That it has two lasers is why 4D can do what one laser cannot.

Inside the cabinet are two lasers. An Er:YAG at 2940 nanometres, almost entirely absorbed by water and so staying at the surface. And an Nd:YAG at 1064 nanometres, held back much less by water and so reaching deeper. Together they cover a range one laser does not.

The warming steps use the SMOOTH mode: the energy comes in a series of slow pulses rather than one hard one. The tissue is warmed without the top layer being removed. What you feel is a rising warmth that stops just short of uncomfortable, and during the session the therapist asks how warm it feels.

There is also a full package, Fotona 4D Full Package, which includes the neck and the jawline. That is often where slackness shows first, while the face still looks taut. And there is Fotona 4D Men, with settings for the generally thicker skin of men.

**Frequently asked questions**

What does Fotona 4D cost in Rotterdam?

At Diba Clinics Fotona 4D costs € 370 per treatment and € 995 for a course of three. The full package with neck and jawline costs € 575, or € 1,495 as a course of three. If it is your first visit, your appointment starts with a € 50 intake.

Why is it called 4D?

Because four treatments follow one another in one session, each at a different depth: from the mucous membrane inside your cheek to the top layer of skin.

Does Fotona 4D hurt?

It is warm. The first step happens in your mouth and feels warm against your cheek; then the warmth on the outside rises to just short of uncomfortable. During the session the therapist asks how it feels and adjusts the device accordingly. The last step feels like short taps.

Is there recovery time after Fotona 4D?

Little. You are red and warm for a few hours to a day, as though you had sat too long in the sun. With the full package the closing peel can leave the skin feeling rough for a few days.

When do I see results from Fotona 4D?

Straight after the session the skin looks fuller from the heat, but that is not a result yet. Building collagen takes weeks; the difference builds across the series.

How many Fotona 4D treatments do I need?

As a one-off or as a course of three, with four to six weeks in between. With the full package, maintenance usually follows once a year after the course. What suits you, you hear at the intake.

Is Fotona 4D an alternative to a facelift?

No. Fotona 4D works on early laxity, texture and colour, without needles and without cutting. For skin that has really started to hang, surgery is the answer, and we tell you so.

Can I also have one of the four steps separately?

Yes. SmoothLiftin, FRAC3, PIANO and SupErficial can each be booked separately. Which one suits you, you hear at the intake.

### /en/knowledge/how-many-sessions

**Tabbladtitel:** How many sessions do you need | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** How many sessions a skin treatment asks for, why there are weeks in between and why the number can only be given after a measurement. Set out per treatment.

**HOW MANY SESSIONS DO YOU NEED**

How many sessions you need depends on the treatment and on your skin. A facial treatment can be a one-off, microneedling and peels usually go in a series of three to six with four to six weeks in between, and laser hair removal takes six to ten, spread over months, because hair grows in cycles. At Diba Clinics in Rotterdam you hear after the measurement which number is realistic in your case.

> knop: BOOK AN APPOINTMENT

> knop: SEE THE PRICES

*PEEL*

Four to six times

*MICRONEEDLING*

Three to six times

*LASER HAIR REMOVAL*

Six to ten times

*IN BETWEEN*

Four to six weeks

**Why it is often a series**

Your skin works in cycles and so does your hair. A treatment that follows those asks for repetition; a treatment that stays at the surface often does not.

The top layer of your skin renews itself in about four weeks. A treatment working there, such as a facial or a superficial peel, does its work within that one cycle. The result is immediate and in the weeks after it falls back to the starting point, which is why those treatments are called maintenance.

If a treatment goes deeper, you are not working with the cycle but setting repair in motion. New collagen builds over weeks, and every session adds a layer to it. So with microneedling and with most laser treatments there are four to six weeks in between: earlier and the previous session is not finished, later and you are partly starting again.

With hair removal it is different again. A laser only hits the hair that is in its growth phase at that moment, and that is only part of what is there. The rest has its turn in the weeks after, which is why six to ten sessions are needed, spread over months. The number depends on the area and on your skin type.

A pigment programme like Cosmelan or Dermamelan counts not sessions but months: one mask in the clinic, and then a fixed routine at home with check-ups along the way. What you do there counts for more than what happens in the treatment room.

The number per treatment is also on the treatment page itself, at all treatments. How a first appointment goes is on the skin consultation.

**Why you are given a range beforehand**

Naming an exact number before your skin has been measured sounds helpful and is not. What you do get is a range with the reason behind it.

What a treatment does depends on how your skin reacts to it, and beforehand that is an estimate. In one person the texture is where it should be after three sessions, in another the same goal takes six. So a number fixed beforehand is a promise about someone else's skin.

So we measure at the start and record that measurement. At every check-up the new image goes beside the previous one, under the same light and from the same angle. That way a conversation is possible halfway about what has changed, rather than a feeling afterwards.

If an approach gives too little, adjusting or stopping is the outcome of that conversation. Finishing a series because it happens to be booked is the wrong order. What you paid in advance for a course then stays credited towards another treatment.

Stopping halfway gives the result of half a series, and that is something other than half the result. With hair removal that is clearest: the hair that was in its growth phase during the missed sessions simply was not hit.

> knop: ABOUT THE SKIN ANALYSIS

**What helps and what we advise against**

A series is there to build something. For anything outside that, repeating is the wrong answer.

**THIS WORKS**

- Repair that builds over weeks, as with microneedling and laser

- Hair growing in cycles, so that only part of it can be hit each time

- Maintenance of a result that falls back on its own

- A programme in which the home routine does most of the work

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- A result that is already settled after one time. Then a second session is one too many

- A concern that does not respond. If the measurement stays the same, the approach changes

- Skin that is inflamed or irritated at that moment. We calm that first

- A number fixed beforehand without your skin having been measured

**Frequently asked questions**

How many laser hair removal sessions do you need?

Usually six to ten, spread over months. That is because a laser only hits the hair in its growth phase at that moment; the rest has its turn in the weeks after. The number depends on the area, on your skin type and on your hair, and you hear at the intake what is realistic in your case.

How many microneedling sessions are needed?

Usually a series of three to six, with four to six weeks in between. That time is not there for the calendar but for your skin: new collagen builds over weeks, and every session adds a layer. With scars and with deeper texture it is more often six than three.

Why are there four to six weeks between two sessions?

Because your skin needs that time to finish what the previous session set in motion. Treating earlier means working on skin that is still busy; much later means part of the gain has already fallen back.

Can I see anything after one session?

With a facial treatment usually straight away, because it works at the surface. With microneedling, laser and peels you often see something in the texture after the first session, but the goal you came for takes the whole series.

What happens if I stop halfway?

Then you keep the result of half a series, and that is something other than half the result. With hair removal that is clearest: the hair that was in its growth phase during the missed sessions was not hit and simply keeps growing.

Why do you not name a fixed number beforehand?

Because it depends on how your skin reacts, and beforehand that is an estimate. You get a range with the reason behind it, a measurement at the start and a check-up along the way where we put side by side what has changed. From that follows the number you really need.

Is a course cheaper than separate sessions?

With a number of treatments, yes. Skin boosters and Fotona 4D have a course rate lower than three separate sessions together. The amounts are with the treatment itself and on the price page, and you only choose after the intake.

How often should I come back for maintenance?

With a facial treatment usually every four to six weeks, because the effect falls back on its own. With a programme that builds repair, maintenance is a check-up every six months to a year, depending on what we measure.

Do I have to book all the sessions in advance?

You do not have to, but it helps. The time between two sessions is part of the treatment, and a series that runs over because there was no space gives less. You can schedule the appointments in one go and still move them later.

Where in Rotterdam are you?

At Weissenbruchlaan 166 in Rotterdam, on the north side of the city in a residential area. You park in the street. The route and the opening hours are on our contact page.

**Not sure whether a series is needed**

That is exactly what the first appointment shows. We measure your skin, discuss what you want to change and say what that takes, even when it is less than you thought. If there turns out to be nothing that needs treating, you hear that too.

### /en/knowledge/hydrafacial-rotterdam

**Tabbladtitel:** HydraFacial Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** HydraFacial in Rotterdam at Diba Clinics. Sixty minutes, € 170 to € 220, no recovery time. What it does, who it suits and how an appointment goes.

**HYDRAFACIAL IN ROTTERDAM**

A HydraFacial is a facial treatment in which a single handpiece cleanses, loosens the top layer of skin, empties pores and delivers active ingredients, all at once. At Diba Clinics on the Weissenbruchlaan in Rotterdam the treatment takes 60 minutes, costs 170 to 220 euros and has no recovery time.

> knop: BOOK AN APPOINTMENT

> knop: SEE THE PRICES

*DURATION*

*RATE*

€ 170 to € 220

*RECOVERY TIME*

None

*DEVICE*

HydraFacial Syndeo

**What a HydraFacial does to your skin**

It starts not with the device but with what is going on in your skin, because that decides whether this treatment does anything about it.

Your skin constantly makes new cells and lets the old ones go at the surface. That letting go does not happen equally smoothly in everyone. If those cells stay too long, they gather in your pores along with sebum and traces of make-up. That is what you see when your skin looks dull and your pores look larger than they are: there is something in them, and the light no longer reflects off a smooth layer but off an uneven one.

A HydraFacial takes that away, and does it in one movement. Inside the handpiece is a spiral channel under suction with fluid running through it. Together the two make a swirling motion across your skin. The fluid loosens the bond between the outermost cells, the suction pulls them out along with whatever was in the pore, and through the same channel, in the same pass, a serum goes in.

The treatment stays at the surface, in the horny layer and the upper epidermis. That is exactly why you see the result straight away and notice nothing else: nothing is damaged that has to heal afterwards. It is also why the effect is temporary. Your horny layer renews itself, so what you remove now builds up again in the weeks that follow.

How the tip is built and why the tips differ is on the page about the HydraFacial Syndeo. The treatment itself, apart from the place, is on the treatment page. Whether a facial is possible during pregnancy is on pregnancy or breastfeeding.

**HydraFacial and hydradermabrasion**

The names are used interchangeably, but it is not the same device. That is worth knowing as soon as you put prices side by side, and not only ours.

HydraFacial is a brand name and not a kind of treatment. There are other devices that work with suction and fluid; those are called hydradermabrasion. They work on the same principle and the result goes the same way, but the handpiece, the fluids and the tips differ per manufacturer.

We work with the HydraFacial Syndeo, the brand's current model. The tips are single-use and go per treatment; which one is used depends on your skin and on the goal. That is not a detail for the brochure: how coarse the spiral is decides how much gets loosened.

If you put prices from different clinics side by side, ask which device they have and which tips go with it. That is an ordinary question and you should simply get an answer. The answer decides whether you are comparing the same thing twice.

> knop: ABOUT THIS DEVICE

**What a HydraFacial costs with us**

Three versions, all 60 minutes. The intake arrangement is set out in full, because that is the amount people do not see coming at a first appointment.

- Signature € 170

- Deluxe € 190

- Platinum € 220

Which of the three suits you is discussed by the therapist at the intake, based on what your skin needs and what you want from the treatment.

**Is this your first visit**

Then you book a treatment on advice. We reserve at most two hours for that: the intake, and then at least an hour to treat. If treating is safe at that moment and you want it, we do the HydraFacial in the same appointment.

**What the intake costs**

If you are treated in the same appointment, the intake fee is waived and you pay only for the treatment. If the treatment does not go ahead, the intake costs € 50. A separate intake without treatment lasts at most 30 minutes and always costs € 50.

**Have you been here before**

Then you book the HydraFacial directly in the calendar. Count on 60 minutes. If anything has changed since your last visit in your skin, your medication or your expectation, say so when you arrive. That sometimes changes the choice of tip or serum.

**What helps and what we advise against**

A HydraFacial works on what lies in and on your skin. For anything deeper there is a different treatment, and then we say so.

**THIS WORKS**

- Dull skin and pores with something visibly in them, especially around your nose and chin

- Skin that has to look better within a day, for an occasion for instance

- Maintenance alongside a running programme for acne, pigmentation or skin improvement

- A first introduction when you do not yet know what your skin needs

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Scars and pigment that sit deeper in the skin. Microneedling or laser works on those, because they reach the layer where the problem is.

- Lasting change in the texture of your skin. A HydraFacial is maintenance; the effect lasts days to weeks and does not build up.

- Active, inflamed acne. Then it starts with the acne programme and not with a single treatment.

- Skin that has just been peeled, lasered or needled. We leave time in between; how much depends on what was done.

**Frequently asked questions**

What does a HydraFacial cost in Rotterdam?

At Diba Clinics a HydraFacial costs € 170 for the Signature, € 190 for the Deluxe and € 220 for the Platinum. A treatment takes 60 minutes. If it is your first visit you book a treatment on advice: that starts with an intake, and the € 50 intake fee is waived as soon as we treat in the same appointment.

How long does a HydraFacial take?

60 minutes. For a first appointment we reserve at most two hours, because the intake comes with it and nothing should be rushed. That time is a maximum and not an obligation; often you are done sooner.

Is there recovery time after a HydraFacial?

No. Afterwards your skin is pink and feels tight, and that usually fades within an hour. Make-up is fine the same day. You can walk straight out after the appointment.

How often can you have a HydraFacial?

As a one-off, or monthly as maintenance. A starting series is usually three to six treatments. What makes sense in your case depends on your skin and on what you want from it; we discuss that at the intake.

Can I have a HydraFacial just before a wedding or party?

Yes, that is one of the reasons people choose this treatment: the effect is immediate and there is no day on which you have to stay in. If you have never had one, book it at least a week beforehand, so that you know how your skin reacts before it matters.

What is the difference from an ordinary facial?

In a classic facial, cleansing, extracting and caring happen one after another and by hand. With a HydraFacial it happens in one pass with one handpiece, with suction doing the work instead of fingers. That is more even across your face and your skin gets less irritated by it.

Does a HydraFacial help against acne?

With blocked pores and blackheads it can help, because that is exactly what is removed. With active, inflamed acne it is not the first step: then you start with the acne programme, where we first calm the skin. What suits you is decided by the therapist after the measurement.

Is a HydraFacial possible with sensitive skin?

Often yes. No acids are involved and the treatment stays at the surface, so your skin takes little from it. With active rosacea or inflamed skin we calm that first. Whether it is possible for you is decided by the measurement at the intake.

Is a HydraFacial covered by health insurance?

No. A HydraFacial is a maintenance treatment without medical necessity and so falls outside the system. If your concern does have a medical reason, with acne or a scar for instance, there is sometimes a route to reimbursement; that is explained on our page about insurance cover.

Where in Rotterdam are you?

At Weissenbruchlaan 166 in Rotterdam, on the north side of the city in a residential area. You park in the street. The route and the opening hours are on our contact page.

**Not sure whether this is the right treatment is**

You do not have to know that before you come. Book a treatment on advice: we measure your skin, discuss what is going on and say which treatment fits. If a HydraFacial turns out not to be the best answer to your question, you hear that and we do something else that day, or nothing.

### /en/knowledge/ipl-rotterdam

**Tabbladtitel:** IPL Rotterdam: pigment and redness | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** IPL in Rotterdam with Candela's Nordlys, for pigment spots, sun damage, thread veins and rosacea. From € 75, usually red for a few hours.

**IPL TREATMENT IN ROTTERDAM**

IPL is a treatment with intense pulsed light that seeks out pigment and small vessels in the skin, so that spots fade and redness clears. At Diba Clinics in Rotterdam we work with the Nordlys by Candela. A treatment takes 30 minutes and costs € 75 for the nose up to € 250 for the whole face, and you are usually red for a few hours.

> knop: BOOK AN APPOINTMENT

> knop: SEE THE PRICES

*DURATION*

*RATE*

€ 75 to € 250

*RECOVERY TIME*

A few hours red

*DEVICE*

Nordlys, Candela

**What IPL does to your skin**

The light seeks out colour. In a pigment spot that is melanin, in a vessel it is blood, and that is where the energy goes.

IPL sends not a single wavelength into the skin but a band, with a filter that takes out the coarsest part. So that band hits several things at once: surface pigment, visible vessels and skin that is structurally red. On average the light goes less deep than a laser, and that is exactly what surface concerns need.

With pigment the spot takes up the energy, turns grainy and works its way to the surface. In the days that follow the spot first gets darker and then fades. That darkening is part of it and does not mean it is getting worse.

With redness the light aims at the blood in the vessels. That heats up, the vessel closes and is cleared away by your body. With rosacea it is less about a single vessel and more about an area that is structurally red; then the light works across the whole surface.

It is worked out separately per concern: IPL for sun spots, for thread veins and for rosacea. If you would rather start from the concern, look at pigment spots. What part your skin type plays in this is on the Fitzpatrick skin type.

**IPL is not a laser**

The two are often confused. The difference decides which device you choose for what.

A laser emits one wavelength and is therefore very precise. IPL emits a band, so it hits several targets at once and covers a larger area. For one specific spot a laser is more precise; for sun damage spread across your cheeks IPL is faster and more even.

We work with the Nordlys by Candela. Candela calls its variant Selective Waveband Technology: two filters cut the top and bottom off the spectrum, leaving a narrower band than ordinary IPL, with pulses shorter than a millisecond.

Which band comes out depends on the handpiece the therapist chooses. For pigment that is a different one from vessels, because each band is chosen around what it has to hit.

> knop: ABOUT THE NORDLYS

The rate depends on the area and is the same for pigment and redness. The intake arrangement is set out in full.

**What helps and what we advise against**

IPL works on what sits near the surface and has colour. For melasma, for what sits deep and in summer we choose something else or wait.

**THIS WORKS**

- Little recovery time: usually you are presentable again the same day

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Melasma. That pigment often reacts to heat, and IPL is not the first choice there

- Pigment in the summer months. Between May and August we do not treat pigment

- Curing rosacea. IPL takes the visible redness away, and it can come back

- Every skin type. On darker skin the chance of new pigment spots is higher, and then we choose a different treatment

**Frequently asked questions**

What does an IPL treatment cost in Rotterdam?

At Diba Clinics IPL costs € 75 for the nose, € 150 for the cheeks and € 250 for the whole face; cheeks, nose and chin together cost € 200. That applies to pigment and to redness. If it is your first visit, your appointment starts with a € 50 intake, which is waived if we treat in the same appointment.

Is IPL the same as laser?

No. A laser emits one wavelength, IPL a band. So that band hits several things at once, such as redness, vessels and surface pigment, and on average goes less deep.

Why does my pigment spot get darker first?

That is part of it. The pigment comes to the surface before it fades, and that takes a number of days. It does not mean it is getting worse.

Does IPL hurt?

With every flash of light you feel a short, warm snap, often compared to an elastic band against your skin. It is brief and manageable.

How many IPL treatments do I need?

Usually three to six, with four weeks in between. With rosacea, maintenance follows, because the redness can come back.

Can I have IPL in summer?

Not for pigment. Between May and August we do not treat pigment, because freshly treated skin reacts especially sharply to sun. For redness and vessels it is different; we discuss that case by case.

Does IPL help against couperose and rosacea?

It removes separate vessels and calms an area that is structurally red. It does not cure rosacea: the visible redness goes, and it can come back. That is why maintenance belongs with rosacea.

Is IPL possible on darker skin?

Not with every skin type. On darker skin the skin itself takes up more light, and the chance of new pigment spots is higher. We establish your skin type beforehand and choose the treatment that suits your skin.

Where in Rotterdam are you?

At Weissenbruchlaan 166 in Rotterdam, on the north side of the city in a residential area. You park in the street. The route and the opening hours are on our contact page.

### /en/knowledge/microneedling-rotterdam

**Tabbladtitel:** Microneedling Rotterdam: SkinPen and Dermapen | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Microneedling in Rotterdam with the SkinPen and the Dermapen 4. From € 180 per session, one to three days red. For scars, pores and skin texture.

**MICRONEEDLING IN ROTTERDAM**

Microneedling is a treatment in which fine needles make a great many small channels in the skin, so that your skin starts making new collagen itself. At Diba Clinics in Rotterdam we work with the SkinPen and the Dermapen 4. A treatment of the face costs € 180 and takes 60 minutes, and afterwards you are red for one to three days.

> knop: BOOK AN APPOINTMENT

> knop: SEE THE PRICES

*DURATION*

*RATE*

From € 180

*RECOVERY TIME*

1 to 3 days red

*SERIES*

3 to 6 sessions

**What microneedling does to your skin**

The result comes not from the pricks themselves but from what your skin does afterwards, and that is why you only see it after weeks.

Beneath the epidermis lies the dermis, and that is where the connective tissue sits that keeps your skin firm and smooth. With a scar, a coarse pore or skin that has lost springiness over the years, that connective tissue has become uneven or thinner. A cream does not reach there; that layer lies too deep.

With fine needles, microneedling makes a great many small channels down into the upper dermis. Your skin treats them as small wounds and starts to repair, and in that repair it makes new collagen. That repair is the goal; the pricks are only the occasion for it.

So you do not see the result after one treatment but across a series. What you see in the first days is redness and a little swelling. The real difference builds over weeks and shows best once the series of three to six treatments is finished, with four to six weeks in between.

What microneedling does for a particular concern is worked out separately: for acne scars, for coarse pores, for fine lines, for scars after surgery and for stretch marks. Why there are weeks between the sessions is on the number of sessions.

**SkinPen and Dermapen 4**

We work with two microneedling pens. Which one you get depends on the area and the depth that suits it, and not on which is better.

The SkinPen has fourteen needles and works a little more calmly. The Dermapen 4 reaches up to 1920 pricks per second and so covers an area faster, with preset modes, including a setting for scars at the maximum depth. On both the depth is adjustable from 0.25 to 3 millimetres.

That depth is the setting that really matters. Shallow only reaches the epidermis and heals within a day; three millimetres goes into the connective tissue and takes longer. Around your eyes and on your forehead, where the skin lies thin over bone, the pen goes less deep than on your cheeks.

The needle cartridges are sterile and are discarded after each treatment. With microneedling that is not a detail, because the needles go through your skin's protective layer. Beforehand a numbing cream goes on that takes half an hour to work; what you feel after that is mostly vibration and pressure.

> knop: ABOUT THE TREATMENT

The rate is the same for the SkinPen and the Dermapen and depends on the area. The intake arrangement is set out in full.

**Frequently asked questions**

What does microneedling cost in Rotterdam?

At Diba Clinics microneedling costs € 180 for the face and € 255 for the back. With the neck included it is € 210, and with neck and décolleté € 240. Does microneedling hurt?

It is manageable. Beforehand a numbing cream goes on that takes half an hour to work. What you feel after that is mostly vibration and pressure, strongest where the skin lies thin over bone, such as on your forehead.

How long am I red after microneedling?

One to three days, roughly like a strong sun flush. For the first twenty-four hours you leave your skin alone: no make-up and no exercise that makes you sweat heavily.

How many treatments do I need?

Usually three to six, with four to six weeks in between. How many that becomes for you depends on your concern and on how your skin reacts. We measure that along the way, and we do not promise a fixed number beforehand.

When do I see results from microneedling?

Not after the first time; what you see then is swelling. The collagen your skin makes builds over weeks, so you see the difference across the series and most clearly a few months after the last treatment.

What is the difference between the SkinPen and the Dermapen?

The motor design and the number of needles. The SkinPen has fourteen and works a little more calmly; the Dermapen reaches more pricks per second and covers an area faster. On both the depth can be set up to 3 millimetres, and the rate is the same.

Does microneedling help against acne scars?

With scars formed by loss of structure, such as the shallow dents after acne, it can help a good deal. Deep or tethered scars often need a combination with laser. While the acne is still active we do not start: the skin has to be calm first.

Is microneedling possible on darker skin?

Often yes, and it is then one of the better options, because no heat is involved. With skin types IV to VI we pay extra attention to pigment forming after the treatment and adjust the depth accordingly. We discuss that beforehand.

### /en/knowledge/oxygeneo-rotterdam

**Tabbladtitel:** OxyGeneo Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** OxyGeneo in Rotterdam at Diba Clinics. € 150, sixty minutes and no recovery time. Exfoliating and feeding in one treatment.

**OXYGENEO IN ROTTERDAM**

OxyGeneo is a facial treatment in which a capsule reacts with a gel on the skin: the top layer is loosened, active ingredients go in, and the skin is prompted to send more oxygen-rich blood to the surface. At Diba Clinics in Rotterdam the treatment takes 60 minutes, costs € 150 and has no recovery time.

> knop: BOOK AN APPOINTMENT

> knop: SEE THE PRICES

*DURATION*

*RATE*

*RECOVERY TIME*

None

*DEVICE*

OxyGeneo, Pollogen

**What OxyGeneo does to your skin**

Three things in one movement: loosening, delivering, and giving the blood flow a push. It stays at the surface, which is why you see it straight away.

Skin that looks dull often has a layer of dead cells that stays too long, and a surface that reflects little light. Creams pass through that layer poorly. What helps is loosening the layer and giving something back at the same time, and that is exactly what this treatment does in one pass.

The handpiece moves a capsule across your skin while a gel lies on it. The two react and small CO2 bubbles form. Your skin responds by sending more oxygen-rich blood to the spot. Meanwhile the capsule loosens the outer layer and the ingredients from the gel go in.

It stays at the surface, which is why you see something straight away and notice nothing else. It is also why the effect lasts days rather than weeks. So many people book this treatment just before an occasion, or every four to six weeks as maintenance.

How the device works is on the OxyGeneo by Pollogen. The treatment itself is on the treatment page.

**One of the calmest treatments**

No needles, no acids and no heat are involved. What you feel is mostly a light fizzing.

First make-up and sebum come off, otherwise the rest works on a film rather than on your skin. Then the gel goes on and the therapist moves the handpiece in strips across your face. The gel and the capsule react and it fizzes lightly; you hear it more than you feel it.

Afterwards your skin is pink and feels soft. That usually fades within an hour, and make-up is fine the same day. There is nothing to take into account except sun protection, and that applies anyway.

On skin that is inflamed or irritated at that moment we do not do it; then we calm your skin first. With sensitive skin it is usually possible, and the therapist judges that at the intake.

> knop: ABOUT THE OXYGENEO

**What OxyGeneo costs with us**

One rate, and no versions to choose between. The intake arrangement for a first appointment is set out in full, because that is where the amount people do not see coming sits.

- OxyGeneo glow € 150

If you want to keep the effect, you book it every four to six weeks as maintenance. How often that makes sense for you, we discuss at the intake.

**Is this your first visit**

Then you book a treatment on advice. We reserve at most two hours for that: the intake, and then at least an hour to treat. If treating is safe at that moment and you want it, we do the OxyGeneo in the same appointment.

**What the intake costs**

If you are treated in the same appointment, the intake fee is waived and you pay only for the treatment. If the treatment does not go ahead, the intake costs € 50. A separate intake without treatment lasts at most 30 minutes and always costs € 50.

**Have you been here before**

Then you book the OxyGeneo directly in the calendar. Count on 60 minutes. If anything has changed since your last visit in your skin, your medication or your expectation, say so when you arrive.

**What helps and what we advise against**

OxyGeneo works on the upper layers. For what sits deeper, and for a difference that lasts, there is a different treatment.

**THIS WORKS**

- Dull skin that may look fresher straight away

- Dry or dehydrated skin

- A treatment just before an occasion, with no day when you have to stay in

- Maintenance alongside a programme, with no recovery time

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Scars or pigment that sit deeper. Microneedling or laser is for those

- Skin that is inflamed or irritated at that moment. We calm that first

**Frequently asked questions**

What does OxyGeneo cost in Rotterdam?

At Diba Clinics an OxyGeneo treatment costs € 150 and takes 60 minutes. If it is your first visit, your appointment starts with a € 50 intake, which is waived if we treat in the same appointment.

What are those bubbles on my skin?

CO2 released when the capsule reacts with the gel. Your skin answers with better blood flow, and that is exactly the point.

Do I feel anything of OxyGeneo?

A light fizzing and some warmth. No stinging and no recovery time; you can walk straight out with it.

How long do I see something of it?

The effect lasts days, not weeks. So many people book this treatment just before an occasion, or every four to six weeks as maintenance.

What is the difference between OxyGeneo and a HydraFacial?

Both work on the top layer and without recovery time. A HydraFacial empties pores with suction and puts serum back; OxyGeneo loosens the layer with a capsule and a gel, prompting your skin to send more oxygen-rich blood to the surface. For blocked pores the HydraFacial is more targeted.

Is OxyGeneo possible with sensitive skin?

Usually yes. The therapist judges that at the intake; with active rosacea or inflamed acne we calm your skin first.

Can I have OxyGeneo just before a party?

Yes, that is exactly what it suits: the effect is immediate and there is no day when you have to stay in. Afterwards your skin is briefly pink, and that usually fades within an hour.

How often can you have OxyGeneo?

As a one-off, or as maintenance every four to six weeks. What makes sense for you, we discuss at the intake.

Where in Rotterdam are you?

At Weissenbruchlaan 166 in Rotterdam, on the north side of the city in a residential area. You park in the street. The route and the opening hours are on our contact page.

You do not have to know that before you come. We look at your skin and say which treatment fits. If your pores are full, a HydraFacial may be the better answer, and you hear so.

### /en/knowledge/pregnant-or-breastfeeding

**Tabbladtitel:** Pregnant or breastfeeding: what is possible | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Which skin treatments are possible during pregnancy and breastfeeding and which wait, and why pigment often changes on its own in that period.

**PREGNANT OR BREASTFEEDING**

During pregnancy and while you are breastfeeding we do not do some treatments: for peels, microneedling, skin boosters and the pigment programmes the research to say they are safe is missing. What is possible is measuring, advising and the gentle facial treatments, such as dermaplaning. Say so when you book, and we choose from those.

> knop: BOOK AN APPOINTMENT

> knop: SEE THE PRICES

*ALWAYS POSSIBLE*

Measuring and advice

*USUALLY YES*

Dermaplaning

*WAIT*

Peels and needling

*PIGMENTATION*

Often changes by itself

**Why part of it has to wait**

It is almost never about a proven danger. It is about the absence of research, and in this period that is a reason in itself.

For understandable reasons, pregnant women are not included in research into skin treatments. So for part of what we do there is no evidence at all that it is safe, and none that it is harmful. When both are missing, not doing it is the only choice that can be defended.

On top of that, your skin reacts differently in these months. Hormones make pigment cells more active, the blood flow is higher and the skin is often more sensitive. A peel or a laser that went calmly before can now give a reaction it otherwise would not have.

With breastfeeding something else plays a part: some of the substances that go on or into the skin during a treatment have not been studied for what ends up in breast milk. So in our policy that period runs along with the pregnancy.

For pigment there is a second reason to wait, and it is practical. Spots that appeared during a pregnancy often largely fade afterwards. Treating while the driver is still on costs money for a result you would partly have got for free.

There is one exception to the waiting, and that is the measurement. It puts nothing into your skin and gives something precisely now, because hormones change pigment, oil and sensitivity all at once. What you record in these months is later the starting point that shows you what really stayed and what faded on its own.

What pigment does in this period is on melasma. How stretch marks work after a pregnancy is on stretch marks.

**What is possible in those months**

More remains than people think. Most of it works at the surface, and that is exactly why it is possible.

The measurement is always possible. Your skin is mapped, you hear what is going on and what will fit later, and that image is the starting point to begin from straight after breastfeeding. For anyone who sees change in her skin during this period, that is often the most useful thing to do now.

Dermaplaning is possible, because only a sterile blade passes over the outer layer and no acids are involved. A gentle, cleansing facial treatment is usually possible too, with products the therapist selects for it. What exactly fits, she judges at the appointment.

Beyond that, this is the period in which sun protection gives the most. With pigment that has come up during pregnancy, protecting daily keeps the spots lighter and stops them spreading. That is not a delay but treatment, and it is the one part that already works now.

Your own routine changes in these months as well. You leave retinol and the stronger acids alone, and your skin also reacts more sensitively than you are used to. What does fit is usually a simpler schedule: gentle cleansing, a moisturiser and daily sun protection.

Put it in your skin profile before you come, too. Then it is in your file before the conversation starts, and the therapist does not have to change the plan halfway through.

> knop: ABOUT DERMAPLANING

**What helps and what we advise against**

The line lies at what goes into or through the skin. What stays at the surface is usually fine, in consultation.

**THIS WORKS**

- The skin analysis and the advice, in any month

- Dermaplaning and a gentle facial treatment, in consultation

- Sun protection and a home routine that keeps your skin calm

- Making a plan for the period after breastfeeding

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Peels with acids, the milder strengths included

- Microneedling, on the face and on the body

- Skin boosters and anything that goes into the skin with a needle

- The Cosmelan and Dermamelan pigment programmes

**What is possible and what waits until after**

Per treatment, what happens during pregnancy and during breastfeeding. Where there is doubt, it is written as doubt and not as a rule.

**Frequently asked questions**

Can I have a facial treatment while pregnant?

A gentle, cleansing treatment is usually possible, with products selected for it. Dermaplaning is possible too, because no acids are involved. What fits in your case, the therapist judges at the appointment.

Is microneedling allowed during pregnancy?

No. We do not treat with microneedling then, not on the body either and not at a shallower depth. After breastfeeding we assess again; with stretch marks that is often also the point at which they have already lightened on their own.

Is a chemical peel allowed while pregnant?

No. Pregnancy and breastfeeding are listed as contraindications by our peel ranges, and that holds for the milder strengths too. For skin that is rough or dull in this period we look at what is possible without acids.

Is laser hair removal possible during pregnancy?

We discuss that case by case, and usually we wait until afterwards. There is no research showing harm, but there is no research showing safety either, and on top of that hair growth changes with the hormones anyway. Say so when booking and we choose the moment together.

I have developed pigment spots during my pregnancy.

Protect, yes; treat, no. Spots that have come up from the hormones often largely fade after the pregnancy, and treating while the driver is still on gives little that lasts. Daily sun protection keeps them as light as possible in the meantime.

How long after the birth can I be treated again?

If you are not breastfeeding, measuring and treating can resume after the birth as soon as you feel up to it. If you are breastfeeding, we wait until that period is over. The measurement can go ahead in the meantime.

Do I have to say if I am pregnant or breastfeeding?

Yes, and preferably when you book. Then we reserve the right treatment and the right amount of time straight away, rather than having to change the plan at the desk. You can also put it in your skin profile beforehand.

Is it worth coming by already?

Often yes. The measurement records how your skin is doing now, and that is the starting point to begin from straight after breastfeeding. A separate intake costs € 50 and lasts at most thirty minutes.

Can I keep using retinol while pregnant?

No. You leave retinol and the related vitamin A acids alone in this period, and that holds for the stronger acids in your own routine too. What does fit is usually a simpler schedule: gentle cleansing, a moisturiser and daily sun protection. Bring your products to the appointment and we will go through them together.

Can I do anything about acne that comes up during pregnancy?

Within the limits above, yes. What falls away in this period are the acids, the medication and the treatments that go into the skin; what remains is gentle cleansing, an adjusted home routine and keeping an eye on how it develops. It often settles after the birth, and then we take up whatever is still there.

Why does breastfeeding run along with pregnancy?

Because for some of the substances used in a treatment it has not been studied what ends up in breast milk. That is the same reason as with pregnancy: the absence of research, and not a proven danger.

Where in Rotterdam are you?

At Weissenbruchlaan 166 in Rotterdam, on the north side of the city in a residential area. You park in the street. The route and the opening hours are on our contact page.

**Not sure what is possible now**

Call or message us before you book. We will look together at what fits in this period and what had better wait, and if need be we book only the measurement. That saves you an appointment that changes at the desk after all.

If you know what you are after but are unsure about the timing or the combination with something else, ask via WhatsApp. There is a therapist on the other end and not a form.

### /en/knowledge/skin-analysis-rotterdam

**Tabbladtitel:** Skin analysis Rotterdam with the EVE-M | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Skin analysis in Rotterdam with the EVE-M. An intake on its own takes at most 30 minutes and costs € 50. What is measured and which appointment to book.

**SKIN ANALYSIS IN ROTTERDAM**

A skin analysis is a measurement of your skin with a scanner that records under the same light every time and also looks under UV, so that you see what sits beneath the surface. At Diba Clinics in Rotterdam that is done with the EVE-M, as part of the intake. A separate intake with skin analysis lasts at most 30 minutes and costs € 50.

> knop: BOOK AN APPOINTMENT

> knop: SEE THE PRICES

*DURATION*

Max. 30 minutes

*RATE*

*DEVICE*

*CONTACT*

None

**What a skin analysis shows**

What you see in the mirror is the outside. A measurement shows what sits beneath it, and records it in a way you can compare later.

Two people with the same spots can have something entirely different. Pigment can sit in the epidermis or deeper, and that depth decides which treatment does anything about it. Redness can come from a vessel or from inflammation. In ordinary light you often cannot see that difference, and then you are treating on a guess.

The EVE-M records your skin and measures. Your face goes into a fixed rest, so that the distance and the angle are the same at every capture, and the lighting comes from the device itself. Besides ordinary light it also records under UV, and then pigment that sits deeper does show. Nothing touches your skin.

What comes out is not a diagnosis; a doctor makes that. It is a record of what is there now: pigment, redness, pores, moisture and signs of ageing. On that the therapist builds the plan, and at every check-up the same measurement is repeated. Then you see on the images whether it is working, rather than having to believe it.

How the device works is on the page about the EVE-M. What happens in the rest of the intake is on the skin consultation.

**Why not a phone photo**

Anyone can take a photo of their skin. The difference lies in what you can do with it after eight weeks.

A photo on your phone is different every time: a different distance, different light, a different angle. Put a new one beside it after eight weeks and you still do not know whether something has changed or whether the sun was in a different place.

The EVE-M takes those differences away. Because the conditions are the same at every capture, a difference in the image is also a difference in your skin. That lets you steer a programme on what has been measured, and stop when something is not working.

Measuring itself does nothing to your skin. You carry straight on with your day, and if you want to be treated in the same appointment we reserve time for that.

> knop: ABOUT THE EVE-M

**What a skin analysis costs with us**

A fixed amount, and an arrangement that decides whether you pay it separately. It is set out in full.

- Consultation, face € 50

- Consultation, laser hair removal € 50

The three consultations cost the same; they differ in what the therapist looks at.

Then you book a separate intake. We reserve at most 30 minutes for it, your skin is measured and you take a treatment plan away with you. No treatment happens in this appointment, and the intake always costs € 50.

**Measure and start straight away**

Then you book a treatment on advice, the appointment most people choose. We reserve at most two hours: the intake with the measurement, and then at least an hour to treat. If treatment goes ahead, the intake is waived and you pay only for the treatment.

**During a programme**

Then the same measurement is repeated at the check-ups. That way you see on the images what has changed, under the same light as the first time.

**What helps and what we advise against**

A skin analysis records what is there. It treats nothing and it makes no diagnosis.

**THIS WORKS**

- Recording what is there now, in a way that is still comparable months later

- Seeing what sits beneath the surface, such as pigment lying deeper

- A treatment plan resting on a measurement rather than on an estimate

- Checking the progress of a programme rather than estimating it

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Making a diagnosis. For a spot or a condition a doctor looks along

- Treating. During the measurement nothing happens to your skin

- Predicting what a treatment is going to give

- Assessing a mole that is changing. For that you go to your GP

**Frequently asked questions**

### /en/knowledge/skin-therapist-rotterdam

**Tabbladtitel:** Skin therapist Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Skin therapist in Rotterdam at Diba Clinics. What a skin therapist does, when skin therapy is covered and how your first appointment goes. Intake € 50.

**SKIN THERAPIST IN ROTTERDAM**

A skin therapist is an allied health professional with a four-year degree who treats skin concerns such as acne, scars, pigmentation, couperose and unwanted hair growth. At Diba Clinics on the Weissenbruchlaan in Rotterdam five skin therapists work, all listed in the Dutch Quality Register for Paramedics. An intake costs € 50 and is waived if you are treated in the same appointment.

> knop: BOOK AN APPOINTMENT

> knop: SEE THE PRICES

*TRAINING*

Degree, four years

*TITLE*

Protected by law

*REGISTER*

Allied health

*INTAKE*

**What a skin therapist does for you**

Skin therapy sits between the beauty treatment and the dermatologist. It helps to know exactly where, because that decides where to go for what.

A skin therapist treats the skin in a medical-cosmetic way: concerns you see and feel daily, but that do not take you to hospital. Think of acne and the scars it leaves, pigment spots, couperose and rosacea, unwanted hair growth, scars after surgery and skin ageing faster than you would like.

The work is done with devices and agents whose settings are chosen per skin: lasers and light, microneedling, medical peels. That is where the training makes the difference. How deep you go, how much energy a skin can take and when it is better not to treat are decisions you learn in four years of training and then keep current through the register.

A skin therapist does not make a diagnosis; that is a doctor's work. If the skin therapist sees something a doctor should assess, such as a mole that is changing, you hear so. We have no standing arrangement with doctors, so in that case we advise you to go to your GP yourself.

Which concerns we treat is set out per concern in the overview of skin concerns. Which treatments we use for them, with the rate and the recovery time, is on the treatments. If you still have to choose where to go, how to choose a skin clinic says what you can look out for yourself.

**A title you can verify**

Not every title in this field says something about the training behind it. This one does, and you can check it yourself.

Skin therapist is a legally protected training title, set down in article 34 of the Dutch Individual Healthcare Professions Act. You may only call yourself one with the bachelor's degree in skin therapy, and that programme exists in two places in the Netherlands: The Hague University of Applied Sciences and HU Utrecht.

The title says someone has completed the training. The Dutch Quality Register for Paramedics says something else: that someone actually practises the profession and keeps their knowledge current. Members of the Dutch Association of Skin Therapists have to be in that register, and our skin therapists are.

If you would rather check it yourself, you can: the register is public and you search it by name. That holds for every skin therapist, outside this clinic too, and it is the fastest way to know who you are dealing with.

> knop: OUR REGISTRATIONS

**What an appointment costs with us**

An intake, and then the treatment that suits your skin. Whether your insurance contributes depends on your concern and your policy.

- Intake with skin analysis € 50

- Medical peel from € 140

- Microneedling from € 180

- IPL for pigment or redness from € 75

- HydraFacial from € 170

Skin therapy is not in the basic policy, but with most insurers it is in the supplementary package. There has to be a medical reason then, and often a referral from your GP before the first treatment. How that works step by step is on the page about insurance cover.

**Is this your first visit**

Then you book a treatment on advice. We reserve at most two hours for that: the intake, and then at least an hour to treat. If treating is safe at that moment and you want it, we do the treatment in the same appointment.

**What the intake costs**

If you are treated in the same appointment, the intake fee is waived and you pay only for the treatment. If the treatment does not go ahead, the intake costs € 50. A separate intake without treatment lasts at most 30 minutes and always costs € 50.

**If you want it reimbursed**

Then arrange the referral from your GP before your first appointment, if your policy asks for one, and say when booking that you expect reimbursement. Then we check straight away whether everything is in order. Insurers rarely accept a referral sent in afterwards.

**What helps and what we advise against**

A skin therapist treats what is going on in and on the skin. For a diagnosis, for medication and for anything urgent, you belong with a doctor.

**THIS WORKS**

- Acne, and the scars and marks it leaves behind

- Pigment spots, couperose and rosacea

- Unwanted hair growth, with PCOS too

- Scars after surgery or a caesarean, and stretch marks

- Skin ageing or slackening faster than you would like

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Making a diagnosis. If you are unsure about a spot that is changing, you go to your GP

- Prescribing medication. Antibiotics, the pill or isotretinoin go through your GP or dermatologist

- An infection that gives fever or worsens quickly. Then you call your GP the same day

- Promising how many sessions you need. That depends on how your skin reacts, and we measure that along the way

- Treating when it is not sensible at that moment. Then you hear so, and we advise waiting or seeing a doctor

**Who does what in skin care**

Four titles you come across when you want something done about your skin. What the training is, whether the title is protected and what you go there for.

*PROTECTED*

*WHAT YOU GO THERE FOR*

Bachelor's degree in skin therapy

Yes, article 34 of the Individual Healthcare Professions Act

Acne, scars, pigment, vessels and hair growth, treated with devices and peels

*Dermatologist*

Doctor, then specialisation as a dermatologist

Yes, in the healthcare professionals register

A diagnosis, skin diseases, suspicious spots and medication. Usually via your GP

*Beauty therapist*

A vocational training, usually at secondary level

Care treatments: cleansing, nourishing and relaxing

*Orthomolecular skin specialist*

An additional training alongside skin therapy or beauty therapy

What plays a part from within: food, hormones and digestion

**Frequently asked questions**

What does a skin therapist cost in Rotterdam?

At Diba Clinics an intake with skin analysis costs € 50. If treatment goes ahead in the same appointment, that amount is waived and you pay only for the treatment. Treatments each have their own rate; a medical peel starts at € 140 and microneedling at € 180. All amounts are on our price page.

Is skin therapy reimbursed?

Sometimes. Skin therapy is not in the Dutch basic insurance, but with most insurers it is in the supplementary package. There has to be a medical reason then, and often a referral from your GP in place before the first treatment. A cosmetic treatment is not reimbursed.

Do I need a referral from my GP?

Not to come to us: you can make an appointment directly. For reimbursement sometimes yes, because many supplementary packages only reimburse with a referral. Arrange it before your first appointment then; insurers rarely accept one afterwards.

What is the difference between a skin therapist and a dermatologist?

A dermatologist is a doctor. They make diagnoses, treat skin diseases and prescribe medication, and you usually get there via your GP. A skin therapist is an allied health professional who treats skin concerns with devices, peels and guidance, and you can go there directly. If you are under a dermatologist's care you can often come here as well; do tell us.

What is the difference from a beauty therapist?

The training and the title. Skin therapist is a protected title with a four-year degree behind it; beauty therapist is not a protected title. In practice you see the difference mostly in treatments where the setting per skin counts, such as laser, microneedling and stronger peels.

How do I know whether a skin therapist is registered?

By checking the Dutch Quality Register for Paramedics. That register is public and you search it by name. Our skin therapists are in it, and their names are on the team page.

Which concerns does a skin therapist treat?

Acne and acne scars, pigment spots, couperose and rosacea, unwanted hair growth, scars after surgery, stretch marks and skin ageing. If you are unsure what you have, we start with a measurement, and if it is something for a doctor, you hear so.

How does a first appointment go?

You book a treatment on advice. We reserve at most two hours: the intake with a measurement of your skin, and then at least an hour to treat if that is safe and you want it. You are not committed to anything afterwards.

Where in Rotterdam are you?

At Weissenbruchlaan 166 in Rotterdam, on the north side of the city in a residential area. You park in the street. The route and the opening hours are on our contact page.

**Not sure whether your are in the right place here**

You do not have to know that before you come. We measure your skin, discuss what is going on and say whether it is something for us, for your GP or for both. If treating turns out not to be sensible, you hear so and we do not do it.

If you know what you are after but are unsure about the timing or the combination with something else, ask via WhatsApp. There is a therapist on the other end and not a form.

### /en/knowledge/skinboosters-rotterdam

**Tabbladtitel:** Skin boosters Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Skin boosters in Rotterdam with the U225 injector. From € 130, with small bumps that settle within a day. For moisture, fine lines and pigment.

**SKIN BOOSTERS IN ROTTERDAM**

A skin booster is a treatment in which active ingredients, such as hyaluronic acid and vitamins, are placed into the skin with very fine injections rather than onto it. At Diba Clinics in Rotterdam that is done with the U225, which puts every injection at the same depth. A single treatment costs € 180 and a course of three € 500.

> knop: BOOK AN APPOINTMENT

> knop: SEE THE PRICES

*DURATION*

60 minutes

*RATE*

From € 130

*RECOVERY TIME*

Small bumps, one day

*COURSE*

Three sessions

**What a skin booster does to your skin**

A cream largely stays at the surface. A skin booster puts the ingredients in the layer where they have to do their work.

Most of what you rub on your skin gets no further than the outer layer. That layer is there precisely to hold things back. For moisture and firmness, ingredients like hyaluronic acid have to sit deeper, in the skin itself, and a cream does not reach there.

With a skin booster a mixture of active ingredients goes just under the skin through very fine injections, spread across the whole area rather than in one place. The goal is not filling but the quality of the skin: that it feels more hydrated and firmer. Which mixture and how much depends on what your skin needs.

There are different boosters: one for fine lines and moisture, such as RRS Hyalift, a separate one for the thin skin around the eyes, and a depigmentation booster for face, neck and décolleté with pigment, sun damage and melasma. Because the skin does the work between sessions, it is usually a course of three.

How the injector works is on the U225. The treatment itself is on the treatment page, and the booster for the eyes on RRS Eyes.

**A skin booster is not a filler**

They are often confused, and the difference decides what you can expect from the treatment.

A filler brings volume to one place: filling a fold, making a lip fuller, changing a contour. A skin booster does not. It is spread thinly across the whole area and works on the quality of your skin, not on the shape of your face. We do not place fillers here.

What makes the difference here is the U225. When injecting by hand the whole syringe moves along; with the U225 the syringe stays still and only the needle moves, up to eight times per second. So there is less vibration and every injection is the same depth, even when a few hundred follow one another.

Beforehand a numbing cream goes on. What you feel after that is a series of short pricks, more sensitive around the eyes than on the cheek. Right afterwards you see small bumps where each injection went; those usually settle within a day.

> knop: ABOUT THE U225

A single treatment or a course of three, and a booster of its own for the eyes. The intake arrangement is set out in full.

- RRS Eyes € 130

A course of three costs € 500, against € 540 for three separate treatments. Because the skin does the work between sessions, the course is usually the sensible choice as well.

**What the intake costs**

If you are treated in the same appointment, the intake fee is waived and you pay only for the treatment. If the treatment does not go ahead, the intake costs € 50. A separate intake without treatment lasts at most 30 minutes and always costs € 50.

**Have you been here before**

Do not book a skin booster just before something where you have to be photographed: around the eyes a bruise can last longer.

**What helps and what we advise against**

A skin booster works on the quality of your skin. For volume, for deep lines and for anyone who cannot tolerate needles, it is not the right choice.

**THIS WORKS**

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

What is the difference between a skin booster and a filler?

### /en/knowledge/sun-and-your-skin

**Tabbladtitel:** Sun, holidays and your skin | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Why tanned skin is not lasered, how long you wait after the sun, what belongs after a treatment and how to plan a treatment around a holiday.

**SUN, HOLIDAYS AND YOUR SKIN**

Light and colour get in each other's way. If there is fresh colour from sun or a sunbed in your skin, it takes up the light from a laser or IPL and the energy goes to the wrong place; that is why tanned skin is not lasered. After a treatment your skin is more sensitive to sun instead, and then daily SPF 50 belongs with it.

> knop: BOOK AN APPOINTMENT

> knop: SEE THE PRICES

*BEFORE LASER*

Your own colour back

*AFTER A PEEL*

SPF 50 daily

*SUN HOLIDAY*

Book it afterwards

*PIGMENT PROGRAMME*

Not in summer

**What the sun does to your skin**

Tanning is not a colour you get but a reaction your skin makes. That is exactly why it gets in the way of a treatment with light.

Under UV the pigment cells in your epidermis make extra melanin. That pigment settles as a layer above the cell nuclei and catches part of the light coming in afterwards. Your skin does that to protect itself, so it is a sign that damage has occurred and not that nothing was wrong.

That extra pigment stays for weeks to months, even when you feel your colour has already gone. For a laser only what is in your skin at that moment counts, and not what you see in the mirror.

Sun also speeds up the ageing of your skin and drives pigment spots. With melasma, sun protection is not advice alongside the treatment but part of the treatment itself: without that protection the rest falls back within one season.

Freshly treated skin is temporarily missing part of its defences. After a peel, after microneedling and after laser the barrier is more open and the pigment reacts more sharply to UV. That is the period in which one day without protection can leave a spot that was not there before.

What sun protection does exactly for pigment is on melasma and on pigment spots. What part your skin type plays is on the Fitzpatrick skin type.

**When we wait a while**

There are two moments when sun moves an appointment: the colour already in there, and the sun that is coming. Each has a different solution.

If you come with fresh colour from sun or a sunbed, a treatment with light does not go ahead. The light aims at pigment, and the pigment you have just built up lies in front of it. The energy then lands in the top layer instead of at the hair root or the spot, and that brings a risk of a burn or a new discolouration.

How many weeks you then wait, you hear at the intake. That is deliberately not given here as a number: it depends on your skin type, on how much colour there is and on where on your body the treatment would happen. The measurement can simply go ahead at that moment, and treatments that do not work with light usually can too.

If a sun holiday is in the calendar, the reverse applies. Freshly treated skin should stay out of the sun for a while, and that is exactly what does not work on holiday. So book the treatment afterwards, or well before, so that your skin has settled before you leave.

The measurement is useful before departure too. You then know what to watch out for in the sun, and on your return there is a starting point to begin from straight away, rather than only then thinking about the waiting time.

Anyone starting in autumn has it easier on all these points. The sun is lower, the holidays are over, and a programme lasting months does not run into summer halfway through. That is also why the calendar for pigment programmes is fuller from September than in May.

> knop: WHAT A SKIN CONSULTATION INVOLVES

**What helps and what we advise against**

A sun holiday need not put your programme on hold. Mostly it decides the order in which you book things.

**THIS WORKS**

- The measurement and the advice, just before departure too

- Treatments that do not work with light, in consultation with your therapist

- Starting a programme in autumn, once the sun is out of it

- Maintenance you have without recovery time, such as a gentle facial treatment

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Laser or IPL on skin with fresh colour from sun or a sunbed

- A peel just before a week in full sun

- Starting a pigment programme in the months of May to August

- Skipping sun protection as soon as a spot lightens. Then it is back within a season

**What the sun does per treatment**

Whether a treatment goes ahead on tanned skin, and what to take into account in the weeks after. The rules apply to a sunbed as well; it gives the same colour.

*TREATMENT*

*WITH COLOUR FROM THE SUN*

*IN THE WEEKS AFTER*

*Laser hair removal*

No. The light aims at pigment, and fresh colour lies in front of it.

Keep the treated area out of full sun and protect it.

*IPL for pigment or redness*

No. IPL sends several wavelengths at once and is even more sensitive to this.

Protect daily, otherwise the discolouration comes back.

*Chemical peel*

Usually not, and otherwise at a lower strength.

Let the peeling happen, do not pick, SPF 50 daily.

*Microneedling*

Often yes, provided your skin is not burnt.

A few days red, then protect against UV.

*Cosmelan and Dermamelan*

No, and we do not start between May and August in any case.

Peeling, and after that protection all year round.

*Fotona 4D*

Not on tanned skin; it is still a laser.

A day red and warm, then protect.

*HydraFacial*

Yes. No light is involved.

No recovery time. The usual sun protection still applies.

*Dermaplaning*

Yes, unless your skin is burnt.

On the north side of the city, in a residential area and not on a shopping street. That helps with parking and it is quieter when you have just been treated.

You park in the street. The route from the ring road and by public transport is on the contact page.

**Frequently asked questions**

How long do I have to wait before lasering after the sun?

Until your skin has its own colour back. How many weeks that takes you hear at the intake, because it depends on your skin type, on how much colour there is and on the area. What you see in the mirror is usually ahead of the pigment still in your skin.

Can I go in the sun after laser hair removal?

The treated area should stay out of full sun for the first few days, and be protected after that. Freshly treated skin reacts more sharply to UV, and then a discolouration can be left that was not there before. Covering up works better than cream alone.

Does a sunbed count too?

Yes, exactly so. A sunbed makes the same pigment as the sun, and that pigment gets in the way of a light treatment in the same manner. So do say it if your colour comes from a sunbed.

What SPF do I need after a treatment?

SPF 50, every day, even when it is cloudy. With a peel and with a pigment programme that is not a side issue but part of the treatment: without protection the result falls back within a season.

Can I have a treatment just before my holiday?

Preferably not. Freshly treated skin should stay out of the sun for a while, and that rarely works on holiday. Book the treatment afterwards, or well before so that your skin has settled. The measurement and the advice are possible, and those are useful before departure.

Why do you not start a pigment programme in summer?

Because a programme like Cosmelan or Dermamelan lasts months and your skin is extra sensitive to UV in that time. In the summer months the sun works against the treatment, and then you pay for a result that falls back straight away. So we start outside the months of May to August.

I am naturally dark. Does this apply to me too?

Your own colour is something other than fresh colour from the sun. Every skin type is treated here, with a setting to match. What matters is the colour that has recently been added, because the setting is not tuned to that.

What is possible when I have just come back from holiday?

The measurement and the advice are always possible, and treatments without light usually are too. Then your starting point is fixed and you can begin as soon as your colour has gone, rather than only then thinking about the waiting time.

Do I need sun protection in winter too?

With a pigment programme and in the weeks after a peel, yes, every day. UV comes through cloud and through glass too, and pigment cells respond to it all year round. Outside those programmes it is mostly a matter of habit: what you skip in winter, you skip in March too.

Does sun protection really help that much with pigmentation?

With pigment it is the largest part of the work. A spot that has been lightened comes back as soon as UV falls on it again, and that goes faster than the treatment lightened it. So protecting daily is cheaper than treating again.

Where in Rotterdam are you?

At Weissenbruchlaan 166 in Rotterdam, on the north side of the city in a residential area. You park in the street. The route and the opening hours are on our contact page.

Let us know when you book. If a holiday is in the calendar or you have just come back, we choose the treatment and the order accordingly, rather than having you come for nothing.

### /en/laser-hair-removal

**Tabbladtitel:** Laser hair removal Rotterdam | GentleMax Pro | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Laser hair removal with the GentleMax Pro in Rotterdam. Work out your price per area, safe for skin types I to VI.

**LASER HAIR REMOVAL IN ROTTERDAM**

We work with the GentleMax Pro, a laser system for safe and effective hair removal. The rates differ per treatment area; you find them per area on the price page.

How many treatments you need differs per person. That depends on your skin type, your hair colour and thickness, the area and the growth phase of the hairs. Because not all hairs are in the same growth phase at once, several sessions are needed.

During the programme we assess the progress, and can estimate better and better how many sessions you need.

> knop: Read on

> knop: BOOK AN APPOINTMENT

> knop: PRICES

ROTTERDAM

Calm in the chair. Precise in the setting.

PROTECTIVE GOGGLES, FOR YOU AND FOR US

- GentleMax Pro A laser aimed at the pigment in the hair root, with cooling so that the top layer does not heat up with it.

- Price beforehand Every area is on the price page with its rate. What you hear at the desk is already there.

- Skin types I to VI The settings are tuned to your Fitzpatrick type and to the area.

> knop: ALL RATES PER AREA

> knop: THE LASER WE USE

**What sets the number of sessions**

Nobody can tell you beforehand how many sessions you need, and anyone who does is guessing. These four things decide it. At the intake the therapist makes a first estimate, and during the series it gets sharper.

- Have your skin type We establish your skin type on the Fitzpatrick scale, from I to VI. From that follows which wavelength is most suitable, alexandrite or Nd:YAG, and which settings we work with.

- The colour and thickness of your hair The laser targets the pigment in the hair root. Dark, thick hair absorbs the energy best. White, grey and red hairs hold too little suitable pigment, and then lasering usually does not work.

- The area Hair growth differs per area. Hair on the upper lip comes back faster than hair on a lower leg, so the number of sessions and the time between them differ per area.

- Your hormones With a hormonal cause such as PCOS your body keeps making new hairs. The existing growth decreases sharply, but maintenance treatments remain necessary.

**What others say about it.**

These come from Salonized and were not picked by us on content. What is not included is a before-and-after, because with hair removal it is mostly the light in the photo that changes and not what you see.

- “I thought the appointment was great! Everything went well and I'm nearly finished with the lasering! Demi is genuinely a very professional skin specialist, so grateful for her! She does her work very precisely.” Monique Laser hair removal OVER 3 YEARS AGO

**Frequently asked questions**

How many sessions do you need?

That depends on the area, your hair type and your hormone balance. Count on a series with weeks in between, because one session only hits the hairs growing at that moment. At the intake you hear what is realistic for you.

Is laser safe for darker skin?

The GentleMax Pro works on Fitzpatrick I to VI. Your skin type decides not whether it is possible, but with which energy and cooling it is done. That is tuned per type.

When do you see a difference?

After the first sessions most people notice the coarser hair thinning. Full reduction takes the whole series; stopping halfway gives the result of half a series and not half the result.

What does laser hair removal cost?

That depends on the area and on which price list applies: for the same area the amount differs between women and men. All sixty-two areas are on the price page with their rate, so you know what a session costs before you book.

**You hear how many sessions at the consult**

At the consultation the therapist establishes your skin type, looks at your hair and the area, and says how many sessions are realistically needed and what that costs. If it does not fit, you hear that too.
