### /en/pcos

**Tabbladtitel:** PCOS and skin | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** The skin concerns with PCOS: unwanted hair growth, acne along the jawline and thinning hair. What we treat and what goes through your doctor.

**PCOS AND YOUR SKIN**

The diagnosis is made by your GP or gynaecologist. The skin concerns that come with it we treat: unwanted hair growth, acne along the jawline, thinning scalp hair and dark patches in skin folds.

Below it says per concern what is possible, what to count on and where your doctor is up.

PCOS is diagnosed by your GP or gynaecologist, with blood tests and an ultrasound.

Once you know what is going on, we work on the skin concerns that come with it. Those two often run alongside each other: your doctor looks at the cause, we look at what you see.

THE ROOM WHERE THE CONVERSATION STARTS

**Who does what.**

Your doctor works on the cause, we work on what you see. The third column says why the two need each other.

- NOT HERE The GP or gynaecologist Establishing whether there is PCOS, carrying out tests, and treating what is going on underneath. Everything to do with hormones, medication and blood values.

- HERE Us The skin concerns you see: unwanted hair growth, acne along the jawline, thinning scalp hair and dark patches in skin folds. Each with its own approach.

- NOT HERE Together As long as the cause plays a part, the skin keeps moving with it. So a treatment works best alongside your doctor's care, and you keep the result up with maintenance.

**What we can do with PCOS**

With every concern both sides stand equally emphatically. One without the other is a sales pitch.

- Unwanted hair growth in a male pattern Coarser, darker hair in places you are not used to it: chin, jawline, neck, chest or stomach. Often the consequence people withdraw over most. HOW LASER HAIR REMOVAL WORKS › WHAT WE DO Laser hair removal works here, and usually well. The hair is coarse and dark and that is exactly what the laser acts on. WHAT TO COUNT ON We do not take away the signal that makes that hair grow. New hairs will keep appearing, so this becomes maintenance and not an end point. Count on more sessions than the standard programme and on coming back periodically afterwards.

- Acne along the jawline and on the neck Deeper, tender spots that stay longer than ordinary acne, often low on the face and on the neck. They come and go in periods. MORE ABOUT ACNE › WHAT WE DO Settling the skin, tackling inflamed spots and limiting scarring. That is real work and it makes a noticeable difference. WHAT TO COUNT ON Taking away the cause. As long as it is there, your skin moves with it. A programme that works in March can flare again in September, and that is not a failed programme but a condition that is still there.

- Thinning scalp hair Less volume, a widening parting, more hair in the brush. Unlike the hair growth elsewhere this is a loss and not a surplus. WHAT WE DO Looking along and recording what we see, so that months later there is something to compare. WHAT TO COUNT ON Treating it. Hair loss with PCOS is a hormonal matter and we have no treatment for it. Anyone who tells you otherwise is selling you something.

- Dark, velvety patches in skin folds On the neck, underarms or groin: a darker discolouration that feels soft and does not wash away. It is not dirt and not a pigment spot. WHAT WE DO We do nothing about this, and that is deliberate. WHAT TO COUNT ON Removing it. This discolouration is a signal and not a cosmetic problem, and treating over it only makes the signal invisible.

**Sometimes we send you away instead.**

A skin clinic sometimes sees something before a diagnosis exists. The right step then is not to offer a programme but to say where you should be.

> knop: WHAT WE DO DO

- Acne along the jawline and on the neck With painful lumps under the skin or scars that stay, a doctor should take a look. There is medication for that and we cannot give it.

- Thinning scalp hair Yes. This belongs with your GP and if needed with a dermatologist, and not with a skin clinic.

- Dark, velvety patches in skin folds Yes, and this is the most important of the four. This discolouration is tied to how your body handles insulin. Have it checked by your GP, even if it does not otherwise bother you.

**Then we find out first what is there.**

A programme starts with a measurement, and with PCOS that is extra useful: your skin moves with periods, so without a starting point you cannot see later whether something worked or whether it was simply a quiet month.

If something is already running with your GP or gynaecologist, say so at the intake. Not because we do anything with it, but because it matters for what we advise and when.

> knop: Read on

**What people asked about this.**

If your question is not here, you get the answer on the phone without an appointment having to come of it.

- COVER PER INSURER

- CANCELLING, PAYING AND RESCHEDULING

**What does this cost?**

That depends on the treatment that suits your skin, and we work that out at the consultation. The consultation costs 50 euros; if you have a treatment in the same appointment, that amount comes off again. You then hear straight away how many sessions it takes and what the total will be. Every price per treatment is published on the price page.

**Is VAT included?**

Yes. The amounts on this page are what you pay at the desk. Nothing is added for materials or for opening a file.

**Is this covered by my insurance?**

That depends on your supplementary policy and on whether there is a medical indication. Diba Clinics has contracts with all health insurers; the insurance cover page says per insurer what is included.

**Are there discounts, packages or offers?**

All rates are public, per session and per version. There are no discounts, promo codes or temporary offers, so there is never a moment when you were too early or too late.

**What if I cancel my appointment?**

Up to 48 hours before your appointment you can cancel or reschedule, by phone or by message. You do not have to give a reason. If you cancel less than 48 hours before, or do not turn up without a message, your deposit is forfeited. For a new appointment we ask for a deposit again.

**When do I pay?**

You pay in the clinic itself. The deposit you paid when booking is set off against the total.

**What if the treatment cannot go ahead?**

Then you do not pay for the treatment.

**You hear how many decides your total**

The amounts above are fixed. What you pay in total depends on how often you come, and that differs per skin. Naming a number before we have measured is a gamble with your money, so we do not do it.

At the intake you hear how many sessions it is for you and what that comes to together. That is the first moment anyone can say anything sensible about it.

### /en/privacy-policy

**Tabbladtitel:** Privacy policy | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** This website collects nothing itself. Where your details do end up, what happens there and which rights you have.

**HOW WE HANDLE YOUR DATA**

Op dibaclinics.nl there is one form, on the contact page. What you fill in there reaches us as an email and nowhere else. No newsletter, no profile we build, no field that quietly does something else.

Most of your data, by the way, sits somewhere other than this site. Below is where, and what happens there.

Questions about your data go to info@dibaclinics.nl or by phone to 010-2038423. Do mention that it is a privacy request, so that it reaches the right person.

**Where your data does end up.**

Three of the four are not this website. With every place it says what sits there and where it goes.

- OURS This website The choice you make on the cookie bar and the skin profile if you fill it in. Both stay in your own browser; that profile consists of choices from lists, without a name, email address or photo. WHERE IT GOES Nowhere. Clear your browser data and it is gone.

- THIS WEBSITE The contact form Your name, your email address, your phone number if you fill it in, the subject you choose and your message. Only if you send that form yourself. WHERE IT GOES As an email to the clinic, sent by Resend as processor. We keep the message in our mailbox and do not put it into a system or a list.

- BOOKING SYSTEM Salonized Your appointment details and the contact details you fill in when booking. Also the reviews you leave, because those are collected there. WHERE IT GOES To Salonized as processor, for scheduling appointments and tracking your programme.

- MESSAGING WhatsApp What you send us, including photos if you attach them to a question about aftercare. WHERE IT GOES Via WhatsApp, which has a privacy policy of its own that we do not control. If you want to share something sensitive, rather call.

- YOUR FILE At the clinic What was discussed at the intake, what was measured, which treatments you have had and how your skin responded. WHERE IT GOES This stays in the clinic and is the only place where truly sensitive data sits. Only the people treating you look into it.

**How long we keep your data**

A medical treatment file has to be kept for twenty years, counted from the last time anything in it changed. That is not our choice: since 1 January 2020 it is in the law, in article 7:454 of the Dutch Civil Code. Before that it was fifteen years. What does not belong to such a file we keep for less time, and below it says per item why.

- Your treatment fileTwenty yearsRequired by law under the Dutch Medical Treatment Contracts Act (article 7:454 of the Civil Code), counted from the last change in the file. This is not a period we are allowed to shorten.

- Photos belonging to a treatmentTwenty yearsThose belong to the file and fall under the same obligation. Photos you have separately allowed us to use outside your file are deleted as soon as you withdraw that permission.

- Invoices and administrationSeven yearsThe retention obligation set by the Dutch tax authority.

- What you message or email usAs long as the conversation runs, cleared out afterwardsNo obligation; we keep it only as long as it serves a purpose.

- Measurement data from this websiteAt most fourteen monthsOnly if you have accepted the cookie bar. If you decline, nothing is measured and so there is nothing to keep.

*WHICH DATA*

*HOW LONG*

*ON WHAT BASIS*

**Six rights, wherever something sits.**

You do not have to work out which party holds something. Put the question to us and we will find out.

- Access You may request which data about you exists and what happens to it.

- Correction If something is wrong, we have it changed.

- Erasure Where the law allows it. Parts of a treatment file are subject to statutory retention periods; we explain that rather than talking around it.

- Objection Against a processing you do not agree with.

- Portability Requesting your data in a readable file to use it elsewhere.

- Complaint If you do not reach an agreement with us, you can go to the Dutch Data Protection Authority. You always have that right, even without complaining to us first.

> knop: SUBMIT A REQUEST

**What we do with your data**

No advertising profiles are built of you and nothing is sold on or traded. The only measurement on this site is anonymous statistics, and it loads only after you agree to it; without agreement those scripts are not loaded.

Your skin profile is deliberately not sent to us. That is the place where the temptation to ask for an email address is greatest, and so it does not happen.

### /en/quality-and-registrations

**Tabbladtitel:** Quality and registrations | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Which registers Diba Clinics, the skin therapists and the beauty specialists belong to, what that registration involves and how a complaint is handled.

**QUALITY AND REGISTRATIONS**

Our skin therapists are in the Dutch Quality Register for Paramedics and members of the professional association. The clinic is a member of ANBOS and contracted with all health insurers.

Below it says per register what it involves and how to check it yourself.

**Six things you can check**

- OUR SKIN THERAPISTS Dutch Association of Skin Therapists The professional association of skin therapists. Members have to be registered in the Dutch Quality Register for Paramedics; one cannot exist without the other. A professional association writes the code of conduct and the guidelines a skin therapist has to keep to. That is a standard from outside the clinic. WHO WORKS HERE AND WITH WHICH TITLE ›

- OUR SKIN THERAPISTS Dutch Quality Register for Paramedics The register is voluntary and the bar is real: re-registration every five years, and for that at least 1600 working hours over at least 36 months plus 160 points of continuing education. Skin therapist is a protected title (article 34 of the Individual Healthcare Professions Act). The title says someone has done the training; the register says someone actually practises the profession and keeps it current. COVER PER INSURER ›

- THE CLINIC AND OUR BEAUTY THERAPISTS ANBOS The trade body for beauty therapists. Member salons work to the industry's code of conduct and hygiene guidelines, and fall under the ANBOS complaints procedure. The part of our work that is not paramedical falls under this. That too comes with a standard written by someone other than us, and a complaints route that does not stop with us. HOW A COMPLAINT RUNS ›

- OUR BEAUTY THERAPISTS SKIN Register The quality register for beauty therapists. It registers people, not salons: every beauty therapist is listed in it by name. Beauty therapist is not a protected title. The register is the way to see that someone has learned the trade and keeps it current. WHO WORKS HERE AND WITH WHICH TITLE ›

- THE CLINIC Contracted with all health insurers There is a contract with all Dutch health insurers. That does not mean everything is covered: what you get back depends on your supplementary policy and on the indication. It saves you the trouble of paying upfront and claiming for the treatments that do fall under your policy. COVER PER INSURER ›

- THE CLINIC ZorgkaartNederland The independent rating site of the Dutch Patients Federation. Patients rate care providers there; we cannot place, change or remove those ratings. A rating that does not go through us says more than one that does. We stand there at 9.7, and you check that figure yourself. SEE US ON ZORGKAARTNEDERLAND ↗

**Who is in which register**

At Diba there are skin therapists and beauty therapists. Those are two professions, each with its own association and its own register. That is why there are four names above and not two.

*Skin therapists*

Members of the Dutch Association of Skin Therapists and registered in the Dutch Quality Register for Paramedics. For members of the association that registration is mandatory.

*Beauty therapists*

Members of ANBOS and registered by name in the SKIN Register, the quality register for beauty therapists.

### /en/referrers

**Tabbladtitel:** For referring practitioners | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** For GPs and other care providers who want to refer. Where the boundary lies, who carries out the treatment and how to refer.

**REFERRING TO DIBA. WHAT YOU SHOULD KNOW.**

This page is for GPs, practice nurses, dermatologists and other healthcare providers considering sending a patient here. It starts with where the line lies, because that is the question that makes your referral usable.

Diba Clinics is in Rotterdam. There are 11 people working here, some of whom carry a legally protected title.

> knop: EMAIL A REFERRAL

There are two reasons why something does not happen here. They are worked out per concern on a page of their own.

- This belongs with a doctor Not because we do not feel like it, but because it falls outside the scope of a skin therapist. This is where a good clinic sends you away.

- This is not possible right now Almost always temporary. It says for how long, so that you know when you can come.

WHERE YOUR PATIENT ENDS UP

**One title is protected by law.**

For referrers we state clearly which job titles and registrations apply.

Skin therapist

Works with the devices and the treatments: laser, light, needling, peels. Judges what your skin can take and tunes the settings to it.

Orthomolecular skin specialist

Looks at what plays a part from within: food, hormones, digestion. With acne and pigment that is often half the story.

Laser specialist

Works with the laser and light equipment: hair removal, and light aimed at colour or vessels. Chooses the setting per skin type and per area.

DUTCH QUALITY REGISTER FOR PARAMEDICS

A voluntary register with a five-year cycle. Anyone who stays in it demonstrates at least 1600 working hours per period, spread over at least 36 months, and 160 points of continuing education.

**What your patient takes away**

Nothing is treated on a referral alone. That is not a formality: it is the reason the advice your patient takes away can be honest.

- A measurement under fixed light Every first appointment starts with an objective skin analysis: the same light, the same angle, the same settings. That image remains the starting point later appointments are measured against.

- A plan with a limit in it What is possible, how many sessions that takes and what it is not going to do. With every treatment on this site the limit is stated as emphatically as the effect.

- Sometimes the advice to do nothing If the measurement shows that treating gives little or that the moment is wrong, your patient hears that. It happens and it is not an exception.

**Referring goes by letter or email**

A referral letter you hand over or an email is enough. There is no portal or form, and there does not need to be.

- FIRST STEP By letter or by email Give your patient the referral letter, or email it to info@dibaclinics.nl. What it says is up to you; a short description of the concern and what you have already tried helps most.

- WHAT HAPPENS THEN The measurement first Nothing is treated on the referral alone. First the measurement, then a plan, and that plan can differ from what the referral says.

- WHEN IN DOUBT Ask first If you are not sure whether something belongs here, email your question or call. That costs you five minutes and saves your patient an appointment that would otherwise come to nothing.

Whether and how the referrer is reported back to after the measurement has not been settled yet, so no promise is made about it. Do call or email with the question; then you hear how it stands at that moment.

> knop: 010-2038423

**What else there is to check.**

- What we treat All treatments, with what they do and what they cost.

- The 12 devices What we have, how deep it reaches and what it cannot do.

- Insurance cover Why the insurer is not the first question, and when a referral is needed.

- The team Who works here, with which title and what that title means.

### /en/skin-concerns

**Tabbladtitel:** Treating skin concerns in Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** With acne what counts is where it sits, with pigment which season it is, with scars how old they are. Choose what troubles you and see where we start.

**ALL SKIN CONCERNS**

With every concern something else counts: where it sits, which season it is, how old it is or how deep it lies. Pick your concern and read what counts in your case.

With acne it is where it sits that counts, because the place says something about the cause. With pigmentation it is which season it is. With scars how old they are, and with melasma how deep the pigment lies. That sounds like a detail and it decides the outcome: start with the wrong question and you spend months treating the wrong thing.

> knop: Read on

You do not need to know what it is called. Tick what you see and we will find the page for it.

> knop: TO THE SYMPTOM FINDER

> knop: OR ASK YOUR QUESTION

WHERE THE CONVERSATION TAKES PLACE

**What we treat.**

Each with its own page that starts with the question weighing heaviest for that concern. Measure first, then a plan, and sometimes the advice is to do nothing.

- Acne Where on your face is it?

- Acne scars Scar or colour?

- Lines and fine wrinkles Does the line move with you?

- Under-eye bags Is it less in the evening?

- Age spots Has the spot changed?

- Milia and oil seeds White and hard, or red?

- Skin laxity What do you see lying down?

- Ingrown hairs Is there a hair in it?

- Congested skin Blackhead or pore?

- Keratosis pilaris Bumps or roughness?

- Dull skin Where does it come from?

- Skin tags On a little stalk?

- Rosacea What sets it off?

- Couperose Vessels or flush?

- Pigmentation Which season is it?

- Melasma How deep does the pigment sit?

- Scars How old is the scar?

- Stretch marks Are they still red or already white?

- Skin ageing Is this time or is this sun?

- Pores What can be done?

- Dry skin Oil or water?

- Sensitive skin What is switched on?

- Dark circles Colour or shadow?

**What we do together with a doctor.**

We do treat these concerns, only not on our own. The doctor does what is medically needed and we do what the skin asks for alongside that. Who starts depends on what is going on.

- Keloids Beyond the edge of the wound?

- Eczema Where does the circle break?

- Psoriasis Your nails as well?

- Skin rash Do you call today or tomorrow?

**What belongs with a doctor.**

These pages have no booking button. They are here because people ask us about this while lying in our chair, and then a good answer beats an evasive one.

- Moles Has anything changed?

**What nobody can do anything about.**

It says so plainly, with the explanation of why no cream or device takes it away. Then you know where you stand before you start anything.

**Then start with what you see.**

Two signposts that sort by colour or by what you feel, rather than by a name you do not know.

- Skin discolouration What colour is it?

- Symptom finder What exactly do you see?

**The same four questions, every time.**

- What is it, really Explained the way we say it in the treatment room, with the medical term alongside.

- What works and what does not What works and what we advise against, and the reason behind both.

- What we do about it Which treatment fits, what you can expect from it and what it costs.

- How we measure it We record how your skin stands at the start, so that a difference can be seen later.

**Everything starts with measuring.**

Every skin question starts with an assessment, which can also end in us advising no treatment at all.

### /en/skin-concerns/acne

**Tabbladtitel:** Treating acne in Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Treating acne with peels, needling and laser. Which type you have, what can be done about it and what a treatment costs with us.

**ACNE THAT KEEPS COMING BACK**

Acne comes in different forms, and each form asks for a different approach. We first work out which one you are dealing with and treat that, with peels, needling, laser or a combination.

Is it mostly what has been left behind? Then it starts with acne scars, because that is often not a scar at all.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

**Where it sits says what it is.**

The jawline points to something different than the T-zone. On the cheeks it can come from outside, from your phone or your pillowcase, but it can just as well be hormonal. And acne on your back, shoulders or chest is a zone of its own, with its own cause. Tap where yours sits and we read along. You can pick more than one.

More than one is fine. The place often says more about the cause than how bad it looks.

> knop: Forehead

> knop: Cheeks

> knop: Nose

> knop: Jawline

> knop: Chin

OUTSIDE THE FACE

> knop: Back and shoulders

> knop: Décolleté and chest

Hover over a zone to read what it usually means on its own. Tap it to count it in the reading beside this.

**Tap where it sits**

You can choose more than one zone. Where acne sits often tells you more about the cause than how it looks.

If you cannot point it out well, we go through the zones together at the consultation.

This is a reading of a pattern, not a diagnosis. Two people with the same zones can get a different plan. That is why we measure before we treat.

**Which acne do you have?**

Acne is not one thing. The type decides what actually helps, and with one of these five it decides that you belong with a doctor rather than with us.

- Blackheads, little redness Small bumps and black dots, but not really inflamed

- Red bumps and whiteheads Red spots that come up, sometimes with a white head

- Deep, painful nodules Hard lumps under your skin that stay for days or weeks

- Mostly on chin and jawline Spots on your chin that follow your cycle

- From friction or contact Spots exactly where something presses against your skin

*WHAT YOU SEE*

Skin that feels rough when you run a hand over it. Open blackheads with a dark head and closed ones you mostly feel. Little redness, hardly any pain.

*WHAT IT MEANS*

The pore is blocked, but your immune system has not stepped in yet. This is the stage where you can prevent the most rather than repair.

*WHAT WE DO FIRST*

Cleaning the pores and working on the build-up of keratin, in steps and without irritating the skin. This is often the course with the fewest sessions.

Those dark dots are not dirt. It is sebum that has discoloured in the air. That is why scrubbing does not get it out.

> knop: HAVE THIS LOOKED AT

**Acne runs through several stages**

At each stage you can do something different. That is why scrubbing harder does not work: it acts on the second stage and makes the fourth worse. Click through and see what changes.

> knop: SEBUM

> knop: KERATIN BUILD-UP

> knop: BACTERIA

> knop: INFLAMMATION

STAGE 1 OF 4

**Sebum**

Your skin shines sooner than you want, mostly on your nose and forehead.

The sebaceous gland sits deep in the skin and makes oil that travels up along the hair shaft. Under the influence of hormones it makes more than the skin can clear.

Creams do little about the production itself. What does work is improving the way out, so that it does not sit there.

**What helps and what we advise against**

On the left what we do with acne, on the right what we advise against. Each point says why, because nobody remembers a “do not” without a reason.

**THIS WORKS**

- A skin analysis before we start, so that we can measure later under comparable conditions

- Cleaning pores and working on keratin build-up, in steps your skin can take

- Inflammation down first, with chemical peels and herbal peels that are also antibacterial. Scars after that, never at the same time

- Sun protection, every day, in winter too. This prevents the dark marks that stay behind after a spot

- Referring you to a doctor when the picture calls for it, even though you came to us

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Toothpaste or lemon juice on a spot. It irritates the skin and leaves a dark mark more often than the spot itself would

- A sunbed. It hides redness for a while and damages your skin in the meantime

- Scrubbing every day. You take away the barrier that is meant to limit the inflammation

- Alcohol toners that make your skin feel tight. Dehydrated skin makes more sebum, not less

- Squeezing it yourself. You push the inflammation deeper instead of out. This is the fastest route to a scar

**Why we start with the inflammation**

Treating scars on skin that is still inflamed makes the picture worse. So we settle the inflammation first and work on the scars after that. That order gives more than trying both at once.

- The inflammation first, the scar after Lasering or needling in active acne makes the inflammation worse and can set a scar. We wait until the skin is calm before we start.

- Medication goes through your doctor Antibiotics, the pill and isotretinoin are prescribed by your GP or dermatologist. We adjust our treatment to what your doctor has given you.

- No fixed number of sessions in advance How many sessions you need depends on your skin and how it responds. So we do not promise a number beforehand: we measure along the way, and we stop if it is not working.

**These are the things we follow with acne**

The EVE-M measurement records your skin before we start. With acne, pores, inflammation, redness and texture are the axes that count. After eight to twelve weeks we measure again and put the two side by side.

That is not to convince you. It is so that we can see it when something is not working, and do something else.

> knop: Read on

> knop: MORE ABOUT THE SKIN ANALYSIS

- Pores Size and density, measured rather than estimated

- Redness How much active inflammation is visible and where

- Texture Unevenness, and whether scars are starting to form

**Frequently asked questions**

Will this get rid of my acne?

For most people acne can be kept under control. For some it keeps coming back, because of hormones for instance. We say beforehand what we think is realistic in your case, and we measure whether it works. Control is sometimes the honest goal, and that is not second best.

How many sessions do I need?

That depends on the type of acne, how long it has been going on and how your skin responds to the first treatments. After the skin analysis you hear what we expect and what a session costs, but we cannot promise a fixed number beforehand.

I have tried everything. Why would this work?

Honestly, we do not know that yet. That is why we start by measuring rather than treating. If we think it will not work here, we would rather say so now than after six sessions.

Can I keep using make-up?

Yes. We do look together at what you use, because a few common products keep the picture going without you noticing.

Can I come if I am under a dermatologist?

You can, and it is often sensible. Do tell us, so that we can work out what combines safely with your medication.

Does it help if I change my diet?

Sometimes. We work with a laboratory and can do a food intolerance test; if something comes out of it, changing your diet really does have an effect. Without that test it stays guesswork, and we are not going to talk you into a diet here.

It is mostly the marks that are left behind.

Those are usually not scars but pigment marks. Sun protection stops them getting darker and stops new ones appearing, but it does not remove a mark that is already there; that needs treatment. If there is a dip in the skin, then it is a scar, and we look at it as soon as the skin is calm.

What does this cost?

That depends on the treatment that suits your skin, and we work that out at the consultation. The consultation costs 50 euros; if you have a treatment in the same appointment, that amount comes off again. You then hear straight away how many sessions it takes and what the total will be. Every price per treatment is published on the price page.

**What others say about it.**

These come from Salonized and were not picked by us on content: they are the reviews in which acne, spots or congestion come up. Watch the time mentioned in them, because with acne that is what it is about.

### /en/skin-concerns/acne-scars

**Tabbladtitel:** Treating acne scars in Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Treating acne scars with peels, microneedling and laser. The difference between a pit, a red mark and pigment.

**WHAT ACNE LEAVES BEHIND ON YOUR SKIN**

What acne leaves behind is usually a red mark, a brown patch or a small dent. They look alike and ask for different treatments: peels for discolouration, microneedling and laser for dents.

At the intake the skin therapist assesses it under light falling from the side. That is the only way to see whether there is a dent in it or whether it is about colour.

> knop: Read on

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

**Four pictures and what each one asks for**

These four cover almost everything acne leaves behind. Which one you have is established by the skin therapist at the intake.

- There is still active acne New spots are still appearing

- Red or purple marks Flat red patches where a spot used to be

- Brown or dark patches Dark patches that stay where the spots were

- Dents or pits Dips in your skin that you see best in side light

*HOW YOU RECOGNISE IT YOURSELF*

Has a new inflamed spot appeared in the past month? Then this is your answer, even if you are mostly looking at the old marks.

*WHAT IT IS*

As long as new inflammations keep appearing, new marks keep appearing too. Treating what is already there while the source is still running is mopping with the tap on.

*DOES IT GO AWAY ON ITS OWN*

Not while the acne is active. The marks fading now are replaced by new ones.

*WHAT WE DO*

Calm the acne first. Only then do we look at what has been left behind, and it is often less than you think now.

No tissue has been lost. That means a different treatment, and often different advice from the one you came for.

> knop: HAVE THIS LOOKED AT

**The order of treating**

Every step asks that the previous one is finished. So a scar programme rarely starts with the laser straight away.

- The inflammation first As long as new spots keep appearing, new marks keep appearing. And any scar treatment in inflamed skin makes the inflammation worse.

- Then let the colour settle Red and brown partly fade on their own. What you still see after six months is what is really there; before that you would be treating something that was going to disappear anyway.

- Only then the pits What remains is scar tissue. That is the only type where a series of treatments really changes something in the long run.

Then it starts with the acne and not with the scars.

Treating what is there while the source is still running is mopping with the tap on, and in inflamed skin it makes the inflammation worse as well.

> knop: TO THE ACNE PAGE

**What helps and what we advise against**

Here the right order often gives more than the heaviest treatment.

**THIS WORKS**

- Establishing first whether it is scar tissue or colour, because that often saves a whole programme

- Waiting until the acne is calm before anything happens to the scars

- Sun protection, every day. With brown patches this is not an extra but the core

- A skin analysis in side light, because in straight light you barely see pits

- Saying when waiting gives more than treating, even when you came here for a treatment

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Lasering or needling skin with active inflammation. That worsens the acne and can lock the scar in place

- Treating a pigment spot as though it were a scar. It is a different layer and a different approach

- Promising that pits disappear completely. Shallower and less visible is realistic, gone is not

- Squeezing them yourself raises the chance of deeper inflammation, discolouration and scars

- Starting on tanned skin

**Pits only show in side light.**

That is why a photo from your phone is not enough here, and neither is your bathroom mirror: straight light fills in every dent. The EVE-M records your skin under fixed light and from a fixed angle.

That way the difference can be seen later rather than believed, and with this concern that matters extra: it takes months, and you see your own face every day.

> knop: MORE ABOUT THE SKIN ANALYSIS

WHAT WE MEASURE HERE

*Relief*

Where the skin has sunk in, and how deep

*Redness*

The vascular response left behind after inflammation

*Pigmentation*

Brown patches, including the ones you cannot see yet

Every axis is measured again at each check-up, under the same lighting. That way a difference later is something you see rather than something you have to take on faith.

**What we use for this**

- Microneedling with the SkinPen € 180 Medically certified microneedling. It works on the layer where the structure of your skin sits. FOR THIS CONCERN WITH THE SKINPEN CIT MICRONEEDLING IN ROTTERDAM

- Dermapen 4 € 180 Microneedling with vibrating needles that pass through the skin evenly. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE DERMAPEN 4

- FRAC3 On request A fractional laser that goes deeper, for texture, pores and irregularities. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER FOTONA 4D IN ROTTERDAM

- Fotona Scar Repair € 195 Laser on scars: acne scars, surgical scars and stretch marks. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER

- Fotona Resurfacing On request Skin renewal with laser, for pores, texture and smoother skin. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER

**What others say about it.**

These come from Salonized and were not picked by us on content: they are the reviews that mention scars, mostly after an acne programme.

- “I've been by 3 times now for the diode laser and I genuinely see an 80% difference! The scars and spots on my skin have hugely improved too thanks to the dermapen. A forever regular anyway!!” Sara Laser hair removal OVER 7 YEARS AGO

**Frequently asked questions**

How do I know whether it is a scar or only colour?

With your finger and with light from the side. If you feel a dent or an edge, and you see a shadow when the light falls at an angle, tissue has been lost. If it feels smooth and you only see colour, it is redness or pigment and not a scar.

Do acne scars go away on their own?

Red and brown marks partly do, over months. Dents do not: they will sit there just the same years from now. That distinction decides whether waiting is sensible or a waste of time.

How long should I wait after my last spot?

There is no fixed period; what matters is that no new inflammations are appearing and that the skin is calm. We look at that at the measurement, and sometimes the answer is that we look again in a few months.

Can pits disappear completely?

No. What we can do is make them shallower and less visible, over a series of several sessions. We do not promise smooth skin, because we cannot know that before the measurement and usually not after it either.

**Book a consultation at Diba Clinics**

At the skin consultation we establish whether it is scar tissue or colour. Sometimes the outcome is that you need do nothing for six months, and then we say so.

### /en/skin-concerns/age-spots

**Tabbladtitel:** Treating age spots in Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Removing age spots and sun spots with IPL or laser, usually in one or two sessions.

**AGE SPOTS TREATED**

Age spots and sun spots are harmless and respond well to treatment. We remove them with IPL or laser, and one or two sessions is usually enough.

The therapist assesses each spot first. If anything about the shape or the colour is changing, it goes to your GP first.

> knop: Read on

> knop: SEE WHICH ONE YOU HAVE

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

**What we look at**

The therapist assesses shape, edge and colour, and records the spot in an image. That way it can be seen later whether anything has changed.

- Shape, edge and colour The therapist looks at whether the colour is even and whether the edge runs sharply. That separates a sun spot from something else.

- Under UV light Under that, how much pigment sits deeper in the skin becomes visible. That decides how many sessions to count on.

- Recorded in images We photograph the spot under fixed lighting. At a following appointment we put the images side by side and you see what has changed.

Then a doctor looks at it first, and we treat it after that.

A ragged edge, uneven colour, growth or itching are reasons to have it assessed first. If it is benign, we remove the spot here afterwards.

> knop: TO THE ABCDE CHECK

**Four kinds of brown spots**

Four kinds of brown spot that look alike. If anything about a spot is changing, it goes to your GP first.

- A flat brown spot An even brown mark on your hand, temple or décolleté

- A rough brown bump A brown spot that feels raised, as though it were stuck on

- Large patches on your cheeks Symmetrical brown areas, often after a pregnancy or the pill

- A spot that is changing Something that grows, changes colour, itches or bleeds

*HOW YOU RECOGNISE IT YOURSELF*

Does it feel completely smooth, is it even in colour with a sharp edge, and does it sit on a place that has had a lot of sun?

*WHAT IT IS*

Pigment that has gathered in one place after years of sun exposure. Harmless, and the most common picture on this page.

*WHAT WE DO*

This responds well to light. We first measure how much there is, including what you cannot see yet, and then treat it in a series.

An even, flat spot on a place that has had a lot of sun. This is the picture where light gives the most.

> knop: HAVE THIS LOOKED AT

**What helps and what we advise against**

With pigmentation, sun protection is not advice afterwards but part of the treatment. Without it, it comes back and the money is gone.

**THIS WORKS**

- Assessing first whether a spot is harmless, and referring rather than treating when in doubt

- A skin analysis under UV light, because that shows pigment that is already there and not yet visible

- Sun protection, every day and all year. Without it the spots come back and the rest does not work

- Light on flat, even spots, in a series with time in between

- Saying honestly that new ones can appear as long as you are in the sun

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Burning off everything brown. A spot that is changing should be assessed first

- Treating melasma as though it were a sun spot. That makes it worse rather than better

- Hydroquinone creams on your own. That belongs under supervision

- Treating in summer without agreements about the sun. That is money thrown away

- Starting on tanned skin

**Under UV you see what is still to come.**

Pigment starts deeper in the skin than where you see it. Under UV light, what is already there and has not yet come through at the surface becomes visible, and that is often more than people expect.

Confronting, and useful: it explains why new spots seem to keep appearing without sun protection. They were not new; they were already there.

> knop: MORE ABOUT THE SKIN ANALYSIS

WHAT WE MEASURE HERE

*Visible pigmentation*

The spots as you see them in the mirror now

*Underlying pigmentation*

What lies deeper and comes through later

*Sun damage*

How much the skin has had to take over the years

Every axis is measured again at each check-up, under the same lighting. That way a difference later is something you see rather than something you have to take on faith.

**What we use for this**

- Medical peels € 140 From light to strong. The strength decides how deep it goes and how much you flake. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE PEEL LINES CHEMICAL PEEL IN ROTTERDAM

- Nordlys IPL for pigmentation € 75 Light on pigmentation and sun damage. The pigment first comes to the surface and then fades. FOR THIS CONCERN WITH THE NORDLYS IPL TREATMENT IN ROTTERDAM

- Cosmelan € 720 A six-month programme against hyperpigmentation, with a mask at the clinic and products at home. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE PEEL LINES COSMELAN AND DERMAMELAN IN ROTTERDAM

**Frequently asked questions**

Are age spots dangerous?

An ordinary sun spot is harmless. Other spots look like one at first, and those are not always harmless. So the first question here is not how to get rid of it but whether it is what you think it is.

Do they come back after the treatment?

The treated spot does not come back, but new ones can appear as long as your skin keeps catching sun. That is why sun protection here is not advice afterwards but part of the treatment.

Why do I see more spots after the measurement than in the mirror?

Because pigment starts deeper in the skin than where you see it. The measurement shows what is already there, and that is sometimes confronting. It is also useful: it explains why new ones seem to keep appearing without protection.

Can this be done on my hands too?

Yes, and that is often the place people find it bothersome first. The skin there is thinner and heals more slowly, so we work more carefully than on the face.

What does this cost?

That depends on the treatment that suits your skin, and we work that out at the consultation. The consultation costs 50 euros; if you have a treatment in the same appointment, that amount comes off again. You then hear straight away how many sessions it takes and what the total will be. Every price per treatment is published on the price page.

**Book a consultation at Diba Clinics**

At the skin consultation we assess the spots and measure, under UV light, the pigment you cannot see yet. After that you know what is possible and what belongs somewhere else first.

### /en/skin-concerns/congested-skin

**Tabbladtitel:** Blemished skin and blackheads | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Treating blackheads and blocked pores with HydraFacial and peels. The difference between normal pore contents and real blackheads.

**BLACKHEADS AND CONGESTED SKIN**

Blackheads and blocked pores we treat with a HydraFacial, peels and targeted care. That empties the pores and keeps them calmer.

At the intake we look along under magnification and establish which type of congestion it is.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

**What we look at**

The skin therapist looks at your pores under magnification and judges whether it is normal pore content or real blackheads.

- The light from the side The skin therapist assesses your skin with light falling from the side. Straight light hides irregularities; light from the side shows them.

- How they are spread across your skin If almost every pore has a grey dot in it, that is normal pore content. If they are scattered and darker, they are blackheads.

- What you feel but do not see Bumps on your forehead and jawline that you feel but cannot see are closed pores. Those ask for a different approach.

**What can sit in a pore**

In everyday language blocked pores, blackheads and congestion run into each other. The difference decides which treatment works.

- Grey dots on your nose Small grey dots in almost every pore on your nose

- Blackheads Separate dark dots that look genuinely stuck in there

- Bumps without a head Small irregularities you feel more than see, often on your forehead

- Red, inflamed spots Spots that hurt and are red, and that keep coming back

*HOW YOU RECOGNISE IT YOURSELF*

Is it spread evenly across almost every pore, rather than here and there? And does gentle pressure bring out a short, light-grey thread?

*WHAT IT IS*

Not a blackhead but the normal content of a working pore: sebum with some cells. Everyone has them, and they are back within weeks because they are meant to come back.

*WHAT WE DO*

Here we mostly tell you what to leave alone. They can be made less visible for a while, not removed, and that difference saves people years of fighting.

This is normal skin, or it is already about acne. In the first case there is nothing to treat; in the second a different programme belongs with it.

> knop: HAVE THIS LOOKED AT

Then it is no longer about congestion.

Regular red, painful spots that leave marks behind is acne, and that asks for a different approach and a different order from relieving pores.

> knop: TO THE ACNE PAGE

**What helps and what we advise against**

Here the gain is more often in what you stop than in what you add. With a blocked pore, cleansing more harshly usually gives nothing.

**THIS WORKS**

- Telling normal sebaceous filaments apart from genuinely blocked pores first

- Letting the top layer renew gradually so that full pores open up again

- Looking at what you use now, because a few common products keep the picture going

- Taking into account that oily skin should not be dried out; it then makes more oil

- Referring on to the acne programme as soon as there is structural inflammation

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Pore strips and suction devices. They remove sebaceous filaments that are back within weeks, and stretch the pore in the meantime

- Scrubbing daily. You take the barrier away and the skin answers with more oil

- Alcohol toners that make your skin feel tight. Dehydrated skin makes more oil, not less

- Squeezing them yourself. A closed pore becomes an inflammation that way, and an inflammation becomes a mark

- Promising that pores get smaller. They can be empty and so stand out less; their size is fixed

**What we use for this**

- HydraFacial € 170 Cleansing, exfoliation and hydration. In one pass, visible straight away and with no recovery time. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE HYDRAFACIAL SYNDEO HYDRAFACIAL IN ROTTERDAM

- Medical peels € 140 From light to strong. The strength decides how deep it goes and how much you flake. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE PEEL LINES CHEMICAL PEEL IN ROTTERDAM

- Herbal peel € 150 A peel of finely ground herbs, without acid. It calms the inflammation and works against bacteria. WHAT IT INVOLVES

- Fotona Acne Control On request Laser for active acne, aimed at the inflammation and the sebaceous gland. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER

- Acne treatment On request One appointment for unsettled skin: cleansing, clearing blockages, calming. Bookable on its own. WHAT IT INVOLVES

- Acne programme € 570 A guided programme for acne: treatments at the clinic, products and check-ups at home. WHAT IT INVOLVES

**What others say about it.**

These come from Salonized and were not picked by us on content: they are the reviews that mention congestion, spots or acne.

Reviews translated from Dutch.

- “The stars at Diba are so friendly! I never let anyone but Diba treat my skin, and I'm rid of my long-term acne.” Busra Visit to Diba Clinics OVER 4 YEARS AGO

- “I felt the therapist had taken the time to remove the blemishes. And she involved me in the process of what the steps were.” Malika Visit to Diba Clinics ABOUT 6 YEARS AGO

- “Had a dermapen and carbon laser appointment yesterday. My skin already feels smooth and the spots are reducing already. Really lovely ladies too!” Jenna Microneedling ABOUT 7 YEARS AGO

**Frequently asked questions**

Why do blackheads on my nose always come back?

Because in most cases they are not blackheads but sebaceous filaments. Those belong in a working pore and fill up again within a few weeks. That is not a failure of your care; it is how a pore works.

Do pore strips work?

They pull something out, and that feels satisfying. What comes out is usually normal pore content, which returns, and tearing it off stretches the opening. So: a brief visible effect, no gain in the long run.

Is congested skin the same as acne?

No, and that distinction is not cosmetic. Congestion is about blockage without much inflammation; with acne the inflammation is the problem. The approach and the order differ.

Should I cleanse my skin more harshly?

Almost never. Treat oily skin harshly and you are left with dehydrated skin that makes more oil, and then after a month the picture is worse rather than better.

What does this cost?

That depends on the treatment that suits your skin, and we work that out at the consultation. The consultation costs 50 euros; if you have a treatment in the same appointment, that amount comes off again. You then hear straight away how many sessions it takes and what the total will be. Every price per treatment is published on the price page.

**Book a consultation at Diba Clinics**

At the skin consultation we look along under magnification. If it turns out to be largely normal pore content, you hear that, and then there is nothing to book.

### /en/skin-concerns/dark-circles

**Tabbladtitel:** Dark circles: which type do you have? | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Treating dark circles: pigment, vessels showing through or shadow. How we establish which of the three it is.

**DARK CIRCLES UNDER YOUR EYES**

Dark circles have three possible causes: pigment, vessels showing through, or shadow from a groove. Pigment we treat with peels and targeted care.

At the intake we establish which of the three it is and what fits with that.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

**What we look at**

Under the eye, light counts double: a lamp from above turns every hollow into a dark patch. So we assess it under fixed lighting.

- Colour or shadow Under fixed lighting from the front a shadow disappears and colour stays put. At home that does not work: a lamp on the ceiling turns every hollow into a dark patch.

- Pigment or vessels Under magnification you can see whether the darkness sits in the skin itself or whether you are looking through thin skin at the vessels beneath. Those two ask for different treatments.

- Recorded in images The photo is taken under the same lighting as at a following appointment. That way you see the difference side by side rather than having to estimate it afterwards.

**Three causes**

The three causes side by side, with, per type, what you see, where it comes from and what can be done about it in the clinic.

- This is pigment PERIORBITAL HYPERPIGMENTATION There is more colour in the skin under your eye. That can be hereditary, can follow eczema or rubbing, and is more common in darker skin. THIS IS WHAT WE TREAT

- These are vessels showing through VASCULAR CIRCLES The skin under your eye is the thinnest on your body. In some people the network of blood vessels beneath shines through, which gives a blue-purple tone. PARTLY TREATABLE

- This is shadow, not colour TEAR TROUGH, STRUCTURAL SHADOW The transition between your lower eyelid and your cheek sits slightly deeper, and light from above turns that into a shadow. The skin itself has no unusual colour. A DIFFERENT DISCIPLINE

Did it come out as pigment? Then the same rules apply as for pigment elsewhere on your face, including the season in which you had better not start.

**What helps and what we advise against**

Treating before it is clear which of the three it is costs most people the most money.

**THIS WORKS**

- Working out first which of the three types it is. That costs you two minutes in front of the mirror and decides whether treatment makes any sense at all.

- Sun protection right up onto the eyelid if it is pigment. That spot is almost always skipped.

- Stopping the rubbing. Rubbing and scratching are a known driver of pigment in this spot.

- Comparing your photos under the same light, because light from above makes every circle worse.

- Accepting that part of what you see belongs to your face and not to your skin.

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Booking a treatment before it is clear which type you have. With one of the three that gives nothing and with a second only half.

- Working aggressively on the thin skin under the eye. That raises the chance of more pigment there instead.

- Thinking it comes down to sleep. Sleep makes the variation worse, but it causes none of the three types.

- Taking concealer as your measure. It covers colour and changes nothing about a shadow.

- Following amounts of vitamin K or caffeine found on the internet. For this spot there is no reliable evidence for that.

**Under the eye, light counts double.**

No area is as sensitive to the position of a lamp as this one. Light from above turns every hollow into a dark patch, and then you are mostly measuring your lighting rather than your skin.

So we record this area with fixed lighting and at a fixed distance. Only then is a difference later a difference, and not a different moment of the day.

> knop: MORE ABOUT THE SKIN ANALYSIS

WHAT WE MEASURE HERE

How much pigment sits in the skin itself

*Showing through*

How strongly the vessel network beneath counts

*Shadow*

How deep the transition to the cheek lies

Every axis is measured again at each check-up, under the same lighting. That way a difference later is something you see rather than something you have to take on faith.

**What we use for this**

- Skin boosters and mesotherapy € 175 Active ingredients placed into the skin rather than onto it, at a fixed depth per injection. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE U225 INTRADERMAL INJECTOR SKIN BOOSTERS IN ROTTERDAM

- RRS Eyes € 130 Active ingredients around the eye contour. For dark circles, fine lines and a tired look. WHAT IT INVOLVES

- Eye peel € 30 A peel that is allowed on the eye contour. For fine lines and a dull, dark eye area. WHAT IT INVOLVES

**Frequently asked questions**

Does it really not come from too little sleep?

Lack of sleep causes none of the three types. It does make your face puffier and paler, which makes existing circles stand out more. So a lie-in makes them look better for a while without anything having changed.

My mother has them too. Is that a coincidence?

Probably not. Both the shape of the eye socket and the tendency towards pigment in this spot run in families. That changes nothing about what is possible, but it does explain why they were there early.

I have darker skin. Does that change anything?

Yes. Pigment under the eye is more common in darker skin, and at the same time the chance of unwanted discolouration after too strong a treatment is higher there. Working more gently is then not caution but necessity.

Does an eye cream help?

With pigment, care can help along; with shadow it does nothing. That is exactly why it pays to know which type you have first rather than buying something.

How many sessions do I need?

Usually three to six, with four to six weeks in between, and you only hear that after the measurement because it depends on the cause. With pigment we deliberately work in smaller steps under the eye, so count on more sessions than for the same spot on your cheek.

What does this cost?

That depends on the treatment that suits your skin, and we work that out at the consultation. The consultation costs 50 euros; if you have a treatment in the same appointment, that amount comes off again. You then hear straight away how many sessions it takes and what the total will be. Every price per treatment is published on the price page.

**First know which type you have.**

We look under fixed lighting at which of the three it is. If it turns out to be shadow, you hear that and it stops there. If it turns out to be pigment, you know straight away what is possible.

### /en/skin-concerns/dry-skin

**Tabbladtitel:** Dry or dehydrated skin: the difference | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Treating dry or dehydrated skin with hydrating treatments. The difference between too little oil and too little water.

**DRY OR DEHYDRATED SKIN**

Dry skin makes too little oil; dehydrated skin holds on to too little water. Those are two different things, and you can have both at once.

We treat both with hydrating treatments and a care schedule. At the intake we establish which of the two is at play in your case.

> knop: Read on

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

**Oil and water**

Oil and water are two separate axes. The skin therapist assesses both, because oily skin can be dehydrated at the same time.

*OIL*

This axis is about what your skin makes itself. That is largely predisposition and changes slowly.

*WATER*

This axis is about how much moisture sits in the top layer. That varies with the season, with your routine and with how often you wash.

**Dry and dehydrated**

IMPAIRED BARRIER FUNCTION

*HOW YOU RECOGNISE THIS*

Rough and tight, quick to redden, and you tolerate fewer products than you used to.

*WHERE IT COMES FROM*

The barrier leaks water and lacks the oil to hold it in. There is often a driver: cold weather, showering too hot, or a routine that has become too harsh.

*WHAT NEEDS TO HAPPEN THEN*

Here leaving things out gives more than adding. Making your routine smaller costs you nothing and gives the barrier room to repair.

> knop: HAVE IT MEASURED

Torn between two boxes? Look at the season. The water axis moves with the winter, the oil axis hardly at all.

**This is what we hear most often.**

All three come from the idea that oil and water sit on one scale. They do not.

- My skin shines and feels tight. Is that possible? Yes, and that is why these two axes stand apart. Oily skin can be dehydrated. Reach for a mattifying cleanser then and you make it worse.

- It is much worse in winter. Has my skin type changed? No. You are dropping on the water axis. Cold air holds less moisture and indoors the heating is on, and together those dry you out. In spring you slide back on your own.

- I have used a rich cream for years and it does not help. Then you are probably in the dehydrated quadrant and not the dry one. Rubbing oil on holds in water that is not there.

Does your skin tolerate fewer and fewer products and redden quickly? Then dry skin is often the effect and not the cause, and the story starts somewhere else.

**What helps and what we advise against**

Using more products because it is not getting better does the most damage.

**THIS WORKS**

- Knowing which quadrant you are in before you buy anything. That saves years of products solving the wrong problem.

- Shower briefly and with lukewarm water, because hot water can dry the skin further.

- Cleansing that does not leave your skin squeaky clean. Squeaky clean means oil you needed has gone too.

- When in doubt, strip back: everything gone except cleansing and one care product, for two weeks. Then you see what it really is.

- Accepting that the oil axis is largely predisposition and that the water axis can be steered.

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Stacking more actives because it is not getting better. With a leaking barrier that is the fastest route to worse.

- Scrubbing against flakes. You remove the layer that was still holding the water in.

- Trying something new every week. A skin needs weeks, so you keep measuring the previous product.

- Seeing drinking water as the solution for dehydrated skin. It helps your body; it does not top up the top layer of skin.

- Booking a treatment while your barrier is damaged. Your skin then reacts more sharply and the same treatment gives less.

**Two axes, so two measurements.**

Your skin feels different one day from the next, so a feeling is not a good starting point. That is why we measure both axes separately instead of asking whether your skin feels dry.

That also shows which axis moves as soon as you change something. Usually it is the water axis within a few weeks, and that tells you straight away where you were.

> knop: MORE ABOUT THE SKIN ANALYSIS

WHAT WE MEASURE HERE

How much the skin makes itself

*Water*

How much moisture sits in the top layer

*Leakage*

How quickly that moisture disappears again

Every axis is measured again at each check-up, under the same lighting. That way a difference later is something you see rather than something you have to take on faith.

**What we use for this**

- HydraFacial € 170 Cleansing, exfoliation and hydration. In one pass, visible straight away and with no recovery time. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE HYDRAFACIAL SYNDEO HYDRAFACIAL IN ROTTERDAM

- OxyGeneo glow € 150 Exfoliating and bringing oxygen into the skin, in one treatment. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE OXYGENEO OXYGENEO IN ROTTERDAM

- Dermaplaning € 150 Dead skin cells and fine hairs removed with a blade. Works without acids, so it suits sensitive skin too. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE DERMAPLANE PRO DERMAPLANING IN ROTTERDAM

- RRS Hyalift € 175 Bringing hyaluronic acid and vitamins into the skin. For firmness and moisture, not for volume. WHAT IT INVOLVES SKIN BOOSTERS IN ROTTERDAM

**Frequently asked questions**

So what is the difference between dry and dehydrated?

Dry is about oil and is largely predisposition. Dehydrated is about water and is a state that comes and goes. They both feel uncomfortable and ask for opposite things, and that is why people buy the wrong thing for years.

Does drinking a lot of water help?

For your body, yes; for the top layer of skin, hardly. It gets its moisture mostly from what you put on it and from how well your barrier stops leakage.

I also have red patches and itching. Does that belong with this?

It can, but with persistent itching, cracks or patches that do not go away a GP should take a look. It could be eczema, and that asks for something other than dry skin.

How soon do I notice a difference?

On the water axis often within two weeks, on the oil axis much more slowly because there you are working against your predisposition. Count on six to eight weeks before you establish anything on that second axis. That difference in pace is itself the best test of where you were.

What does this cost?

The measurement costs fifty euros and that is the whole consultation. What follows depends on what comes out of it and is listed per treatment on the price page. If the measurement shows you are in balance, our advice is to do nothing and it stops there.

**First know which box you are in.**

We measure oil and water separately, and tell you which axis moves in your case. If you are in balance, our advice is to do nothing and it stops there.

### /en/skin-concerns/dull-skin

**Tabbladtitel:** Dull skin: where does that grey tone come from | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Treating dull skin with peels, HydraFacial and microneedling. Where dullness comes from and what can be done about it.

**DULL SKIN WITHOUT SHINE**

Dull skin reflects less light back. That usually comes from a build-up of dead skin cells, from too little moisture or from a combination of the two. The skin therapist has several treatments for it: medical peels, HydraFacial, OxyGeneo, dermaplaning and microneedling.

Which of those it becomes differs per person, because no two skins are the same. At the intake the skin therapist establishes where it comes from in your case and tunes the approach to that.

> knop: Read on

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

**What we look at**

The skin therapist assesses your skin in daylight and under magnification. Dullness is light scattering rather than reflecting, and you only see that at the right angle.

- In daylight The skin therapist assesses your skin in daylight from the side. Under a lamp from above every skin looks equally flat, and then you cannot see where the light scatters.

- Under magnification Magnification shows whether there is an unbroken shine across your cheekbone or whether it stays equally matt everywhere. That distinction decides the direction.

- Measuring with the EVE-M The measurement shows whether it is about built-up cells, about a lack of moisture or about colour. The skin therapist chooses the treatment on that outcome.

**Four causes of dullness**

Two of the four causes we treat in the clinic. With the other two the gain sits in your own care, and you hear that from us.

- Built-up dead cells Your skin feels rough and looks grey, even just after washing

- Too little moisture Fine lines and a washed-out tone, especially in the morning

- Uneven colour Your skin looks patchy and therefore tired, even without separate spots

- Sleep, smoking, dehydration A grey tone that comes and goes with your weeks

*HOW YOU RECOGNISE IT YOURSELF*

Does your skin feel slightly rough under your fingertips, and does more come off on a flannel than you would expect?

*WHAT IT IS*

The top layer renews more slowly than it used to, so cells stay behind that scatter the light rather than reflect it. This is the most common cause.

*WHAT WE DO*

Getting the renewal going again, with a facial treatment or a light peel. Here the effect is visible straight away.

This sits in the top layer of your skin and can be influenced. With dullness the effect is often visible at the first treatment.

> knop: HAVE THIS LOOKED AT

Then dullness is the effect and pigment the cause.

Your eye reads an uneven tone as tired, even without a clear spot anywhere. That cannot be solved with a facial treatment; a pigment programme running over months belongs with it.

> knop: TO PIGMENTATION

**What helps and what we advise against**

With dullness the effect is often visible quickly and lasts a number of weeks. That is why this treatment is often repeated.

**THIS WORKS**

- Working out first whether it is about cells, moisture, colour or lifestyle, because that saves a whole programme

- Getting the renewal going with a peel or microneedling, at a pace your skin can handle

- Saying honestly that the effect of a facial treatment on dullness is often temporary

- Sun protection, because uneven colour is the slowest of the four to turn around

- Saying when sleep and water give more than anything we can do

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Scrubbing daily. You take the barrier away, and a damaged barrier looks duller

- Starting a long programme when a change in care or habits may be enough

- Drying out oily skin to make it less dull. It answers with more oil

- Promising the shine stays. A facial treatment gives an immediate effect and that effect fades again

- Peeling ever more strongly because the previous effect wore off

**Shine can be measured.**

That sounds odd for a complaint with no medical term, and it is exactly why it is useful here: dull is an impression, and impressions shift with your mood and the light in the room. The EVE-M records how your skin reflects light, under fixed light and from a fixed angle.

That way, after a series, it can be seen whether something has really changed or whether you were having a good week. With this concern that difference is larger than with any other.

> knop: MORE ABOUT THE SKIN ANALYSIS

WHAT WE MEASURE HERE

*Texture*

How smooth the surface is, because that is where the shine starts

*Moisture*

What the top layer holds on to

*Evenness*

How even the colour is across the whole area

Every axis is measured again at each check-up, under the same lighting. That way a difference later is something you see rather than something you have to take on faith.

**What we use for this**

- HydraFacial € 170 Cleansing, exfoliation and hydration. In one pass, visible straight away and with no recovery time. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE HYDRAFACIAL SYNDEO HYDRAFACIAL IN ROTTERDAM

- OxyGeneo glow € 150 Exfoliating and bringing oxygen into the skin, in one treatment. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE OXYGENEO OXYGENEO IN ROTTERDAM

- Dermaplaning € 150 Dead skin cells and fine hairs removed with a blade. Works without acids, so it suits sensitive skin too. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE DERMAPLANE PRO DERMAPLANING IN ROTTERDAM

- Medical peels € 140 From light to strong. The strength decides how deep it goes and how much you flake. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE PEEL LINES CHEMICAL PEEL IN ROTTERDAM

- Herbal peel € 150 A peel of finely ground herbs, without acid. It calms the inflammation and works against bacteria. WHAT IT INVOLVES

- Microneedling with the SkinPen € 180 Medically certified microneedling. It works on the layer where the structure of your skin sits. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE SKINPEN CIT MICRONEEDLING IN ROTTERDAM

- Dermapen 4 € 180 Microneedling with vibrating needles that pass through the skin evenly. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE DERMAPEN 4

- Fotona Resurfacing On request Skin renewal with laser, for pores, texture and smoother skin. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER

- Full Face Brushing € 170 A light laser pass across the whole face. Fresher skin without taking time out. WHAT IT INVOLVES

**Frequently asked questions**

Why does my skin look duller in the morning?

While you sleep you lose moisture through your skin and the blood flow runs lower. Across the morning that recovers. If it stays all day, it is not in your night but in your horny layer.

How long does the effect of a facial treatment last?

With dullness the effect is often visible straight away and usually noticeable for a number of weeks. That is not a shortcoming as long as you know it: buying shine every so many weeks is a legitimate choice. It only becomes a problem when you think you are treating a cause.

Does drinking more water help?

If you habitually drink too little, yes. Above a normal intake, no: extra water does not make your skin extra moist. What does matter is what your skin holds on to, and care does more for that than a bottle.

Is dull the same as dry?

No. Dry is about too little oil, dehydrated about too little water, and dull about how your skin reflects light. You can have oily skin that is dull. The page about dry skin works that distinction out.

What does this cost?

That depends on the treatment that suits your skin, and we work that out at the consultation. The consultation costs 50 euros; if you have a treatment in the same appointment, that amount comes off again. You then hear straight away how many sessions it takes and what the total will be. Every price per treatment is published on the price page.

**Working out which of the four is yours**

At the skin consultation we work out which of the four is yours. If it turns out to be mostly your nights, you hear that, and then there is nothing to book.

### /en/skin-concerns/eczema

**Tabbladtitel:** Eczema: a circle, not a spot | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** With eczema we work on your skin barrier, alongside the treatment from your GP. How that cycle of itching and scratching works.

**ECZEMA: ITCHING THAT KEEPS COMING BACK**

Eczema is a loop: itching leads to scratching, scratching breaks your skin barrier, and a broken barrier lets more irritants through.

We work on that barrier, with treatments and care that repair it. The medication goes through your GP, and we tune our approach to it.

> knop: Read on

> knop: LOOK AT THE CIRCLE

Itching that keeps you from sleeping, cracks, or patches that keep coming back in the same place: that is a reason to see your GP.

There is treatment for it, and that starts there. The longer the circle turns, the harder it is to break.

**The four links**

Every point in this loop keeps the next one going. We work on the barrier, because that is the link we can repair.

TURNS ON UNTIL YOU BREAK IT

> knop: ITCHING

> knop: SCRATCHING

> knop: BARRIER

> knop: IRRITANTS

Tap a link. Every point has someone who can break it, and that is far from always the same person.

*WHAT HAPPENS*

The skin sends out a signal you can hardly ignore, and it is strongest in the evening and at night.

*THIS IS WHERE THE CIRCLE CAN BREAK*

This is the point where medication matters most. An anti-inflammatory ointment at the right moment often breaks the loop in days, and your GP prescribes that.

Two of the four points lie outside our door, and that is not modesty but simply how the work divides. Anyone telling you a skin treatment solves eczema is looking at one point of a circle that keeps turning afterwards.

**Three things that look like this.**

Eczema is often used as a catch-all for everything red and flaky. These three look like it and ask for something else.

- Dehydrated skin Tight and rough, but without the itching that keeps you from sleeping and without patches that keep coming back in the same place. TO DRY SKIN

- Contact allergy The reaction sits in a defined spot with a clear shape and starts hours to days after contact with something. TO SKIN RASH

- Psoriasis Thicker, sharply bordered patches with silvery-white scales, often on elbows, knees and scalp, and usually less itchy. TO PSORIASIS

**What helps and what we advise against**

Putting off your GP because you want to try something yourself first usually costs the most time.

**THIS WORKS**

- To your GP with persistent itching, cracks or patches that come back. This is a condition with a treatment, and that starts there.

- Keep moisturising daily, including on the days when there is nothing to see. With eczema that is the basis and not a side issue.

- Shower lukewarm and briefly, and moisturise within a few minutes afterwards.

- Keeping your nails short and something between your nails and your skin at night. Most scratching happens in your sleep.

- Keeping track of when it flares. Triggers are personal and you only see a pattern afterwards.

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Putting off your GP because you want to try a cream first. The longer the circle turns, the harder it is to break.

- Stopping a prescribed ointment as soon as it improves, without discussing it with your doctor.

- Using soap and hot water on a spot that is already broken.

- Cutting foods out on suspicion of allergy. That costs you nutrients and rarely gives an answer.

- Booking a cosmetic treatment on active eczema. It makes it worse, so we do not do it.

**Frequently asked questions**

Can I come to you with eczema?

Not for the eczema itself, that goes to your GP. Sometimes for the skin around it, if it is calm and you want to tackle something else. We then look at whether it is sensible and say so when it is not.

Does eczema ever go away?

In children it often largely disappears. In adults it usually runs in periods, with quiet times and flare-ups. That does not mean nothing can be done, only that it is managed.

Is it contagious?

No. Eczema cannot be passed on.

Why is it worse at night?

During the day you are distracted and in the evening you are not, and the skin is warmer then too. On top of that you scratch in your sleep without noticing.

Does sunlight help?

In some people yes and in others no, and burning always makes it worse. Light therapy exists as a treatment but it belongs with a dermatologist and not with a skin clinic.

**Together with your GP**

The diagnosis and the medication go through your GP. Alongside that we work on your skin barrier, with treatments and care that repair it. If your skin is calm at that moment, we can start.

**Book a consultation at Diba Clinics**

The diagnosis and the medication go through your GP. What your skin needs alongside that, we look at: which care repairs the barrier and which treatment is possible once your skin is calm. If that is nothing at that moment, we say so.
