### /en/skin-concerns/eye-bags

**Tabbladtitel:** Under-eye bags: fluid, fat or shadow | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Bags under your eyes: where they come from and what a skin treatment can add with fluid or thin skin.

**BAGS UNDER YOUR EYES**

Bags come from fluid, a fat pad or shadow from a groove. With fluid and with thin skin around the eyes we can do something, with targeted care and treatments that make the skin firmer.

At the intake we establish where it comes from in your case.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

**What we look at**

The skin therapist looks at how the skin under your eye sits, at how it runs across the day and at how thick the skin is there.

- How it runs across the day Fluid drains away across the day; a fat pad and a groove stay the same. That is where the assessment starts.

- The thickness of the skin Under your eye the skin is the thinnest on your body. Exactly how thin decides what a treatment can add.

- How the bone beneath sits If the eye socket sits deeper, a shadow falls. That looks like a bag and asks for something other than fluid.

**What sits under your eyes**

Bags come from fluid, a fat pad or shadow from a groove. Which of the three it is decides what a skin treatment can add. And sometimes it is not a bag but a yellow patch on the eyelid.

- Moisture Puffy in the morning, less so across the day

- Slipped fat A bulge that is always there, the same morning and evening

- Shadow, not swelling A groove or hollow under your eye that looks dark

- Yellow patches on the eyelid Soft, yellowish bumps on or around your eyelids that do not go away

*HOW YOU RECOGNISE IT YOURSELF*

Is it worst on getting up and a good deal less by midday? And does it differ from night to night, after salty food or a glass too many?

*WHAT IT IS*

Fluid that gathers overnight in the loose tissue under your eyes and drains away during the day. This is the only one of the three that changes from day to day.

*WHAT WE DO*

Here there is something to do. Stimulate drainage, make the skin firmer, and look at what in your routine or your nights plays a part. If there is brown colour under the eye as well, a pigment bag, the eye peel belongs with it, often together with RRS Eyes.

Of the three causes this is the only one a skin treatment can influence, and the only one that changes from day to day.

> knop: HAVE THIS LOOKED AT

Then you are not looking for a bag but a circle.

A bag is volume: there is something there. A dark circle is colour: pigment or vessels showing through. They often occur together and ask for different things.

> knop: TO DARK CIRCLES

**What helps and what we advise against**

The skin under your eye is the thinnest on your body. That decides both what is possible and how carefully we work.

**THIS WORKS**

- Establishing first whether it is fluid, fat or shadow, because two of those we do not solve here

- With fluid: stimulating drainage and firming the skin around the eye, in a series

- With a pigment bag, a brown colour under the eye: the eye peel, often together with RRS Eyes

- Sun protection around the eyes, because thinner skin shows everything beneath it more clearly

- Weighing what else is going on: sleep, salt, alcohol, allergy

- Referring you to a doctor when the answer lies there, even when you were already sitting here

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Fillers under the eye. We do not do that, and with a real bag it is rarely the solution either

- Aggressive treatments on the thinnest skin of your face

- Recommending a cream for a fat pad. A cream cannot move a slipped fat pad under the eye.

- Promising it will go when it does not change from day to day

**What we use for this**

- RRS Eyes € 130 Active ingredients around the eye contour. For dark circles, fine lines and a tired look. WHAT IT INVOLVES SKIN BOOSTERS IN ROTTERDAM

- SmoothEye € 150 Laser around the eye contour, for crow's feet and fine lines. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER

- Eye peel € 30 A peel that is allowed on the eye contour. For fine lines and a dull, dark eye area. WHAT IT INVOLVES

**Frequently asked questions**

What is the difference between bags and dark circles?

A bag is volume: there is something there, whether fluid or fat. A dark circle is colour: pigment or vessels showing through thin skin. They often occur together and ask for different things. If it is mostly colour for you, read on at the page about dark circles.

Does sleeping better help?

With fluid it makes a difference, as do less salt and less alcohol before bed. With fat or shadow nothing changes, however well you sleep. That is exactly why we want to know first what you have.

Can I do something about it myself?

Sleeping with your head slightly raised and cooling in the morning helps against fluid, temporarily. Rubbing your eyes is the one thing you really must stop: the skin there is the thinnest on your body and stretches easily.

**Book a consultation at Diba Clinics**

At the skin consultation we establish whether it is fluid, fat or shadow. With two of the three our advice is to start somewhere else, and you hear that straight away.

### /en/skin-concerns/ingrown-hairs

**Tabbladtitel:** Treating ingrown hairs in Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Treating ingrown hairs with laser hair removal. If there is a hair in the bump, hair removal tackles it at the root.

**INGROWN HAIRS AFTER SHAVING OR WAXING**

Bumps on your neck, bikini line or legs look alike and are not. If there is a hair in it, hair removal is the logical route: where no hair grows, nothing can grow in. If there is no hair in it, hair removal changes nothing.

If it keeps coming back, laser hair removal is the solution that tackles it at the root. Sometimes a different shaving technique is already enough, and then you hear that from us too.

> knop: Read on

> knop: WHAT EXACTLY YOU SEE

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

**What we look at**

The skin therapist looks under magnification at whether there is a hair in the bump. That distinction decides whether hair removal makes sense or not.

- Under magnification The skin therapist uses magnification to see whether there is a hair in the bump. That distinction decides whether hair removal makes sense or whether it is something else.

- The loop or the tip If there is a dark loop or tip under the skin, it is ingrowth. If none of that is visible, we look further at what it is instead.

- Across a larger area Then we assess the whole area. Is it in one spot or across a larger area, because that decides whether you have an area treated or a single spot.

**Four kinds of bump after shaving**

Neck, bikini line, legs and jawline are the areas where these four occur. Two of them benefit from hair removal and two do not.

- A hair that does not come out A bump with a dark curl in it that you cannot get out

- Red, warm and with a pus head Painful red bumps with a yellow head, shortly after shaving

- Rough bumps without a hair Goose bumps that do not go away, on your upper arms or thighs

- Dark marks without a bump Brown dots where the bumps used to be

*HOW YOU RECOGNISE IT YOURSELF*

In good light, do you see a dark loop or tip under the skin, and is the bump in a place you shave or epilate?

*WHAT IT IS*

The hair curls back into the skin instead of out of it, and your immune system reacts to something that belongs there. It happens more often and more fiercely with curly hair.

*WHAT WE DO*

This is the picture where hair removal with light gives the most: no hair, no ingrowth. First we look at whether your skin type and hair colour are suitable for it.

A hair is involved, and that is what light aims at. Count on a series rather than one session.

> knop: HAVE THIS LOOKED AT

Then it starts with the treatment and not with the concern.

If it is not the bumps you care about but the hair removal itself, the areas, the rates and what is possible per skin type are on the laser hair removal page.

> knop: TO LASER HAIR REMOVAL

**What helps and what we advise against**

Shaving close, tweezing and scrubbing keep the problem going. Stopping them often gives more than adding anything.

**THIS WORKS**

- Looking first at whether there really is a hair in it, because without a hair, hair removal does nothing

- Switching off the hair root, because a hair that is not there cannot grow in

- Looking at how you remove hair now. Sometimes shaving differently is the whole solution, and then we say so

- Adjusting the settings to your skin type, because with darker skin that has to be more precise

- Sun protection on the treated area, otherwise the dark marks stay put

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Lasering an area that is inflamed at that moment

- Picking them out yourself with tweezers or a needle. That is the fastest route to a dark mark or a dent

- Scrubbing against ingrown hairs. On an irritated area it makes the inflammation worse

- Treating tanned skin

- Promising every hair will go. Light and grey hairs barely respond to light

**What we use for this**

- Electrolysis € 60 Hair by hair, grey and blond included. For what the laser cannot see. We charge the treatment time per half hour. WHAT IT INVOLVES ELECTROLYSIS IN ROTTERDAM

- Laser hair removal € 20 Switching off the hair root. Per area or as a package, for women and men. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE GENTLEMAX PRO

**What others say about it.**

These come from Salonized and were not picked by us on content. They are about laser hair removal, because that is what stops ingrowth.

Reviews translated from Dutch.

- “I had a really lovely experience with Demi. Well informed about how the process (lasering) works. I was put at ease and helped well. You've got a new client!” Andrijana Laser hair removal with Demi 4 MONTHS AGO

- “I've been by 3 times now for the diode laser and I genuinely see an 80% difference! The scars and spots on my skin have hugely improved too thanks to the dermapen. A forever regular anyway!!” Sara Laser hair removal OVER 7 YEARS AGO

- “I thought the appointment was great! Everything went well and I'm nearly finished with the lasering! Demi is genuinely a very professional skin specialist, so grateful for her! She does her work very precisely.” Monique Laser hair removal OVER 3 YEARS AGO

**Frequently asked questions**

Do ingrown hairs go away with laser hair removal?

In the majority they do, and for a logical reason: where no hair grows, nothing can grow in. It goes gradually, over a series of sessions, and it only works if the hair is dark enough to catch light.

Why do I get them mostly on my neck and bikini line?

There the hair more often grows curly and the follicle lies at more of an angle, so a regrowing hair goes back into the skin sooner. Clothing that rubs and shaving close make it worse.

Can I keep shaving during the programme?

Shaving is allowed and in fact required: the area should be short on the day of the treatment. What is not allowed is plucking, waxing or an epilator, because that pulls out precisely the root the light aims at.

And those dark marks that are left?

That is pigment and not a scar. As long as new bumps keep appearing, treating makes little sense, because new marks appear too. Cause first, colour after.

### /en/skin-concerns/keloids

**Tabbladtitel:** Keloids and raised scars in Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** The difference between a keloid and a raised scar, what we treat and what goes through your doctor.

**KELOID AND THICKENED SCARS**

A thickened scar that stays within the edges of the wound we treat with microneedling and laser. That makes it flatter and less red.

If it grows beyond the edge of the wound it is a keloid and the treatment goes through your doctor. We assess alongside and coordinate, because too strong a stimulus makes a keloid larger.

> knop: Read on

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

**What we look at**

You tell a keloid from a thickened scar by three things. Those also decide who does the treatment.

- Whether it grows beyond the edge of the wound A hypertrophic scar stays within the original wound. A keloid grows beyond it, into the healthy skin.

- How old it is and what it does A hypertrophic scar often flattens after months to a year. A keloid stays or keeps growing, and that difference counts.

- Where it sits and whether it itches The breastbone, shoulders and earlobes are where keloid forms most often. Itching and pain come with it and say something about how active it is.

**Inside or over the edge**

They look alike and ask for different routes. The difference lies in whether the tissue stays within the original wound.

- RAISED AND RED, BUT NO LARGER THAN THE SCAR ITSELF Thickened scar within the wound edge HYPERTROPHIC SCAR Collagen production overshot during healing, but the tissue stays within the borders of the original wound. This we do treat, with microneedling and laser that make the tissue more even. Often in consultation with your doctor. Flatter and less red is achievable. How much and in how many appointments, you hear after the assessment.

- KEEPS GROWING BEYOND THE ORIGINAL WOUND A scar that grows over the edge KELOID The tissue grows over the edges of the wound, into the healthy skin. Keloid is more common in darker skin; that is tied to predisposition. Here the treatment goes through your doctor or dermatologist. We assess alongside and coordinate, because too strong a stimulus makes a keloid larger. With a referral we look at what is possible alongside the medical treatment.

**What helps and what we advise against**

With keloid the predisposition counts for more than the care. What you do hold in your hands is how early someone looks at it.

**THIS WORKS**

- Protecting a new scar from sun and tension, certainly in the first year

- If you are prone to keloid, mentioning it before any procedure, a piercing included

- Having it assessed as soon as it stays raised or starts to grow

- Mentioning itching and pain, because they say something about how active the tissue is

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Scratching, squeezing or pulling a plaster tight over it yourself

- Having a keloid treated without a doctor having looked at it

- Waiting for it to pass on its own. A keloid usually does not

- A new piercing or tattoo in a place where keloid formed before

**What we use for this**

- Scar therapy € 100 For scars after surgery or a caesarean. The price follows the length of the scar. WHAT IT INVOLVES

**Frequently asked questions**

What is the difference from an ordinary thick scar?

A hypertrophic scar stays within the original wound and often flattens over time. A keloid grows beyond it and stays.

Do you treat keloid?

The treatment of a keloid goes through your doctor or dermatologist. We assess alongside and coordinate on what is possible in addition, because too strong a stimulus makes a keloid larger.

Why do I get them and others do not?

Predisposition plays the largest part, and keloid is more common in darker skin. It says nothing about how you cared for a wound.

Can I still get a piercing or a tattoo?

In a place where keloid formed before, that is inadvisable. Discuss it with your doctor before having anything done.

Does it come back after treatment?

With keloid that chance is real, and that is exactly why it belongs with a doctor. What the chance is in your case, you hear there.

**Book a consultation at Diba Clinics**

The therapist establishes whether it is a thickened scar or a keloid, and what fits with that in your case. With a keloid we consult your doctor.

### /en/skin-concerns/keratosis-pilaris

**Tabbladtitel:** Treating keratosis pilaris | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Treating keratosis pilaris with peels and targeted care that dissolves the build-up of keratin around the follicle.

**ROUGH BUMPS ON YOUR UPPER ARMS**

Keratosis pilaris is a harmless and often hereditary skin condition. The bumps can lessen over the years, but they do not disappear on their own in everyone.

We treat it with peels and targeted care that dissolve the build-up of keratin. Scrubbing does not work here: the plugs sit around the hair follicle and not at the surface.

> knop: Read on

> knop: WHAT WE LOOK AT IN THE CONSULTATION

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

**What the skin therapist looks at**

Keratin build-up and dry skin look alike and ask for different treatments. These are the three things the skin therapist tells them apart by.

- How the bumps feel Keratin build-up feels like fine sandpaper and sits fixed in the pore. Dryness feels rough, but rubs away.

- Whether it is on both sides Keratosis pilaris is almost always symmetrical. If it is on one side or on shaved areas, it is something else.

- How it runs across the year Clearer in winter and calmer in summer fits keratin build-up. With dryness it virtually disappears in summer.

**Four pictures that feel rough**

Keratin build-up, dryness and ingrown hairs feel almost the same under your hand. Where it sits and whether it is symmetrical makes the difference.

- Rough bumps on your upper arms Goose bumps that do not go away, not even when you are warm

- Red cheeks with small bumps A lasting red flush on the cheeks, often since childhood

- Rough from dryness Chapped, rough skin that is worse in winter and gone in summer

- Bumps with a hair in them Bumps in places you shave, sometimes with a dark curl in them

*HOW YOU RECOGNISE IT YOURSELF*

Does a large area feel like sandpaper, are the bumps close together, and is it roughly the same on both arms?

*WHAT IT IS*

Keratin build-up around the hair follicles: a plug of horny cells forms above each hair. Harmless, largely hereditary, and in many people it lessens over the years.

*WHAT WE DO*

Gradually making the top layer suppler and the plugs looser, at a pace your skin can handle. Maintenance belongs with it; this is not a course with an end point.

Keratin build-up around the hair follicles. Not curable, but it can be made suppler and less red, with the maintenance that belongs to it.

> knop: HAVE THIS LOOKED AT

Then this is not your page.

Bumps in shaved areas with a dark curl beneath are ingrown hairs. That is a different indication and a different treatment.

> knop: TO INGROWN HAIRS

**What helps and what we advise against**

This is a condition that comes with maintenance. With a series of treatments and the right care you keep it calm.

**THIS WORKS**

- Saying honestly that this cannot be cured, and what can be done instead

- Making the top layer suppler gradually, at a pace the skin can handle

- Maintenance you can keep up yourself, because without it the picture returns

- Tackling the redness separately, because it often bothers people more than the bumps themselves

- Taking into account that it is worse in winter; that is not a relapse but the season

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Scrubbing. The plugs sit around the hair follicle and not at the surface; you only make the redness worse

- Squeezing or picking. That leaves you with dark marks and sometimes dents

- Presenting a course of treatment as a definitive solution. Keratosis pilaris usually asks for lasting care and maintenance.

- Promising that the skin becomes smooth. Suppler and less red is realistic

- Treating it as acne. There is no inflammation and no bacterium in it

**Frequently asked questions**

Does goose-bump skin ever go away?

A cure is not possible, but in many people it lessens on its own over the years, often from around thirty. In the meantime the picture can be softened. That is not a pretty story, and it is the honest one.

Why does scrubbing not work?

Because the keratin build-up sits around the hair follicle and not at the surface. So you scrub over the bumps rather than into them. What you do achieve is more redness and a damaged barrier.

Does it come from something I am doing?

No. It is largely hereditary and it has nothing to do with hygiene, food or how you care for your skin.

Why is it worse in winter?

Cold air and indoor heating dry the skin out, and drier skin makes the keratin build-up more visible and rougher. In almost everyone it is less in summer. That is the season and not a relapse.

What does this cost?

That depends on the treatment that suits your skin, and we work that out at the consultation. The consultation costs 50 euros; if you have a treatment in the same appointment, that amount comes off again. You then hear straight away how many sessions it takes and what the total will be. Every price per treatment is published on the price page.

**What we establish first**

For most people the most useful outcome is that it has a name, is harmless and is not their fault. What can be softened besides that, we discuss in the same conversation.

### /en/skin-concerns/melasma

**Tabbladtitel:** Treating melasma in Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Treating melasma with peels, care and sun protection. How deep the pigment sits decides what is possible, and we see that start under a UV scan.

**MELASMA TREATED**

We treat melasma with peels, targeted care and sun protection. How deep the pigment sits decides what is possible, and in ordinary light you cannot see that.

So we look under UV light first. If the pigment sits deep, we aim at control: fewer flare-ups and a calmer picture.

> knop: Read on

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

**How you recognise it**

They look alike and ask for different approaches. The difference is in the pattern, the place and how the mark behaves across the year.

- THE PATTERN Areas with soft edges, usually the same amount on the left and the right.

- THE PLACE Cheeks, forehead, above the lip and along the jawline.

- THE COURSE Gets darker in summer and lighter in winter.

- WHAT DRIVES IT Hormones, sun and heat together. It often starts during a pregnancy.

- THE PATTERN Separate spots with a sharp edge, scattered at random.

- THE PLACE Where the sun has been falling for years: face, hands, décolleté.

- THE COURSE It stays as it is, and new ones slowly appear.

- WHAT DRIVES IT Hours of sun added up over the years, without a hormonal side.

- Behind glass too UVA passes through a car window and through the glass at home. Indoors and on a grey day, pigmentation simply carries on.

- Heat counts as well It is not only about UV. A hot kitchen, a sauna or a hairdryer close to your face stirs melasma up just as well.

- The depth sets the pace Pigment high in the skin lightens faster. If it sits deeper, it takes more sessions and more patience.

**Three things that steer melasma**

A sun spot is there and stays there. Melasma opens and closes, and three things decide how far it is open. Look at the third column: that is the part you hold in your own hands.

- Sun The strongest of the three, and the only one you fully hold in your own hands. Winter light and light through a car window count too. IN YOUR HANDS Fully

- Hormones Pregnancy, the pill and hormonal coils play a part. This is why melasma is more common in women and sometimes fades on its own after a birth. IN YOUR HANDS Hardly at all

- Heat Sauna, hot showers, a warm kitchen, and the heat of a treatment itself. This is the driver that gets overlooked most often. IN YOUR HANDS Partly

With melasma, protection is not advice alongside the treatment but part of the treatment itself. Without it the rest does not work, and that is why we keep going on about it here.

**What helps and what we advise against**

With melasma the first cross on the right is the most expensive mistake there is, and it is made by clinics rather than by clients.

**THIS WORKS**

- Protecting every day, all year round. With melasma this is not advice but the treatment itself; without it the rest does not work.

- Treating gently and building up slowly. Melasma is the only condition on this site where working harder takes you further from where you want to be.

- Looking first at how deep it sits. That decides whether treatment makes sense, and it takes one appointment.

- Avoiding heat around a treatment, including sauna and hot showers.

- Accepting that this is managed rather than cured. Anyone who knows that beforehand is not disappointed afterwards.

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- An aggressive laser or a strong peel. With melasma that is the best-known way to make it worse than it was.

- Starting in summer. You would be working against the very driver you are trying to switch off.

- Stopping the protection as soon as it lightens. It is then back within a season and you have paid for nothing.

- Treating melasma as though it were ordinary pigmentation. The same approach gives a different and worse result here.

- Ordering whitening agents yourself that you cannot get here without a prescription. There is a reason they are restricted.

**Measuring here is about depth.**

With ordinary pigmentation we measure how dark and how large. With melasma the first question is how deep it sits, because that decides whether the rest of the measurement still matters.

We also record what your drivers are. Melasma that lightens while the tap is open is a result that does not last, and you want to know that beforehand.

> knop: MORE ABOUT THE SKIN ANALYSIS

WHAT WE MEASURE HERE

*Depth*

High, mixed or deep in the skin

*Intensity*

How strongly it stands out against the skin around it

*Spread*

Which areas are involved and how large they are

Every axis is measured again at each check-up, under the same lighting. That way a difference later is something you see rather than something you have to take on faith.

**What we use for this**

- Skin boosters and mesotherapy € 175 Active ingredients placed into the skin rather than onto it, at a fixed depth per injection. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE U225 INTRADERMAL INJECTOR SKIN BOOSTERS IN ROTTERDAM

- Dermamelan € 920 The more intensive approach to pigmentation, usually for melasma. Six months, with a strict routine at home. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE PEEL LINES COSMELAN AND DERMAMELAN IN ROTTERDAM

**Frequently asked questions**

Does melasma ever go away completely?

Usually not on its own, and treatment lightens it without removing it. After a pregnancy it sometimes largely fades; that is the hormonal part falling away rather than something a treatment did.

Why is this different from ordinary pigmentation?

A sun spot is there and stays there. Melasma has a tap that opens and closes, and that tap is partly beyond your control. So the same treatment gives a different result.

I am pregnant. Can I do anything now?

Protect, yes; treat, no. We wait until after the pregnancy and breastfeeding, partly because some of it fades on its own by then.

I have darker skin. Does that change anything?

Yes, in two directions. Melasma is more common, and the chance that too strong a treatment leaves more pigment behind is higher. Working more gently is then not caution but necessity.

How long before I see something?

You usually see the first change after two to three months. So count on months rather than weeks, and on maintenance after that. That last part is not a side issue but most of the work.

What does this cost?

The measurement costs fifty euros; the programmes after that are on the price page with their rates. If the measurement shows that the pigment sits deep, we advise against treatment and it stops there.

**Book a consultation at Diba Clinics**

We estimate the depth and record your drivers. If it sits deep, you hear that and we advise against treatment. If it sits high, you know straight away what there is to gain and what it takes.

### /en/skin-concerns/milia

**Tabbladtitel:** Removing milia and styes | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Having milia and styes removed. A hard white bump is gone in seconds; red and painful belongs with your GP.

**MILIA AND WHITE BUMPS**

In everyday speech and in the consulting room, a stye means two different things. What people usually mean is a milium: a hard white bead that sits there for months, does not hurt and cannot be squeezed out. That is gone in seconds.

A milium we remove with a fine needle, in a few seconds per bead. If it is red, warm and painful, it is an inflammation; come by then, because the approach is a different one.

> knop: Read on

> knop: SEE WHICH ONE YOU HAVE

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

**How we remove milia**

A fine needle opens the bead and the contents come out. Per milium that takes a few seconds, and no wound is left.

- Looking first, with magnification The skin therapist looks at each bead up close. If something among them is not a milium, you hear that straight away and not halfway through.

- One prick per bead The skin above it is opened with a sterile needle and the contents lifted out. A few seconds per bead, and you feel a prick like having a splinter taken out.

- Done, and you can go There is no anaesthetic, no plaster and no recovery time. Sometimes a red dot is visible for a few hours, and after that nothing.

Then this is only half your story.

Separate white beads are a thing on their own. If you also see blocked pores, spots or a shiny T-zone, it is congestion and the acne page is the better way in.

> knop: TO THE ACNE PAGE

**White bead or inflamed gland?**

White and hard on one side, red and painful on the other: that difference decides whether it can go here or goes to your GP.

- A hard white bead A white grain under your eye or on your cheek that has been there for months

- A red, painful bump on the eyelid edge A painful red swelling on the edge of your eyelid

- A firm lump in the eyelid A firm bump in your eyelid that stays for weeks

- A black or dark dot A small dark dot in a pore

*HOW YOU RECOGNISE IT YOURSELF*

Is it white or yellowish-white, not red, does it not hurt, and can you not squeeze anything out of it?

*WHAT IT IS*

A tiny cyst of keratin, enclosed under the epidermis. There is no opening to it, which is why squeezing does not work.

*WHAT WE DO*

Opening it with a sterile needle and lifting the contents out. That takes a few seconds per bead and nothing is left to see.

A sterile needle, a few seconds per bead, and nothing is left to see. Almost always a one-off treatment.

> knop: HAVE THIS LOOKED AT

**What helps and what we advise against**

With milia the answer is usually short: if it is the right bump, it is done in one appointment.

**THIS WORKS**

- Establishing first whether it is a white grain or an inflammation, because that decides between your GP and us

- Opening milia with a sterile needle, one by one, in a treatment of minutes

- Looking for a trigger: an eye cream that is too rich, sun damage, or something that damaged the skin

- Referring to your GP with anything that is red, painful or warm

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Pricking something that is inflamed. Around the eye that is a risk with no need for it

- Squeezing it yourself. There is no opening in it, so you only damage the skin around it

- Recommending a cream as removal. A cream does not open an enclosed milium.

- Scheduling several appointments unnecessarily. Removing a milium is usually a one-off treatment.

**Frequently asked questions**

Why can I not squeeze a milium out?

Because there is no opening to it. A blackhead has a pore channel to the outside; a milium is completely enclosed under a layer of skin. So squeezing only damages the tissue around it.

Does having them removed hurt?

You feel a prick per bead, comparable to having a splinter taken out. No anaesthetic is needed and you can simply leave afterwards.

Do they come back?

The treated beads do not. New ones can form, and then we look for a trigger: in some people that is an eye cream that is too rich, in others years of sun damage.

How many can be done at once?

Usually everything that is there, in one appointment. If there are many, we sometimes spread it out to give the skin rest. You hear that beforehand and not halfway through.

What does this cost?

That depends on the treatment that suits your skin, and we work that out at the consultation. The consultation costs 50 euros; if you have a treatment in the same appointment, that amount comes off again. You then hear straight away how many sessions it takes and what the total will be. Every price per treatment is published on the price page.

**Just let us look. It is often done in no time.**

With milia the appointment is short and one-off. If it turns out to be something else, you hear that straight away and we refer you on rather than trying it.

### /en/skin-concerns/moles

**Tabbladtitel:** Having moles removed | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** A mole that bothers you can go. What happens first, what we look out for and why a spot that is changing goes past a doctor first.

**MOLES REMOVED**

If it gets in the way when shaving, catches on your collar or you simply find it ugly: we will look at it. Our skin therapist assesses the spot, and after a referral from your doctor we coagulate it where that is possible.

The referral is not a formality: only a doctor can have tissue examined, and that cannot be done afterwards. With that referral in hand we do the rest.

> knop: Read on

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

> knop: THE ABCDE CHECK FIRST

We assess the spot and coagulate it after a referral from your doctor.

Coagulating is removal with heat, in a brief procedure per spot. Getting the referral costs you an appointment with your GP; after that you can come to us.

**Six things to look at.**

Five letters dermatologists use, plus a sixth that most sites leave out. Go through it before you make an appointment. It gives no verdict and can rule nothing out; it helps you decide whether a doctor should look first.

- A: ASYMMETRY Fold the spot in half in your mind. Do the two halves match? The halves look alike One half is clearly different from the other A quiet mole grows evenly from one point and is therefore usually roughly symmetrical.

- B: BORDER Look at the edge. Is it smooth and clear, or ragged and vague? A smooth, clear edge Ragged, angular or running out into the skin The transition to ordinary skin says something about how the spot behaves at its edges.

- C: COLOUR Does the spot have one colour, or several shades mixed together? Roughly the same colour throughout Several shades, or black, red or white in it Different colours within one spot are one of the best-known reasons to have it checked.

- D: DIAMETER Is the spot larger than a pencil eraser, about six millimetres? Smaller than about six millimetres Larger than about six millimetres Size on its own says little. It mostly counts alongside the other points, and a small spot that changes matters more than a large spot that has been the same for years.

- E: EVOLVING Has anything changed in shape, colour, size or feel in recent months? Think of itching, bleeding or a scab that does not go away. Nothing changed as far as I know Yes, something has changed This is the most important point of the five. Change counts for more than how the spot looks, even when the other four show you nothing unusual.

- THE UGLY DUCKLING Put this spot next to your other moles. Does it look like the rest, or does it stand out? It looks like my other spots It clearly differs from the rest One person's moles usually look alike. So one that clearly stands out is worth checking, even if on its own it seems nothing special.

Go through the points above. Whatever you fill in, the outcome of this check is never a verdict on your spot: it only helps you decide whether to take it to your GP.

This check is information and not a medical examination. It cannot see what a doctor sees with a dermatoscope, so it can rule nothing out. When in doubt the advice is always the same: have it checked.

**What helps and what we advise against**

The first cross on the right is the only one on this site that is not about money: having something removed that is changing means there is nothing left to examine.

**THIS WORKS**

- Looking yourself once a month, preferably at the same moment. It is about change, and you only see that if you have a picture in your head.

- Taking photos of spots you are watching, up close and with something beside them for scale.

- Looking where you do not look automatically: your back, your scalp, between your toes and under your nails.

- When in doubt, to your GP. That is what the surgery is for.

- Taking sun protection seriously, because this is the subject that is not about your looks.

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Having something removed that is changing, anywhere. What is gone cannot be examined. That is the one step you cannot make up for later.

- Burning or freezing it off yourself with something from a shop. The same objection, with more damage.

- Waiting until it hurts. Most suspicious spots do not hurt at all.

- Going by a photo app or a verdict from the internet. A screen sees no depth and no change.

- Thinking it is only about your face. Spots on the back, legs and soles of the feet are the most often overlooked.

**Before we remove anything**

On the other pages this is where the things we do not do are listed. Here are the three steps that come before a treatment, and the first is the only one on this site you cannot make up for later.

- We assess the spot Our skin therapist looks at shape, colour, border and whether anything about it is changing. You hear straight away what we see and what the next step is.

- Coagulating happens after a referral from your doctor With a referral in hand we remove the spot with heat, in a brief procedure. That order is fixed: only a doctor can have tissue examined, and that cannot be done afterwards.

- We cover moles up If we laser nearby, a cover goes over it. Light on pigment can change the picture, and then a later assessment no longer holds.

**What we use for this**

- Fibroma removal € 30 Removing skin tags, usually in one appointment. We charge the treatment time per quarter of an hour. WHAT IT INVOLVES

**Frequently asked questions**

Then why is this page here at all?

Because people ask us this during a treatment, and because you lie in our chair with your skin in full view. We want you to know what to watch for and where to go, even when it is not us.

Can I have a mole removed at your clinic?

No. Not with a suspicious spot and not with one you simply want gone. That goes to your GP, who can do it or refer you on.

I have a treatment booked and there is a mole in the area.

Then we cover it. That takes half a minute and it means a doctor can still assess later what is there.

Do I get new moles from sunbathing?

Sunlight plays a part in new spots forming and in the risk of skin cancer. Exactly how large that part is differs per person and is not something we put a number on.

How often should I check myself?

Once a month is common advice and mostly practical: often enough to notice change, rare enough to keep up. Ask your GP what is sensible in your case.

**It starts with looking**

If you come for something else and there is a mole in the area, we cover it and carry on. If you come for the mole itself, it starts with looking.

> knop: I AM LOOKING FOR PIGMENTATION

- IS IT CHANGING? Then your GP first. They can have tissue examined and we cannot.

- IS IT NOT CHANGING? Then we look at it together and you hear what is possible and what it costs.

- REMOVAL A brief procedure per spot. Then a scab that comes off on its own.

**Tabbladtitel:** Treating pigment spots in Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Treating pigment spots with laser, IPL and peels. Which approach fits depends on the type of spot, your skin type and the season.

**PIGMENTATION TREATED**

We treat pigmentation with laser, IPL and peels. Which approach fits depends on the type of spot and on your skin type. We work that out together at the consultation.

The season counts. With little sun the result holds better, so autumn and winter are the best time.

> knop: LOOK AT THE SUN YEAR

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

**The year decides whether it will work.**

The height of each bar is the average UV index in the Netherlands. Click a month and you see what happens to pigmentation then, and whether we would advise you to start. This month is already open.

> knop: JAN

**September**

The UV drops. This is the month in which pigmentation shows its darkest state.

From now on it gets interesting. Measuring in September gives the most honest starting point of the year.

> knop: BOOK YOUR SKIN CONSULTATION

These are monthly averages. On a clear summer day the strength of the sun in the Netherlands is a good deal higher than what you see here, and that is the moment pigmentation forms.

**Three kinds of pigmentation**

Sun damage and melasma look alike but ask for different treatment. We establish which type you have before we start. Pick the pattern that comes closest to yours.

- Separate spots with clear edges Brown spots with a clear edge, mostly where the sun reaches

- Symmetrical, hazy patches Larger cloud-like areas, often the same on both sides

- A dark mark after a spot or a wound The mark that stays behind once something has healed

*THE PATTERN*

On the parts that stick out: cheekbone, bridge of the nose, forehead, back of the hand and décolleté. Not symmetrical; each spot has its own shape.

*WHERE IT COMES FROM*

UV exposure added up over years. Each spot is a place where pigment cells have been thrown off.

*WHAT WE DO FIRST*

We establish the type, treat it specifically and then keep it in check with sun protection. Without that last part it comes back.

This is often where the most can be gained. This type usually responds well and comes back less quickly than melasma, as long as you keep the sun off it.

> knop: HAVE THIS PATTERN LOOKED AT

**Why pigmentation comes back**

Pigment cells that have once been thrown off respond to sunlight faster the next time. So every unprotected summer adds to the one before it.

With pigmentation, daily sun protection and limiting new exposure matter at least as much as the treatment at the clinic.

> knop: Read on

- Without protection Every summer lays a layer on the one before. What you gain in winter you lose in July.

- With protection The pigmentation that is there can lighten, and little new appears.

- With protection and treatment This is where the most is to be gained. Do start with the protection, because without it the result does not hold.

**What helps and what we advise against**

With pigmentation it usually goes wrong by starting too early, not by treating too little.

**THIS WORKS**

- Sun protection every day, on a grey day too. With pigmentation that is the most important part

- Starting in autumn, so that you have months of low UV ahead of you

- Measuring per season, because pigmentation moves with the year

- Establishing before the first treatment which type it is and how deep it sits: in the epidermis, in the dermis or in both

- A cap or a hat. It keeps off more sun than any cream does

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Starting in May or June. You then treat against the sun for four months and that costs you the result

- Going in hard with melasma. That stirs it up rather than removing it

- Whitening creams from the internet. They regularly contain hydroquinone or mercury, outside any supervision

- A sunbed, not even to cover it up. You make the pigmentation darker, not lighter

- Comparing in the mirror every day. Pigmentation changes over months, not days

**These are the things we follow with pigmentation**

The EVE-M measurement records how dark and how widespread the pigmentation is before we start. With pigmentation we measure per season rather than per session, because the picture moves with the year.

How deep it sits matters just as much. Pigmentation can lie in the epidermis, in the dermis or in both, as it often does with melasma. Surface pigmentation responds faster and to more treatments; deeper pigmentation takes more time and a different choice. Under UV light that difference is visible; with the naked eye it is not.

That is also the most honest way to see whether it works. Pigmentation changes slowly, and your eye gets used to it.

> knop: MORE ABOUT THE SKIN ANALYSIS

WHAT WE MEASURE HERE

How dark and how widespread, mapped objectively

*Depth*

In the epidermis, in the dermis or in both. That decides the outlook and the choice of treatment

What the sun has already done, including what you cannot see

*Texture*

Whether unevenness plays a part alongside colour

Every axis is measured again at each check-up, under the same lighting. That way a difference later is something you see rather than something you have to take on faith.

**What we use for this**

- Microneedling with the SkinPen € 180 Medically certified microneedling. It works on the layer where the structure of your skin sits. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE SKINPEN CIT MICRONEEDLING IN ROTTERDAM

- Dermapen 4 € 180 Microneedling with vibrating needles that pass through the skin evenly. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE DERMAPEN 4

- Nordlys IPL for pigmentation € 75 Light on pigmentation and sun damage. The pigment first comes to the surface and then fades. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE NORDLYS IPL TREATMENT IN ROTTERDAM

**Frequently asked questions**

Will my pigmentation go away completely?

With sun damage, often largely. With melasma, control is more realistic than disappearance, and we would rather say that now than after five sessions. So which of the two you have decides the answer.

Why can I not start in the summer?

Because you would then be working against the sun for four months. Pigment cells that have just been treated respond extra strongly to UV. You would be paying for a result you lose again in September.

Does sunscreen really help that much?

With pigmentation, daily protection gives you more than any treatment does, and we earn nothing from it.

I have darker skin. Can I be treated?

Yes, and it asks for a different approach. With skin types IV to VI the chance of new pigmentation from the treatment itself is higher, so we go more carefully and more slowly. We discuss that beforehand.

My spot looks different from the rest. Should I be worried?

A spot that changes shape or colour, or that bleeds, should be assessed by your GP. That is not scaremongering but the right route. We do look at it and refer you on if that is needed.

Can I do anything about the spots on my hands?

Yes, and hands are honestly the most awkward area: they get the most sun and they are the easiest to forget. Treatment is possible; keeping up the protection is the real work.

**Why the season counts with pigmentation**

The skin analysis can be done all year round. That way we have a starting point ready for the moment the season does work in your favour.

### /en/skin-concerns/pores

**Tabbladtitel:** Pores: what can and cannot be done about them | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Making large pores less visible with peels, microneedling and HydraFacial. What the skin around them decides.

**LARGE PORES ON YOUR FACE**

The diameter of a pore is fixed by your make-up, but how much they stand out depends on the skin around them. There is a lot to be done about that.

With peels, microneedling and a HydraFacial we empty the pores and smooth the skin around them. Together that makes them stand out a good deal less.

> knop: Read on

> knop: TURN THE THREE DIALS ON

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

**Three things that make pores visible**

Three things decide how visible a pore is, and all three can be influenced with treatment and care.

Notice what does not happen: no opening gets smaller. They are exactly the same size in every position.

- Content out A filled pore reads as a dark dot and so looks larger.

- Firmer skin around it With less firm skin the opening sags into a teardrop shape, especially on the cheeks.

- Less shine on top A shiny surface outlines every pore edge with a small shadow.

> knop: Make the pore smaller This switch does not work. Press it if you want to know why.

**This is how it looks with none of them**

Filled, stretched and shiny. This is the picture people walk in with, thinking the pore itself is too large.

**Four pictures**

The fourth picture is the one most often confused with large pores, and that costs people sessions of the wrong treatment.

- Blackheads Small dark dots, mostly on the nose

- Small white bumps Bumps under the skin that you mostly feel

- Visibly wide pores Pores you clearly see up close, without anything in them

- Dents that look like pores Pits you mostly see in side light

*WHAT YOU SEE*

Dark dots in the pores of the nose, chin and sometimes the forehead. They return after you remove them.

*WHAT IT MEANS*

A pore filled with sebum and dead skin cells. The dark colour is not dirt but oxidation: the top layer changes colour in contact with air.

*WHAT WE DO*

Emptying them visibly helps, but the pore fills up again. So it is about how fast that goes, not whether it happens.

This is not dirt and it does not come from not washing your face properly. Scrubbing harder usually makes it worse.

> knop: HAVE THIS LOOKED AT

Do you have red, inflamed spots as well? Then the story starts there, because working on pores in inflamed skin is mopping with the tap on.

**What helps and what we advise against**

Four of these habits people do at home convinced they help. Stopping them costs nothing and often makes the biggest difference.

**THIS WORKS**

- Accepting that the diameter is fixed and steering on what does change. That makes a visible difference and saves you a run of disappointments.

- Cleansing consistently and mildly. Twice a day gently works better than once a week thoroughly.

- Working on the firmness of the surrounding skin, because that decides the shape of the opening.

- Knowing whether you are looking at pores or at dents. That difference decides the whole approach.

- Comparing photos under the same light. Pores always look worse in light from the side.

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Squeezing. You widen the opening and raise the chance of a mark or a small scar.

- Steaming to open pores. They have no muscle, so they do not open anywhere.

- Pore strips as a fixed habit. You pull the top layer off with it and the pore simply fills up again.

- Stacking strongly drying products. Dehydrated skin usually makes more oil instead.

- Booking a treatment on the promise of smaller pores. Ask what exactly changes then.

**Why we measure under fixed light**

Pores are the most sensitive of all subjects to how you look at them. In light falling from the side and up close everyone sees them; in ordinary daylight almost nobody does. So without a fixed set-up you are mostly measuring your lamp.

So we record them under the same lighting and at the same distance. Then a difference later is really a difference and not a different moment of the day.

> knop: MORE ABOUT THE SKIN ANALYSIS

WHAT WE MEASURE HERE

*Visibility*

How strongly the openings stand out under fixed light

*Filling*

How many pores have a dark core

*Shine*

How much the surface reflects

Every axis is measured again at each check-up, under the same lighting. That way a difference later is something you see rather than something you have to take on faith.

**What we use for this**

- HydraFacial € 170 Cleansing, exfoliation and hydration. In one pass, visible straight away and with no recovery time. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE HYDRAFACIAL SYNDEO HYDRAFACIAL IN ROTTERDAM

- OxyGeneo glow € 150 Exfoliating and bringing oxygen into the skin, in one treatment. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE OXYGENEO OXYGENEO IN ROTTERDAM

- Medical peels € 140 From light to strong. The strength decides how deep it goes and how much you flake. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE PEEL LINES CHEMICAL PEEL IN ROTTERDAM

- Microneedling with the SkinPen € 180 Medically certified microneedling. It works on the layer where the structure of your skin sits. FOR THIS CONCERN WITH THE SKINPEN CIT MICRONEEDLING IN ROTTERDAM

- Dermapen 4 € 180 Microneedling with vibrating needles that pass through the skin evenly. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE DERMAPEN 4

- FRAC3 On request A fractional laser that goes deeper, for texture, pores and irregularities. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER FOTONA 4D IN ROTTERDAM

- SupErficial laser peel On request A superficial laser peel for smoother skin and more shine. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER

- Fotona Resurfacing On request Skin renewal with laser, for pores, texture and smoother skin. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER

**Frequently asked questions**

Can my pores really not get smaller?

The opening itself not permanently, no. That is tied to the oil gland beneath and to your make-up. What does change is how visible they are, and that is in the end what you see in the mirror.

Why do blackheads keep coming back?

Because the pore keeps doing what it is meant to do: produce oil. So emptying it is maintenance and not a solution. The question that counts is how fast it returns, and that can be steered.

Does steaming help?

Not to open pores, because there is no muscle there. Heat does make sebum more fluid, which makes emptying easier. That is something other than what is usually promised.

I have acne as well. Where do I start?

With the acne. As long as there is inflammation, working on pores is mopping with the tap on, and treating inflamed skin raises the chance of scars.

Do pore strips work?

For a moment. You pull the top of the plug off with it and it looks better straight away. The pore then simply fills up again, and with frequent use the skin around it gets irritated.

What does this cost?

That depends on the treatment that suits your skin, and we work that out at the consultation. The consultation costs 50 euros; if you have a treatment in the same appointment, that amount comes off again. You then hear straight away how many sessions it takes and what the total will be. Every price per treatment is published on the price page.

**Less visible is achievable.**

Under fixed light we look at what you are looking at, whether it is pores or something else, and what can realistically be changed in your case.

### /en/skin-concerns/psoriasis

**Tabbladtitel:** Psoriasis: more than skin | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Psoriasis comes from your immune system. What your GP does, and what we can do alongside for your skin barrier.

**PSORIASIS AND YOUR SKIN**

Psoriasis is a condition of your immune system that shows itself in the skin. The treatment goes through your GP or dermatologist, and alongside that we work on your skin barrier.

Your nails and joints can be involved too. With joints especially it matters that they are looked at in time.

> knop: SEE WHERE IT SITS

Stiff joints in the morning, swollen fingers or toes, or back pain that improves with movement. Mention that to your GP, even if your skin patches are mild.

Damage to a joint is permanent. This is the one part where being on time really changes something.

**Four patches**

They do not always flare at the same time but they do belong together. Nails and joints are the most often mistaken for something else.

- FROM TOP TO BOTTOM They belong to the same condition, even when they do not flare at the same time.

- Scalp

- Elbows and knees

- Joints DO NOT WAIT ON THIS

PSORIASIS CAPITIS

*WHAT YOU SEE OR FEEL*

Thick scales stuck to the hair, often just past the hairline on your forehead or behind your ears.

*WHY THIS COUNTS*

This is most often mistaken for stubborn dandruff. The difference is in the thickness and in the sharp border.

Psoriasis can appear in several places. That is why a cream tackles the patch and not the cause: the diagnosis and the medical treatment belong with your GP or dermatologist. We assess the skin and advise on supporting care.

**What helps and what we advise against**

Have joint complaints assessed in time. Delay there costs damage that does not come back.

**THIS WORKS**

- To your GP with sharply bordered, scaly patches that do not go away. There is treatment for it and it starts there.

- Mentioning joint complaints straight away, even if your skin is mild. This is the one part where waiting can cause permanent damage.

- Showing your nails during that conversation. They are often forgotten and they say something.

- Keep moisturising on quiet days. Supple skin splits open less easily, and damage can trigger a new patch.

- Knowing that it runs in periods. That makes a quiet period no cure and a flare-up no failure.

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Scraping or scrubbing scales off. Damage in a spot can trigger new psoriasis there.

- Treating nail changes as fungus on your own. That is the most common mistake and it takes months before you know it is not working.

- Booking a cosmetic treatment on active patches.

- Stopping prescribed medication as soon as it improves, without discussing it.

- Assuming it is contagious or that it comes down to hygiene. Neither is true.

**Frequently asked questions**

Is psoriasis contagious?

No. It is a condition of your own immune system and cannot be passed on, not even by touch.

What can you do with psoriasis?

With psoriasis we can assess the skin and advise on supporting skincare. For the diagnosis and medical treatment we work with, or refer to, your GP or dermatologist where needed. We do not treat active psoriasis patches with damaging or intensively exfoliating treatments.

I only have pits in my nails. Does that count?

That is reason enough to have it looked at. Nail changes are often the first or only sign and are almost always mistaken for fungus.

My joints are stiff in the morning. Does that belong with this?

It can, and it is the part you should not wait on. Morning stiffness lasting longer than half an hour should be discussed, even if your skin patches are small.

Can I come to you for something else?

If your skin is calm at that moment and it is about a different subject, we will look along. We do not treat over patches and we say so when we do not think it is sensible.

**When you belong with your GP**

Mention your nails and your joints in that conversation, even if you notice little of them yourself. Those two are the most often skipped. Alongside your doctor's treatment we work on your skin barrier.

**Book a consultation alongside your treatment**

The medication goes through your GP or dermatologist. We look at your skin barrier and at what is possible between flare-ups, in consultation with your doctor.

### /en/skin-concerns/rosacea

**Tabbladtitel:** Treating rosacea in Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Rosacea can be steered: fewer flare-ups and a calmer base colour. Which triggers are in your own hands and what a treatment can add.

**ROSACEA: SKIN THAT KEEPS FLARING UP**

Rosacea is a long-term condition that can be steered well. With the right treatments and care your base colour settles, you flare up less often and the vessels become less visible.

Do you mostly see separate vessels and no flare-ups? Then it is probably couperose. They often go together; the skin therapist assesses under magnification which one you are dealing with.

> knop: SORT YOUR TRIGGERS

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

**Which triggers you can steer yourself**

You already knew wine makes you red. The question that counts is how many of your triggers you can influence and how many you cannot, because that ratio decides whether habits or treatment gives you the most. Tap what you recognise.

> knop: ALCOHOL

> knop: SPICY FOOD

> knop: HOT COFFEE OR TEA

> knop: SKINCARE WITH FRAGRANCE

> knop: SAUNA OR A HOT SHOWER

> knop: SUN

> knop: COLD AND WIND

> knop: STRESS

> knop: HORMONES

> knop: EXERCISE

**YOU HAVE A SAY IN THESE**

You can change something about these triggers, and that often gives you the most.

- Nothing in this group yet.

**THESE ARE OUT OF YOUR HANDS**

These triggers are hard to avoid. Treatment can then help to keep the symptoms under control.

**Tap what makes you red**

Pick everything you recognise. It is about the ratio: how many of your triggers can you influence yourself?

Not sure? Keep track of it for two weeks. That gives you more than any test.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

This is not a diagnosis and not a test. It is a way to see your own pattern before you walk in here, so that the conversation does not start from zero.

**Which form of rosacea do you recognise?**

Rosacea has stages that ask for a different approach. With two of them our answer is that you belong with a dermatologist. So that is what it says, because that is quicker than a course of treatment here first.

- Flushing that lingers You go red quickly and it fades more slowly than it does for others

- Visible vessels Small red lines on your cheeks or beside your nose

- Red bumps on a red base Spots that look like acne, but on skin that is already red

- Thickened skin on the nose The skin of your nose thickens and the pores get larger

*WHAT YOU SEE*

Waves of redness across cheeks, nose and forehead. At first it fades; later a base colour stays behind.

*WHAT IT MEANS*

The vascular response is overactive but there is no lasting damage yet. This is the best moment to step in.

*WHAT WE DO FIRST*

Mapping the triggers, and only then looking at whether the vessels need treatment. This is often the stage with the fewest sessions.

This is not sensitive skin from the wrong products. It is a vascular response, and that does not change with a different cream.

> knop: HAVE THIS LOOKED AT

**Rosacea or acne?**

This is what goes wrong most often, and it is not harmless: treating rosacea as acne makes it worse. Four differences you can check yourself.

- Blackheads Present with acne, absent with rosacea. The quickest difference.

- Where it sits Acne on the jawline and forehead, rosacea in the middle of the face.

- Flushing Flaring up is part of rosacea; it is not part of acne.

- What scrubbing does With acne sometimes something. With rosacea it makes things worse.

If after reading this you think you have acne after all, then the other page is where you belong, and that is not a detour but the shortest route.

**What helps and what we advise against**

With rosacea the first point on the left is free and often gives you the most. That is not the answer a clinic is supposed to give, but it is the right one.

**THIS WORKS**

- Keeping track of your triggers for two weeks before you buy anything. This is free and gives you the most

- Sun protection, every day. With rosacea, UV is both a trigger and an accelerator

- Lukewarm showers and rinsing your face lukewarm. Unappealing advice, large effect

- Products without alcohol and fragrance, and no more than three steps

- Referring you to a doctor when bumps appear

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Treating it as acne. Scrubs and drying products demonstrably make rosacea worse

- Sauna, hot showers and steaming. Heat is the strongest trigger there is

- Trying new products all the time. Every change is another stimulus for skin that already overreacts

- Covering it with a thick layer and then not cleansing. That gives you a second problem

- Expecting it to go away. Rosacea can be controlled, not cured, and we would rather say that now

**With rosacea, redness is what counts.**

Redness is the kind of thing your eye gets used to. That is why we measure it: not to convince you, but so that we can see the difference on a day when you think nothing has changed.

We also measure the visible vessels separately, because they respond differently than the base colour does.

> knop: MORE ABOUT THE SKIN ANALYSIS

WHAT WE MEASURE HERE

The base colour of your skin, apart from a flare-up

*Vessels*

How many are visible and where they sit

*Barrier*

How reactive your skin is at this moment

Every axis is measured again at each check-up, under the same lighting. That way a difference later is something you see rather than something you have to take on faith.

**What we use for this**

- Nordlys IPL for redness and vessels € 75 Light on visible vessels, rosacea and lasting redness. The vessel darkens and then fades. FOR THIS CONCERN WITH THE NORDLYS IPL TREATMENT IN ROTTERDAM

- LED therapy € 30 Light that calms the skin. In several wavelengths, without needles or acids. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE PRECISION PHOTONIC SYSTEM

- Food intolerance test € 300 A blood test that maps which foods your body reacts to. WHAT IT INVOLVES

**Frequently asked questions**

Will my rosacea go away?

No, rosacea is long-term. What is possible: fewer flare-ups, fewer visible vessels and a calmer base colour. For most people that is a large difference in how they feel.

How do I know it is rosacea and not acne?

The quickest difference: acne has blackheads, rosacea does not. Rosacea also sits more in the middle of your face and comes with flushing. You only know for certain after an assessment.

Do I have to give up wine and spicy food?

That is your choice, not our prescription. We do tell you what it does, and then you decide what it is worth to you. For some people it makes a big difference, for others little.

Does laser help against the vessels?

With visible vessels, treatment usually gives the most of everything we do. New vessels can still appear as long as the triggers continue, so maintenance is part of it.

Can I still exercise?

Yes. Stopping exercise is not advice we give. We look at timing, cooling and what you do afterwards.

I am embarrassed that I go red so quickly.

We hear that often, and it is the reason people wait for years. You do not have to explain anything here. We look at your skin, not at your behaviour.

What does this cost?

That depends on the treatment that suits your skin, and we work that out at the consultation. The consultation costs 50 euros; if you have a treatment in the same appointment, that amount comes off again. You then hear straight away how many sessions it takes and what the total will be. Every price per treatment is published on the price page.

**Book a consultation at Diba Clinics**

At the consultation we measure your redness, go through your triggers and you hear what is realistic in your case. Including when that means you belong with a doctor.

### /en/skin-concerns/sagging-skin

**Tabbladtitel:** Treating skin laxity in Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Treating skin laxity with needling and laser, which get collagen production going. What there is realistically to gain.

**A SLACKENING JAWLINE AND DROPPING CHEEKS**

A dropping jawline and cheeks we treat with techniques that get collagen production going: microneedling with the SkinPen or the Dermapen 4, fractional laser with the Fotona, and radiofrequency. That gives firmer tissue and a tighter line.

Which technique suits you depends on your skin and on the stage the laxity is in. The skin therapist establishes that at the intake, and usually it is a combination.

> knop: Read on

> knop: WHERE IT BECOMES VISIBLE

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

**What there is to gain**

The therapist looks at your skin standing and lying down. The difference between those two pictures shows what a treatment can give.

- Assessed standing The skin therapist looks at your face upright and at rest. That is how you look at the moments when you notice it yourself, and that is where we count from.

- Compared lying down Then the same face lying down, where gravity has no grip. The difference between those two pictures shows how much firmness there is to gain.

- Recorded in images We take both photos under fixed lighting. At a following appointment we put them side by side, so that you see the change rather than estimate it.

**The four stages**

Laxity, volume loss and skin that has truly let go get mixed up and ask for three different things. Only the first is our trade.

- The skin springs back more slowly You pinch your cheek and it takes a moment to go smooth again

- The jawline gets vaguer The border between your jaw and your neck is less sharp than it used to be

- Your face has become narrower Your cheeks are flatter and your face looks hollow

- Skin that really hangs A fold you can take hold of and that stays hanging

*HOW YOU RECOGNISE IT YOURSELF*

Gently pinch a fold on your cheek or the back of your hand and let go. If the fold stays for a second, that is what you are measuring.

*WHAT IT IS*

Elastin and collagen decline, which makes the skin spring back more slowly. This is the earliest stage and the stage in which a treatment gives the most.

*WHAT WE DO*

Getting repair going in the deeper layers, with laser or needling, in a series over months. There is gain to be had here.

There is still structure to build on. Count on a series over months, and on sharper rather than tight.

> knop: HAVE THIS LOOKED AT

Then laxity is not your subject.

Lines and laxity occur together but are not the same. If it is the lines themselves you care about, it starts with the difference between skin and muscle on the lines page.

> knop: TO LINES AND WRINKLES

**What helps and what we advise against**

Here patience is not a side issue. Collagen builds over months, and coming more often does not speed that up.

**THIS WORKS**

- Establishing first whether it is about firmness, about volume, or about skin that has truly let go

- Tightening the deeper layers with laser, in a series with weeks in between

- A skin analysis, because change over months does not show in the mirror and does show in a measurement

- Daily sun protection, because UV radiation breaks down collagen and elastin

- Saying when the difference gets too small to be worth the investment

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Imitating surgery. What has let go is not fastened back here

- Filling volume. We do not work with fillers, and for a face that has become narrower that is often the answer

- Starting a series of treatments while the assessment shows that little improvement is to be expected

- Promising a result in weeks. Collagen building runs over months

- Treating tanned skin

**Why we record it beforehand**

Laxity changes slowly, and you look every day. So you notice progress as little as you notice decline. The EVE-M records your skin under fixed light and from a fixed angle, before the first session takes place.

That works both ways. It makes a difference demonstrable, and it also makes visible when little changes. The latter is a reason to stop or do something else, and not to carry on because a package still had sessions left.

> knop: MORE ABOUT THE SKIN ANALYSIS

WHAT WE MEASURE HERE

*Elasticity*

How quickly the skin springs back, and where it no longer does

*Contour*

The line along the jaw and neck, recorded from a fixed angle

*Texture*

The surface, because that often changes before the shape does

Every axis is measured again at each check-up, under the same lighting. That way a difference later is something you see rather than something you have to take on faith.

**What we use for this**

- Fotona TimeWalker € 150 Fifteen treatments on one device, from a light laser peel to the complete 4D. Each with its own purpose. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER FOTONA 4D IN ROTTERDAM

- Fotona 4D € 370 Four laser treatments in one session. From the inside through the cheek to a closing peel. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER

- Fotona 4D Men On request The same protocol of four, set for the generally thicker skin of men. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER

- SmoothLiftin On request Collagen stimulation from the inside, through the lining of your cheek. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER

- PIANO skin tightening On request Deep, even heating to firm the face, jawline and neck. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER

- VectorLift € 150 A laser brow lift and firming of the forehead, without needles. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER

- Fotona 4D Full Package € 575 The full 4D protocol with the neck and the jawline included, in one appointment. WHAT IT INVOLVES

**Frequently asked questions**

Is this an alternative to a facelift?

No. Tightening the skin and removing tissue are two different things, and we only do the first. What we do works in the stage before that, and once that stage has passed we say so.

From what age does this make sense?

Age says little here. What matters is how much your skin still springs back, and the therapist establishes that in the consultation. If there is little to gain, you hear that, and that is the advice.

How long does the result last?

The process itself carries on, so it is not an end point but a shift. How long it stays noticeable differs a great deal per person; we agree beforehand when we measure again rather than naming a number.

Does it hurt?

You feel warmth and sometimes short stings. Most people describe it as manageable, and no anaesthetic is needed. What you notice afterwards depends on the treatment and is on the treatment page.

What does this cost?

That depends on the treatment that suits your skin, and we work that out at the consultation. The consultation costs 50 euros; if you have a treatment in the same appointment, that amount comes off again. You then hear straight away how many sessions it takes and what the total will be. Every price per treatment is published on the price page.

At the skin consultation the therapist looks at how much your skin still springs back and measures what is there now. If there turns out to be little to gain, you hear that, and that is the advice.
