### /en/skin-concerns/scars

**Tabbladtitel:** Treating scars and stretch marks in Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Treating scars and stretch marks with microneedling and laser. Red scars usually respond best; with white ones we focus on the texture.

**SCARS AND STRETCH MARKS THAT STAY VISIBLE**

With scars and stretch marks the age decides what is possible. Red and purple scars generally respond best; with white scars we focus on the texture and the relief. At the intake the skin therapist assesses which stage it is in and which treatment belongs with that.

> knop: SET THE SCAR CLOCK

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

**How old it is decides what is possible.**

Slide to how long you have had it. The colour in the drawing changes with you, and the answer gets blunter the further you go. Scars and stretch marks follow the same axis.

This is the period in which you can influence the most.

The bar is not a measurement but a proportion: it shows how the room to change something shrinks as a scar gets older.

> knop: JUST APPEARED

> knop: 3 TO 12 MONTHS

> knop: 1 TO 3 YEARS

> knop: 3 TO 5 YEARS

> knop: OLDER THAN 5 YEARS

**3 to 12 months**

*WHAT HAPPENS IN YOUR SKIN THEN*

The collagen is being rearranged. In this period the scar can still go either way: flatter and lighter, or thicker if production overshoots.

*WHAT IS REALISTIC*

This is the window. Here there is the most to gain, with scars as well as with red stretch marks. Anyone who comes now comes at the right moment.

*WHAT WE WOULD DO*

Measure and then treat in a targeted way. With red and raised scars we often work on the blood vessels first, then on the texture.

> knop: HAVE THIS LOOKED AT

Not sure exactly how old it is? Look at the colour. Red means young, white means old. That is more accurate than your memory.

**Which kind of scar do you recognise?**

Dents respond best. Raised scars and keloids belong with a doctor. And with stretch marks the colour matters more than the place. Pick what comes closest to you.

- Dents in the skin Pits you mostly see in side light

- Raised, firm scars A lump or cord that stands above the skin

- Red or purple stretch marks Lines that look new and are still red

- White stretch marks Lines that have long been white and thin

*WHAT YOU SEE*

Small dips, often on the cheeks and temples. They stand out in light from the side and far less straight on.

*WHAT IT MEANS*

Tissue was lost during healing. The skin around it is normal.

*WHAT WE DO FIRST*

This type responds best of all scars. We work on the edge of the dent, not on its floor.

These are not large pores. A pore is round and has an opening; a dent does not.

**The step everyone wants to skip.**

Almost nobody comes here for step one. Yet it decides whether the rest makes sense, because treating scars in inflamed skin produces new scars.

- Calm first As long as there is active acne or inflammation, you are adding scars rather than removing them. This is the step people want to skip.

- Then measure We record how deep and how extensive it is. Scars change slowly, so without a measurement you cannot see later whether it worked.

- Then treat Targeted treatment, with an agreed number of sessions and a moment at which we look again. If it does not work, we stop.

- And then protect A treated scar stays more sensitive to the sun for a while. Without protection you trade the scar for a dark patch.

Do you still have active acne? Then step one belongs on the acne page, and only after that here. That is not a detour but the shortest route to fewer scars.

**What helps and what we advise against**

The first cross on the right is the most expensive mistake on this page, and it costs nothing to avoid: waiting until it is white.

**THIS WORKS**

- With a fresh scar: out of the sun, every day, for a year. This is the cheapest treatment there is

- Coming in time. Red and young responds better than white and old, and that matters more than the choice of treatment

- Calming the acne or the underlying problem first, and only then the scar

- Measuring before we start, because scars change slowly and your eye gets used to them

- With stretch marks in pregnancy: waiting until after breastfeeding and then measuring

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Waiting until it is white. That is the most common mistake, and then there is little left to do

- Treating scars while the acne is still active. Then you are making new ones

- Creams that promise white stretch marks will disappear. That does not happen, whatever the price

- A sunbed to camouflage the difference. Scar tissue does not tan, so the difference only grows

- Sanding or pricking it yourself. You are making a new wound where the old one was

**With scars, depth counts.**

Scars change slowly. So we record the starting situation and compare it after a while with a fresh assessment.

With stretch marks we also measure the colour, because it tells us which phase they are in and so what is still possible.

> knop: MORE ABOUT THE SKIN ANALYSIS

WHAT WE MEASURE HERE

*Texture*

How deep the dents are and how extensive

*Colour*

Red, pink or white: that decides the phase

*Surface*

How large the area is that we treat

Every axis is measured again at each check-up, under the same lighting. That way a difference later is something you see rather than something you have to take on faith.

**What we use for this**

- Microneedling with the SkinPen € 180 Medically certified microneedling. It works on the layer where the structure of your skin sits. FOR THIS CONCERN WITH THE SKINPEN CIT MICRONEEDLING IN ROTTERDAM

- Dermapen 4 € 180 Microneedling with vibrating needles that pass through the skin evenly. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE DERMAPEN 4

- Fotona TimeWalker € 150 Fifteen treatments on one device, from a light laser peel to the complete 4D. Each with its own purpose. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER FOTONA 4D IN ROTTERDAM

- FRAC3 On request A fractional laser that goes deeper, for texture, pores and irregularities. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER

- Fotona Scar Repair € 195 Laser on scars: acne scars, surgical scars and stretch marks. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER

- Scar therapy € 100 For scars after surgery or a caesarean. The price follows the length of the scar. WHAT IT INVOLVES

**What others say about it.**

These come from Salonized and were not picked by us on content: they are the reviews that mention scars. They are about programmes lasting months, and you hear that in them.

Reviews translated from Dutch.

- “Very happy overall. I came in the first time with a lot of blemishes and scars and I can say with positivity that my face looks very even and lovely.” Brayson Visit to Diba Clinics ABOUT 6 YEARS AGO

- “Had a really lovely Hydrafacial treatment. I have such a lovely glow! My scars have been treated for the first time too so I'm looking forward to the progress of this process :) Thank you dear Rojda.” Elif HydraFacial ALMOST 4 YEARS AGO

- “I've been by 3 times now for the diode laser and I genuinely see an 80% difference! The scars and spots on my skin have hugely improved too thanks to the dermapen. A forever regular anyway!!” Sara Laser hair removal OVER 7 YEARS AGO

**Frequently asked questions**

Will my scars disappear completely?

No. A scar is permanent tissue; what we do is make it less noticeable. With fresh scars that difference is large, with old ones small. We say beforehand which category yours falls into.

I have stretch marks from pregnancy. Can I come already?

You can always come, and measuring too. We prefer to treat after breastfeeding. If your stretch marks are still red, this is the best moment to have the conversation, because that window is closing.

Why does my acne have to be calm first?

Because treating inflamed skin can give new scars. You would be paying for a treatment that makes the picture worse. That is why we sometimes say no to someone who came especially for it.

Do those scar creams from the chemist work?

With fresh scars silicone can do something, especially with raised scars. With white stretch marks and old scars it does not. The price says nothing about that.

I am ashamed of my stretch marks when swimming.

We hear that often, and it is a real reason to come. We are just not going to pretend we can make them vanish. What we will do is say honestly how much difference there is to expect in your case.

How many sessions do I need?

That depends on the age of the scar and the type. After the measurement you get a number and a price, and a moment at which we look again at whether it is working.

What does this cost?

That depends on the treatment that suits your skin, and we work that out at the consultation. The consultation costs 50 euros; if you have a treatment in the same appointment, that amount comes off again. You then hear straight away how many sessions it takes and what the total will be. Every price per treatment is published on the price page.

**Young scars respond best**

With a red scar or red stretch marks this is the moment when it matters most. With old scars we work out honestly whether it gives enough.

### /en/skin-concerns/sensitive-skin

**Tabbladtitel:** Sensitive skin: a type or a consequence? | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Calming sensitive skin with mild treatments and a care routine your skin can handle.

**SKIN THAT REACTS QUICKLY**

Skin that reacts quickly usually has a weakened barrier. We calm it with mild treatments and a care schedule your skin can handle.

At the intake we go through your skincare. Often there are several irritating products in it that together become too much.

> knop: Read on

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

**What we to go through**

We go through your care. Each product can be fine on its own; what matters is what works together on the same barrier.

- Retinol or vitamin A In low strength too, and even if it is only twice a week

- Fruit acids Glycolic, lactic or mandelic acid, often in a toner or serum

- Salicylic acid Often in products for congestion

- Benzoyl peroxide For acne, on prescription or from the chemist

- Vitamin C in acid form Usually a serum for the morning

- Scrubbing or a cleansing brush Grains, textured cloths, or a device

- Toner with alcohol Recognisable by the fresh, cold feeling right afterwards

- Fragrance in your care Listed as parfum or fragrance on the packaging

- Cleansing more than twice a day Exercising and then washing again counts too

- Hot showers or steaming A long warm shower in winter counts too

**Sometimes the cause is not in your skincare**

What you ticked is not much in itself. If your skin still reacts to everything, we would rather look for the cause somewhere other than your bathroom cabinet.

Look below and see whether one of the conditions sounds familiar. If so, the story starts there and not with your products.

> knop: THEN READ ON BELOW

**Four conditions that start like this.**

Sensitive skin is a complaint and not a diagnosis. These four conditions often start the same way and each asks for something different.

- Rosacea Lasting redness on cheeks and nose, flare-ups after heat or alcohol, sometimes bumps without blackheads. TO THE ROSACEA PAGE

- Eczema Itching first and foremost, dry flaking patches that come back in the same places, sometimes cracks. TO THE ECZEMA PAGE

- Contact allergy The reaction appears in a defined spot and starts hours to days after contact, often with a clear shape. TO SKIN RASH

- A dehydrated barrier A tight feeling after washing, products that sting while they used to be fine, and worse in winter. TO DRY SKIN

With itching that keeps you from sleeping, with cracks or open spots, with patches that do not go away or keep coming back in the same place. That is no longer sensitive skin and we are not the right place for it.

**What helps and what we advise against**

Stinging does not mean a product is working. That is the most stubborn misunderstanding in skincare.

**THIS WORKS**

- Stripping back to the minimum and building up from there, one product every two weeks. Otherwise you will never know which one it was.

- Trying anything new on one small spot for a few days first, for example on your neck.

- Reading the ingredient list rather than the claim. The front says what the brand wants; the back says what is in it.

- Keeping track of what happened and when. Sensitive skin often reacts with a delay, and then your memory is not a good witness.

- Postponing treatments until your skin is calm. Waiting two weeks gives more than pushing on.

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Keeping on with a product that stings because you are supposed to get used to it. Stinging is not efficacy.

- Changing several things at once. It may well work, but you will not know what did it.

- Replacing everything with products labelled sensitive. That word is not protected and says nothing on its own.

- Tidying your skin up by scrubbing when it is already irritated.

- Assuming it is predisposition before you have stripped the routine back. In many people the predisposition only shows once the rest is gone.

**Why we look for the cause first**

Sensitive skin feels different one day from the next, and afterwards nobody remembers how it was last month. So without a fixed starting point you are talking about a memory.

So we record how red it is, how quickly moisture disappears and how the top layer sits. Then in two months the question is not whether it feels better, but whether it is better.

> knop: MORE ABOUT THE SKIN ANALYSIS

WHAT WE MEASURE HERE

*Redness*

How much is visible at rest

*Leakage*

How quickly moisture disappears through the barrier

*Texture*

How evenly the top layer sits

Every axis is measured again at each check-up, under the same lighting. That way a difference later is something you see rather than something you have to take on faith.

**What we use for this**

- LED therapy € 30 Light that calms the skin. In several wavelengths, without needles or acids. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE PRECISION PHOTONIC SYSTEM

**Frequently asked questions**

Is sensitive skin something you are born with?

Sometimes, but far from always. Many people only develop it after years, and then something has usually changed in what they use or how often. Predisposition often only shows once the rest has been taken away.

My skin stings from almost everything. What now?

Back to the minimum, for two weeks. Cleansing and one care product, nothing else. If it calms down, it was the stack; if it stays the same, we look elsewhere.

Does stinging mean it works?

No. That is a stubborn story and it is not true. A light tingle with certain ingredients can be normal, but burning and persistent stinging are a sign to stop.

Can I be treated with sensitive skin?

Usually yes, only more gently and in smaller steps. What is not possible is treating while your skin is irritated at that moment, because then it reacts more sharply and gives less.

What does this cost?

The measurement costs fifty euros. What follows is listed per treatment on the price page, and with sensitive skin that more often starts with doing less than with doing more. If the outcome is that you should strip back for two weeks, you hear that at the consultation and it costs you nothing further.

**First work out what is switched on.**

We go through your routine, measure how your barrier is doing and say what can go. Often that is the whole advice, and then the treatment is that you do less for two weeks.

### /en/skin-concerns/skin-ageing

**Tabbladtitel:** Treating skin ageing in Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Treating skin ageing with peels, needling and laser. Most of it comes from the sun and not from age, and that is exactly what can be tackled.

**SKIN AGEING TREATED**

Most of what makes your skin older comes from sunlight and not from your age. And that is exactly the part that responds well to treatment. The skin therapist chooses from medical peels, microneedling with the SkinPen or the Dermapen 4, fractional laser on the Fotona, IPL for pigment and vessels, and mesotherapy.

What it becomes for you depends on your skin and on what exactly is going on; usually it is a combination over a number of months. At the intake the skin therapist establishes what comes from the sun and what belongs to your age.

> knop: Read on

> knop: WHICH AGEING IS WHICH

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

**Sun or age**

The therapist compares a piece of skin that has seen little sun with your face. That difference shows which part comes from sun damage.

Your inner arm is exactly as old as your face. Yet it looks younger.

So everything extra you see on your face was added and did not simply grow along. That is the part a treatment does something about. Put your age in below and see how the two compare.

35 years

WHAT IS THE SAME

INSIDE OF THE UPPER ARM

YOUR FACE AND HANDS

Age

12,784 days

Genes

The same person

Food and sleep

The same body, the same years

Hormones

Smoking and alcohol

Days the skin spent outdoors

Almost none

Almost all of them

And that is with the face usually getting the most care of the two. The variable left over is not your routine.

Has hardly ever seen the sun

Smoother, more even, few spots. This is what time alone does to your skin: it gets thinner and drier, but stays even.

Sun every day, in winter too

Fine lines, uneven colour, widened vessels, rougher texture. This is time plus tens of thousands of hours of UV.

What was built up has a dial. What simply grew along does not.

The part built up by the sun is the part we can treat. At the intake the skin therapist establishes how large that part is for you, and which treatment fits with it.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

**What ageing changes in your skin**

Skin ageing is not a switch that flips at a certain age. Several things run alongside each other, they do not start at the same time and they do not share a cause. Pick a stage of life and see what is going on then.

> knop: 20 TO 30 YEARS

> knop: 30 TO 40 YEARS

> knop: 40 TO 55 YEARS

> knop: 55 YEARS AND OLDER

- Collagen declines TIME AND SUN Running, usually still invisible Production drops gradually from your twenties onwards. UV speeds it up and breaks existing collagen down as well, so this track runs in everyone but not at the same speed. COLLAGEN LOSS

- Spots come up SUN Running, usually still invisible This is almost entirely a sun track. What you see now was built up in years already gone, and what you do today decides the spots of ten years from now. LENTIGINES, HYPERPIGMENTATION

- Vessels become visible SUN Running, usually still invisible Small widened blood vessels, mostly on the nose and cheeks. Sun and heat are the biggest drivers. TELANGIECTASIA

- Texture gets rougher TIME AND SUN Running, usually still invisible Cell renewal slows down, which makes the skin look duller and reflect light differently. This is the part that responds fastest to treatment. CHANGES IN KERATINISATION AND TEXTURE

- Volume shifts TIME Not yet in play Fat pads shrink and drop, and the bone beneath changes too. This is the purest time track, and exactly the part we do nothing about. FAT AND BONE REMODELLING

**Now measuring becomes worthwhile**

The first sun damage becomes visible while nothing is set yet. A skin analysis now gives you a point of comparison, so that later you know whether something worked or whether you imagined it.

Count the ochre bars. That is the part of what you see that comes from the sun, and so the part something can still be done about today. The green bars run on whatever you choose.

**What people call ageing**

Three of them we treat. To the fourth we say no, and that is stated with the same emphasis. Pick what comes closest to you.

- Fine lines Lines around the eyes and mouth that stay put

- Dull, uneven skin Your skin looks tired while you are not

- Spots and discolouration Brown spots that were not there ten years ago

- Less defined contours The jawline and cheeks drop

*WHAT YOU SEE*

Lines that at first appeared only when smiling or frowning and now stay visible at rest too.

*WHAT IT MEANS*

The skin has less spring in that spot and the fold has worn in. That is partly movement and partly accumulated sun damage.

*WHAT WE DO*

We work on the quality of the skin around it, not on the fold itself. Expect a softer line, not smooth skin.

A line that appears only when you smile is not ageing. It belongs to a face that moves.

> knop: HAVE THIS LOOKED AT

Is it mostly about spots for you and not about lines? Then the story starts somewhere else, because there the season plays a large part in when to begin.

**What helps and what we advise against**

The first line on the left is the cheapest treatment on this whole site, and the only one that works on all five tracks at once.

**THIS WORKS**

- Use sun protection daily, in winter too and when you spend a lot of time behind glass.

- Tackling one part at a time and measuring whether it worked, rather than buying a package.

- Starting with colour and texture, because there you see fastest whether the direction is right.

- Putting your expectation on the table beforehand. If it is not achievable, you hear that before you pay.

- Accepting that part of it cannot be solved with skin treatments, and simply saying so.

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Waiting until it really starts to bother you. The tracks you cannot see yet are already running.

- Buying a treatment package without a skin analysis. Then afterwards there is no way to establish whether it did anything.

- Several aggressive treatments close together. Irritated skin makes more pigment, not less.

- Steering by an age rather than by a skin. Two people of fifty rarely need the same thing.

- Thinking an expensive cream replaces sun protection. A cream with SPF does that job, a day cream without does not.

**Ageing asks for a starting point.**

This is the subject where your eye fools you hardest. The change runs over years and you look in the same mirror every day, so you do not see the difference, in either direction.

We record the starting situation, so that after a while we can better judge whether anything has changed.

> knop: MORE ABOUT THE SKIN ANALYSIS

WHAT WE MEASURE HERE

*Colour*

Spots, evenness and widened vessels

How the skin reflects light and how it feels

Where they are and whether they stay at rest

Every axis is measured again at each check-up, under the same lighting. That way a difference later is something you see rather than something you have to take on faith.

**What we use for this**

- Dermaplaning € 150 Dead skin cells and fine hairs removed with a blade. Works without acids, so it suits sensitive skin too. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE DERMAPLANE PRO DERMAPLANING IN ROTTERDAM

- Microneedling with the SkinPen € 180 Medically certified microneedling. It works on the layer where the structure of your skin sits. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE SKINPEN CIT MICRONEEDLING IN ROTTERDAM

- Dermapen 4 € 180 Microneedling with vibrating needles that pass through the skin evenly. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE DERMAPEN 4

- Skin boosters and mesotherapy € 175 Active ingredients placed into the skin rather than onto it, at a fixed depth per injection. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE U225 INTRADERMAL INJECTOR SKIN BOOSTERS IN ROTTERDAM

- Fotona TimeWalker € 150 Fifteen treatments on one device, from a light laser peel to the complete 4D. Each with its own purpose. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER FOTONA 4D IN ROTTERDAM

- Fotona 4D € 370 Four laser treatments in one session. From the inside through the cheek to a closing peel. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER

- Fotona 4D Men On request The same protocol of four, set for the generally thicker skin of men. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER

- PIANO skin tightening On request Deep, even heating to firm the face, jawline and neck. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER

- RRS Hyalift € 175 Bringing hyaluronic acid and vitamins into the skin. For firmness and moisture, not for volume. WHAT IT INVOLVES

- Fotona 4D Full Package € 575 The full 4D protocol with the neck and the jawline included, in one appointment. WHAT IT INVOLVES

**Frequently asked questions**

From what age is this worthwhile?

There is no age at which it starts. There is a moment when measuring becomes worthwhile, and that is as soon as you want to change something. Without a starting point you will not know later whether it worked.

Can I still undo sun damage from the past?

Partly. Colour and texture can be improved a good deal, and that is usually what people notice in the mirror. Volume that is gone does not come back, and we would rather say that now than after four sessions.

Why do you not start with laser straight away?

Because we want to know first what we are looking at. The same line can be dehydration or worn-in sun damage, and those ask for different things. The measurement costs you one appointment and usually saves more.

My skin is dark. Does this apply to me too?

Yes, but differently. Darker skin shows lines less readily and shifts in pigment more, and it reacts more sharply to overly aggressive treatment. So the settings and the order are different.

How long does the result last?

As long as the cause does not carry on. Without protection the sun damage simply keeps building and then you see the same thing return; with protection people usually get one to two years before maintenance is needed. That is a figure from experience and not a measurement, and it is written here as such.

What does this cost?

That depends on the treatment that suits your skin, and we work that out at the consultation. The consultation costs 50 euros; if you have a treatment in the same appointment, that amount comes off again. You then hear straight away how many sessions it takes and what the total will be. Every price per treatment is published on the price page.

**Start by knowing what is going on.**

We measure colour, texture and lines, and tell you which part comes from the sun and which does not. After that you decide whether you want to do something, and what.

### /en/skin-concerns/skin-discolouration

**Tabbladtitel:** Skin discolouration: which colour is it? | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Brown, red or white: the colour decides which layer the discolouration sits in and which treatment belongs with it.

**DISCOLOURATION ON YOUR SKIN**

Discolouration is a catch-all word. Brown, red and white each have a different cause, sit in a different layer and ask for a different treatment.

Below you find, per colour, which treatment belongs to it, with a link to the page about it.

> knop: CHOOSE YOUR COLOUR

**Four colours**

You do not need to know the medical term. Look in daylight with your forearm next to it for comparison, and pick the colour that fits.

> knop: BROWN OR BEIGE

> knop: RED OR PINK

> knop: WHITE OR LIGHTER

> knop: BLUE OR PURPLE

More pigment than the skin around it. The question that counts is not how dark but why it is there, because that decides what is possible.

Did it come gradually over the years, or did it appear in patches at once?

- Pigmentation Separate spots that were not there ten years ago, mostly where the sun reaches.

- Melasma Larger areas on cheeks, upper lip or forehead, often started with a pregnancy or the pill.

- Dark circles Only under your eyes, while the rest of your face stays even.

Why the colour and not the place: the colour says something about the layer it sits in. Pigment lies differently from blood vessels, and that decides whether something responds to treatment. So a therapist looks at this first, and you can too.

**Everything in a row**

Above you see one colour at a time. Here they stand side by side, so that you can scan rather than click.

Brown or beige

Red or pink

Does it come up and fade again, or is it always there?

- Rosacea Lasting redness on cheeks and nose, with flare-ups after heat, alcohol or exercise.

- Acne Red patches with bumps or spots in them, that come and go.

- Skin rash Appeared suddenly, spread out, or alongside feeling ill. Then call your GP first.

- Scars One red line or patch in the place of an old wound or of stretch marks.

White or lighter

Is it on one old spot, or are new patches appearing here and there?

- Scars and stretch marks One patch that lines up exactly with an old scar or old stretch marks.

- To the GP Scattered white patches that grow or increase in number.

Blue or purple

Is it under your eyes, or somewhere else?

- Dark circles Under the eyes, blue-purple in tone, and it varies with sleep and fluid.

- Scars and stretch marks Purple lines on the stomach, thighs or breasts, often still fairly new.

- To the GP A bruise without having knocked yourself, or something that changes quickly.

**What the colour does not say.**

The colour is the first question and not the last. It points the direction; what is possible in that direction depends on things you cannot see from the outside.

- How bad it is A light discolouration can be more stubborn than a dark one. What can be done depends on the layer it sits in, and you cannot tell that from the intensity.

- Whether it goes away Two people with the same colour in the same place can have a different course. Predicting an outcome on colour alone is guessing, and we do not do that.

- How long it has been there Fresh and old often look the same, while that difference is exactly what decides how much still moves. So we ask about it rather than only looking at it.

One thing counts for more than the colour

Does a spot change shape, colour or size, does it itch or bleed, or has it appeared in a short time? Then the colour does not matter and it belongs with your GP. That holds for brown, red, white and blue alike.

**What we use for this**

- Nordlys IPL for pigmentation € 75 Light on pigmentation and sun damage. The pigment first comes to the surface and then fades. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE NORDLYS IPL TREATMENT IN ROTTERDAM

- Dermamelan Intimate € 550 Pigment treatment for the intimate area, set up the same way as the facial programme. WHAT IT INVOLVES COSMELAN AND DERMAMELAN IN ROTTERDAM

- Happy Intim € 175 Peels that make pigment in the intimate area and underarms lighter and more even. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE PEEL LINES

**Frequently asked questions**

What if I have several colours at once?

That is common and it usually means more than one thing is going on. Start with the colour that bothers you most; the rest comes up in the conversation by itself.

I am not sure which colour it is.

Look in daylight rather than under a lamp, and hold your forearm next to it for comparison. If you are torn between brown and red, press on it: red goes pale under pressure, brown does not.

Is discolouration dangerous?

Usually not, and there are exceptions that do matter. A spot that changes shape, colour or size belongs with your GP, and that holds for every colour.

Why is there no price on this page?

Because nothing is for sale here. This is a signpost; the prices are with the treatment it eventually points to.

What does this cost?

That depends on the treatment that suits your skin, and we work that out at the consultation. The consultation costs 50 euros; if you have a treatment in the same appointment, that amount comes off again. You then hear straight away how many sessions it takes and what the total will be. Every price per treatment is published on the price page.

**Just come by. We will look with you.**

If you are torn between two colours or several changes are going on at once, have the spot assessed.

### /en/skin-concerns/skin-rash

**Tabbladtitel:** Skin rash: do you call today or tomorrow? | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** A skin rash is a symptom with dozens of causes. When to call today, and which kinds are the most common.

**SKIN RASH, AND WHEN IT IS URGENT**

A skin rash is a symptom and not a condition. The causes run from harmless to urgent, and a diagnosis belongs with your GP.

On this page are the signs that mean you call today, and the common kinds of rash with what can be done about them.

> knop: Read on

> knop: LOOK AT THE WARNING SIGNS FIRST

**Six signs that mean you call today.**

- Fever, chills or you feel yourself getting more ill quickly

- The rash clearly spreads within hours

- Swelling of lips, tongue or throat, or trouble breathing or swallowing

- Drowsiness, confusion, neck pain or sharp headache in bright light

- Blisters or skin peeling away, or spots in your mouth or eyes

- A rash in a baby, or in someone with a weakened immune system

If you recognise any of this, calling is the only right answer. How the rash looks no longer counts then.

*During office hours*

Your own GP

*Evening, night or weekend*

The out-of-hours GP service

*Someone looks ill and waiting does not feel right*

112

**How a rash behaves**

Not what you see but what it does says the most. This is also the first question you get, from us and from your GP.

- Gone within hours Welts that come up and disappear within a day, sometimes returning elsewhere. That pattern fits hives, and then what came before it counts.

- The same for weeks Patches that stay put and change slowly. That points more to something with the skin barrier than to a reaction of the moment.

- Exactly where something touched A sharp border following the shape of a strap, a piece of jewellery or a collar. The shape gives the cause away, and it is usually contact.

- Outward from one spot Started at one point and spread from there. That course belongs to a different group of causes than something that came up everywhere at once.

**Four that are common.**

These four are the most common. They help you describe what you see, and that makes the conversation with your GP shorter.

- Contact reaction A defined spot with a clear shape, exactly where something touched your skin. Starts hours to days afterwards. WHERE TO GO Your GP, who can request allergy tests if needed.

- Eczema Itching comes first, dry flaking patches that keep coming back in the same place. WHERE TO GO Your GP. There is treatment for it and it starts there. TO THE ECZEMA PAGE

- Hives Raised, itchy welts that move around and are gone again within a day, to return elsewhere. WHERE TO GO Your GP. With swelling of lips or throat: call the emergency number.

- A virus A rash together with fever or feeling ill, often fairly sudden and spread over the body. WHERE TO GO Your GP, and urgently if someone looks ill with it.

**What helps and what we advise against**

Ointment on an unexplained rash changes the picture the doctor has to assess.

**THIS WORKS**

- Watching how ill someone feels. That counts for more than how the rash looks, and it decides whether you call today or tomorrow.

- Taking a photo at the start. A rash changes quickly and the doctor rarely sees the first day.

- Writing down when it started and what came before it: a new product, a new medicine, something eaten, somewhere you walked.

- When in doubt, contact your GP or the out-of-hours service. They can judge how quickly you need to be seen.

- Cooling for itching, and otherwise leaving it alone until you know what it is.

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Putting ointment or cream on an unexplained rash before a doctor has looked. You change the picture with it.

- Waiting with fever, rapid spread or spots that do not fade under pressure.

- Searching the internet for a photo that looks like it. A rash looks different on everyone, and that is why a doctor looks.

- Booking a cosmetic treatment while there is an unexplained rash.

- Scratching, however hard that is. Scratching makes the picture less clear and the skin more vulnerable.

**Frequently asked questions**

Can I tell from the rash whether it is serious?

Not reliably. A rash that looks harmless can still be serious, and on darker skin the difference is hard to see anyway. How ill someone feels counts for more: fever, drowsiness, neck pain or breathlessness are reasons to call at once.

My rash itches badly but otherwise I feel fine.

Then there is usually no hurry, and it is still a question for your GP. With swelling of lips, tongue or throat, or with breathlessness, that does not apply and you call at once.

Could it come from a new product?

It could, especially if the spot has the shape of where the product was. Stop using it, keep the packaging and take it to your appointment.

Why is there no list of photos here?

Because you would go looking for the photo that looks most like you, and that is exactly the wrong way round. A rash looks different on everyone, and on darker skin often very different from the photos you find online.

Can I come to you for this?

With an unexplained rash your GP makes the diagnosis first. Once you know what it is, you can come to us for the repair of your skin barrier, in consultation with your doctor.

**To your GP. If in doubt, today.**

With an unexplained rash a doctor should make the diagnosis. Once you know what it is, we can work on your skin barrier alongside that, in consultation with your doctor.

**Book a consultation once you know what it is**

With an unexplained rash a doctor makes the diagnosis first. After that we look at what can be done for your skin barrier. If you do not know yet, do call; then you hear whether it belongs with us or not.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

### /en/skin-concerns/skin-tags

**Tabbladtitel:** Having skin tags removed in Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Having skin tags removed, usually in one appointment. We charge per quarter of an hour and not per tag.

**SKIN TAGS REMOVED**

A soft, skin-coloured flap on a narrow stalk on your neck, underarm or groin is a skin tag. Harmless, it does not go away on its own, and it is usually sorted in one appointment.

We charge per quarter of an hour rather than per tag, so several in one appointment is usually better value. The skin therapist assesses each spot first, because all sorts of things hang from a neck that look like one.

> knop: Read on

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

**What we look at**

The skin therapist assesses the shape, the colour and whether the spot hangs from a stalk. That decides whether it can go here.

- See whether there is a stalk Does it hang loose from a narrower piece of skin, or is it attached across a broad base? A stalk points to a skin tag; a broad base points to something else that we look at separately.

- Look at the colour Skin-coloured or light brown and even throughout is ordinary. Uneven brown, black, or several colours mixed together is a reason to have someone else look at it first.

- Think back Was it exactly like this six months ago? Unchanged is reassuring. If it is growing, itching or bleeding, it goes to your GP and not to us.

**Four kinds of growths**

They sit in the same places and feel almost the same. The difference decides whether it is done here in a quarter of an hour.

- A flap on a stalk A soft hanging flap on your neck, underarm or groin

- A rough brown lump A brown spot that feels raised, as though it were stuck on

- A raised mole A brown lump that has been there for years, sometimes with a hair in it

- Something that is changing A spot that grows, changes colour, itches or bleeds

*HOW YOU RECOGNISE IT YOURSELF*

Does it hang from a narrower stalk, is it soft, skin-coloured to light brown, and has it been there unchanged for months?

*WHAT IT IS*

A benign little outgrowth of skin and connective tissue, usually where skin rubs over skin. Harmless, and it does not go away on its own.

*WHAT WE DO*

Assess and then remove, usually in one appointment. We charge per quarter of an hour, so several small spots at once does not cost more each.

Benign, on a stalk, and unchanged. Usually done in one appointment, and charged per quarter of an hour so that several spots together do not work out dearer.

> knop: HAVE THIS LOOKED AT

Then this is not the place.

Assessing and removing pigmented spots belongs with a doctor, who can have the tissue examined. We do not remove them, not even when they bother you.

> knop: TO MOLES

**What helps and what we advise against**

With a skin tag the answer is usually short: if it is the right spot, it is done in one appointment.

**THIS WORKS**

- Assessing every spot before anything happens to it, even when you know exactly what you want

- Removing benign skin tags, usually in one appointment

- Charging per quarter of an hour, so that several small spots at once do not cost more each

- Referring to your GP with anything that is changing or is not clear

- Explaining why they sit in those places, because then you understand why new ones appear

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Removing something that is changing. That should be assessed by a doctor first

- Removing something that is changing. Then there is nothing left to examine

- Tying it off with thread or snipping it with nail scissors yourself. That goes well for a long time and once it does not

- Promising no new ones will ever appear. The predisposition and the friction stay

**What we use for this**

- Fibroma removal € 30 Removing skin tags, usually in one appointment. We charge the treatment time per quarter of an hour. WHAT IT INVOLVES

**Frequently asked questions**

Why do I get them on my neck and underarms?

In those places skin rubs over skin, and that is where these little outgrowths form. Clothing, a necklace or a bra strap speed it up. Predisposition plays a part too: in some people they come by the dozen.

Can I tie them off myself?

We would rather you did not, and that is not a sales argument. It goes well for a long time and once it does not, and that once is an infection in a neck or a scar on an eyelid. On top of that you would be cutting away something nobody has looked at.

Do they come back?

A removed skin tag does not come back, but new ones can form elsewhere. The predisposition and the friction are not changed by a treatment.

Is a scar left behind?

With a small skin tag usually a red dot that fades over weeks. The larger the base, the greater the chance that something stays visible. We discuss that beforehand per spot and not afterwards.

**Book a consultation at Diba Clinics**

With benign skin tags it is a short appointment, charged per quarter of an hour. If something among them turns out to need assessing, you hear that before we start.

### /en/skin-concerns/stretch-marks

**Tabbladtitel:** Treating stretch marks in Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Treating stretch marks with microneedling and laser. Red stretch marks respond best; with white ones we work on the texture.

**STRETCH MARKS TREATED**

The stage decides what is achievable. Red and purple stretch marks respond best; with white ones we work on the texture. At the intake the therapist establishes where you stand.

> knop: Read on

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

**What we look at**

Colour, age and relief together decide what there is to gain. The therapist goes through those three before a plan is made.

- The colour Red or purple means there is still blood flow in it and the tissue is young. White means it has matured.

- How long they have been there The therapist asks since when you have had them. With stretch marks after a pregnancy or a growth spurt that is usually easy to date.

- The relief Do they lie level with the skin or are they sunken? That decides whether we work on colour or on texture.

**Red or white**

Stretch marks go through two phases. Which of the two you have decides what a treatment gives and how quickly you need to act.

- STILL RED OR PURPLE, USUALLY RECENT Red or purple stretch marks STRIAE RUBRAE The skin has been stretched and the connective tissue beneath has torn. The red colour comes from the blood vessels still running through it. Microneedling and laser get collagen production going in tissue that still responds. This is the stage where the most gain sits. With red stretch marks there is room to improve colour and texture. How much, you hear after the assessment.

- WHITE OR SILVERY, OFTEN PRESENT FOR YEARS White stretch marks STRIAE ALBAE The tissue has matured. No active blood vessels run through it any more and it holds fewer pigment cells than the skin around it. Microneedling improves the texture and makes the stretch marks less noticeable to the touch. Bringing the colour back is not possible. With white stretch marks we work on texture and not on colour. You hear that beforehand, so you know what you are starting.

**What helps and what we advise against**

With stretch marks the moment counts for more than the technique. Start while they are still red and you keep the most room.

**THIS WORKS**

- Starting while they are still red or purple, because then there is something to gain

- With stretch marks in pregnancy, waiting until after breastfeeding, and then having them assessed

- Keeping the skin supple with care you can keep up

- Agreeing a series with a moment at which we look again

- Sun protection on the spot, because fresh tissue discolours faster

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Waiting until they are white. That is the point where the least is left

- Creams that promise white stretch marks will disappear. That does not happen, whatever the price

- A sunbed or sun on fresh stretch marks. It only makes the difference in colour larger

- Comparing in the mirror every week. Stretch marks change over months, not weeks

**What we use for this**

- Microneedling with the SkinPen € 180 Medically certified microneedling. It works on the layer where the structure of your skin sits. FOR THIS CONCERN WITH THE SKINPEN CIT MICRONEEDLING IN ROTTERDAM

- Dermapen 4 € 180 Microneedling with vibrating needles that pass through the skin evenly. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE DERMAPEN 4

- Fotona Scar Repair € 195 Laser on scars: acne scars, surgical scars and stretch marks. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER

**Frequently asked questions**

Do stretch marks ever go away completely?

No. What can happen is that they stand out less: less red, flatter and less noticeable to the touch. With red stretch marks there is more to gain than with white.

Why do I have them and my sister does not?

Predisposition plays the largest part. How quickly your skin stretches and how much elastin it holds differs per person. Stretch marks also occur in people who have never gained weight.

Can I have treatment during pregnancy?

No. We wait until after the birth and breastfeeding, and then assess again. By that point they have often already become lighter.

How many appointments do I need?

That depends on the stage and on how large the area is. At the intake you hear what is needed in your case and what it costs.

Does a cream help?

Good care keeps the skin supple and that is useful. The stretch marks themselves sit in the layer beneath, and a cream does not reach there.

**Book a consultation at Diba Clinics**

The therapist assesses which stage your stretch marks are in and what a series can give in your case. You hear straight away what to expect from it and what it costs.

### /en/skin-concerns/thread-veins

**Tabbladtitel:** Treating thread veins in Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Treating thread veins with IPL and laser. Red vessels on your cheeks or beside your nose, how to recognise them and what a treatment costs.

**COUPEROSE TREATED**

Those thin red or purple lines on your cheeks or beside your nose are called couperose. An even red haze is something else and asks for a different approach, even though the two often sit together. The skin therapist assesses under magnification which of the two you have.

We treat couperose with the Nordlys IPL and with laser. Our skin therapists work with these daily and set the device to your skin type and to the vessels that are there. How many sessions that takes you hear at the intake.

> knop: Read on

> knop: WHAT WE LOOK AT IN THE CONSULTATION

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

**Vessels or redness**

To the naked eye couperose and rosacea run into one another, and they ask for different approaches. This is how the skin therapist establishes what you are dealing with.

- Under magnification The skin therapist looks at the red patch magnified. Separate, branching lines look very different from an even haze, and to the naked eye the two are easily confused.

- With light pressure A brief press on the spot shows whether the red fades or whether a line stays put. That difference decides whether it is vessels or redness in the skin itself.

- Recorded in images The photo is taken under fixed lighting, so that we can compare at a following appointment. Redness varies by the day, so without fixed light you are mostly measuring the weather.

Did you see both? That is the most common outcome, and not some in-between form you have to sort out yourself. Below is what each of the two asks for.

**Which picture do you recognise?**

What the skin therapist sees decides which picture you end up with. With one of them it starts with light, with another it does not, and that difference is the whole point of this page.

- Separate red lines Thin red or purple threads on your cheeks or beside your nose

- A red flush A haze of red across your cheeks, without separate lines

- Both mixed together A red background with a few clear lines in it

*UNDER LIGHT PRESSURE*

The line stays visible while you press. The blood will not be pushed out of it.

*WHAT IT MEANS*

A blood vessel that has been permanently stretched. Such a vessel no longer closes by itself, and it sits beneath the epidermis, where skincare products do not reach.

*WHAT WE DO FIRST*

Here light gives the most. We first record how much is visible, so that after a few sessions you can see the difference rather than having to estimate it.

Many people call this a burst vein. Nothing has burst: the vessel has been stretched and stands open. That sounds like a detail, but it changes what can be done about it.

> knop: HAVE THIS LOOKED AT

**Couperose or rosacea?**

They often go together and are therefore mixed up, by our profession too. Four differences you can check yourself before you book anything.

*Under light pressure*

If a line stays put, it is couperose. If everything fades, it is a flush.

*Flare-ups*

With rosacea it comes and goes in attacks. Separate vessels are there the same every day.

*A burning feeling*

This can fit rosacea; a widened vessel is usually not something you feel.

*Bumps*

Red bumps without blackheads point to rosacea, and a doctor belongs with that.

Then this is not your page, and we would rather say so now.

Flare-ups after heat or wine, a burning feeling, bumps without blackheads: that points to rosacea. A different conversation belongs with that, and sometimes a doctor.

> knop: TO THE ROSACEA PAGE

**What helps and what we advise against**

With couperose the list is shorter than with most skin concerns, and that is not modesty. There is one thing that works on a vessel that is already visible, and there is a lot that does nothing to it.

**THIS WORKS**

- Recording beforehand how many vessels are visible, under fixed light, so that you can compare later

- Targeted light on the vessels that stay put under pressure, spread over several sessions

- Sun protection every day. UV stretches vessel walls further and is the main reason new ones appear

- Working out what brings the flush on, because as long as it keeps coming back new vessels keep forming

- Saying beforehand when one session is probably enough and when you should count on a series

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Scrubbing or brushing hard. It makes your skin redder while the vessels stay where they are

- A hot shower or the sauna right after a vessel treatment, because heat can bring the redness back up

- Presenting camouflage as treatment. Green concealer makes redness less visible and leaves the vessels as they are

- A cream that promises to make vessels disappear. A stretched vessel lies beneath the epidermis, out of reach of anything you rub on top

- Starting on tanned skin

**Vessels can be counted.**

That sounds small, but it is why with this concern you do not have to believe that it worked. The EVE-M records the vessel structure under fixed light, before the first session.

After the series we put the two images side by side. If you see no difference yourself, that is the answer and we do not carry on just because a package still had sessions left in it.

> knop: MORE ABOUT THE SKIN ANALYSIS

WHAT WE MEASURE HERE

*Vessel structure*

How many visible lines there are and how they run

The base colour of the skin, apart from the separate vessels

*Sensitivity*

How quickly your skin reacts, because that decides the setting

Every axis is measured again at each check-up, under the same lighting. That way a difference later is something you see rather than something you have to take on faith.

**What we use for this**

- Nordlys IPL for redness and vessels € 75 Light on visible vessels, rosacea and lasting redness. The vessel darkens and then fades. FOR THIS CONCERN WITH THE NORDLYS IPL TREATMENT IN ROTTERDAM

- LED therapy € 30 Light that calms the skin. In several wavelengths, without needles or acids. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE PRECISION PHOTONIC SYSTEM

**Frequently asked questions**

Do those vessels come back after the treatment?

A vessel that has been closed stays closed. What does happen is that new ones can appear over time, because your predisposition and the things that set your skin off are not changed by a treatment. So we pay as much attention to what brings the redness on as to what is visible now.

Is couperose the same as rosacea?

They often go together, but they are not the same. Couperose is the visible, permanently stretched vessels. Rosacea is an inflammatory picture with flare-ups, sometimes bumps and a burning feeling. You can have the vessels without rosacea, and rosacea without visible vessels. If you recognise more than the lines alone, read on at the rosacea page.

Do I get this from alcohol?

Alcohol opens the vessels wide and can trigger a flare-up, but it does not explain the predisposition. That stubborn association mainly makes people ashamed of something they could do little about.

Can I keep wearing make-up?

Yes, between sessions too. We only ask you to leave your skin clean on the day of the treatment itself.

What does a treatment cost?

A vessel treatment with the Nordlys starts at 75 euros for a small area. What it comes to for you depends on how large the area is and how many sessions are needed; you hear that after the first appointment. All rates are on the price page.

**First we count how much is visible**

The skin consultation records what is visible now. After that you know how many sessions are needed, and so do we.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

### /en/skin-concerns/wrinkles

**Tabbladtitel:** Treating wrinkles in Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Treating wrinkles and fine lines with microneedling, laser and peels that get collagen production going.

**LINES AND FINE WRINKLES**

We treat lines and fine wrinkles with microneedling, laser and peels. These get collagen production going, which makes the skin firmer and the lines shallower.

A line can sit in your skin or in the muscle beneath it. The therapist establishes which of the two it is, because that decides what works.

> knop: Read on

> knop: WHICH LINE DO YOU HAVE

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

**Skin or muscle**

A line in the muscle and a line in the skin look the same and ask for different things. The therapist looks at rest and in movement.

- At rest first The therapist looks at your face at complete rest. The lines that are there then are in your skin; they do not disappear when you sit still.

- Then in movement Smiling, frowning, eyebrows up. The lines that appear only then come from the muscle beneath, and not from the skin itself.

- Why that difference counts A line in the skin we treat with microneedling, laser or a peel. A line in the muscle asks for something else; we do not work with that.

Then you are looking wider than this page.

With skin ageing, pigment, texture, elasticity and laxity run into each other. If that is what you are dealing with, the wider page is the better way in.

> knop: TO SKIN AGEING

**Four kinds of lines**

Four kinds of line that look the same. Whether a line sits in the skin or in the muscle decides which treatment works.

- Dehydration lines Fine lines that are there in the morning and less so later

- Expression lines Lines you see when you smile or frown, and not otherwise

- Lines that stay put Lines that are there even when your face is at rest

- Laxity Your face drops and the contour of your jawline gets vaguer

*HOW YOU RECOGNISE IT*

They disappear once you take proper care of your skin, and they differ by the day and by the season.

*WHAT IT IS*

Not a wrinkle but skin short of moisture. The top layer does not lie smooth and catches light in small lines.

*WHAT WE DO*

Often nothing drastic. Repair the barrier and hydrate, then look again. This is the picture where people most often buy too much.

This works on the skin, and that is what we do. Count on a series over months rather than on a single session.

> knop: HAVE THIS LOOKED AT

**What helps and what we advise against**

With lines the gain sits in the right choice and in patience. Collagen builds over months, and coming more often does not speed that up.

**THIS WORKS**

- Establishing first whether the line sits in the skin or in the muscle, because those two ask for different things

- Getting collagen building going, in a series over months rather than in one session

- Sun protection, every day. This is by far the biggest factor in how quickly new lines appear

- A skin analysis, because with this concern it takes months and you see your own face every day

- Saying when care gives more than a treatment

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Injectables. We do not work with them, and for some lines that is exactly the logical route

- Promising that lines disappear. Shallower and less visible is realistic

- Starting a series for lines caused by dryness. Those go with care

- Treating skin that has truly let go as though it were laxity. That is surgery

- Starting on tanned skin

**Why we record it beforehand**

With lines it takes months, and in those months you see yourself every day. So you barely notice a gradual change, in either direction. The EVE-M records your skin under fixed light and from a fixed angle.

That makes the difference visible later rather than something you have to believe. And it works the other way too: if little has changed after a series, that is a reason to do something else and not to carry on.

> knop: MORE ABOUT THE SKIN ANALYSIS

WHAT WE MEASURE HERE

*Texture*

How fine or coarse the surface of your skin is

*Elasticity*

How quickly the skin springs back, and where it no longer does

*Sun damage*

What has already built up beneath the surface

Every axis is measured again at each check-up, under the same lighting. That way a difference later is something you see rather than something you have to take on faith.

**What we use for this**

- Microneedling with the SkinPen € 180 Medically certified microneedling. It works on the layer where the structure of your skin sits. FOR THIS CONCERN WITH THE SKINPEN CIT MICRONEEDLING IN ROTTERDAM

- Dermapen 4 € 180 Microneedling with vibrating needles that pass through the skin evenly. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE DERMAPEN 4

- Skin boosters and mesotherapy € 175 Active ingredients placed into the skin rather than onto it, at a fixed depth per injection. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE U225 INTRADERMAL INJECTOR SKIN BOOSTERS IN ROTTERDAM

- RRS Eyes € 130 Active ingredients around the eye contour. For dark circles, fine lines and a tired look. WHAT IT INVOLVES

- Fotona TimeWalker € 150 Fifteen treatments on one device, from a light laser peel to the complete 4D. Each with its own purpose. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER FOTONA 4D IN ROTTERDAM

- Fotona 4D € 370 Four laser treatments in one session. From the inside through the cheek to a closing peel. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER

- SmoothLiftin On request Collagen stimulation from the inside, through the lining of your cheek. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER

- SmoothEye € 150 Laser around the eye contour, for crow's feet and fine lines. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER

- LipLase € 150 Fuller, smoother lips without filler, with laser from inside and out. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER

- VectorLift € 150 A laser brow lift and firming of the forehead, without needles. WHAT IT INVOLVES WITH THE FOTONA TIMEWALKER

- Eye peel € 30 A peel that is allowed on the eye contour. For fine lines and a dull, dark eye area. WHAT IT INVOLVES

**Frequently asked questions**

How do I know whether it is a wrinkle or a dehydration line?

Look at different moments over a week. A dehydration line changes with the day, the season and your care; a real wrinkle is there the same every morning.

Do you do botox?

No. We work on the skin and not on the muscle. For a line that is only visible in movement an injectable is often the logical route, and then we would rather refer you on than sell you a series that changes little about it.

At what age should I start with this?

There is no age. What does matter is whether there is anything to gain: on skin that is still firm a series gives little, and then sun protection is the whole treatment.

How long before I see something?

Collagen building is a matter of months rather than weeks. So we measure beforehand: over that stretch your own impression is not a reliable measure.

**See progress instead of guessing**

With lines it takes months, and you see your own face every day. The skin analysis records under fixed lighting where you started, so that at a following appointment you see the difference side by side.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

### /en/snoring

**Tabbladtitel:** Treating snoring with laser in Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Snoring rarely starts in the throat alone. First look at where the sound comes from, only then whether NightLase gives you anything.

**SNORING THAT DISTURBS YOUR NIGHTS**

There is a laser treatment that tightens the soft palate, and we are good at it. But it only works if the sound starts there. If it is in your nose, your tongue or the position of your jaw, it gives nothing, and you would rather hear that now than after three sessions.

So this page starts with the source and not with the device.

> knop: WHERE DOES YOUR SOUND COME FROM?

> knop: RATHER ASK A QUESTION FIRST

Laser on the soft palate, with no cutting and no mouthguard.

*HOW LONG*

30 minutes

*HOW OFTEN*

A series of three, with about three weeks in between.

*RECOVERY*

After NightLase you can eat and talk normally.

Whether this works for you depends on where the sound starts. We establish that at the intake.

**Four places where snoring can start**

This is a signpost and not a diagnosis; the real answer comes from looking at the back of your mouth. But the recognition below already brings most people to the right door, and sometimes that is not ours.

- The soft palate THIS ONE IS OURS HOW YOU NOTICE IT A low, rattling sound with your mouth open. Often worse on your back and after a glass of wine. WHAT IT MEANS The slack tissue at the back of your mouth vibrates with the airflow. This is the most common source and the only one a laser changes anything about. WHAT WE DO Here NightLase makes sense. We first look at the back of your mouth and then agree a series.

- Your nose NOT HERE HOW YOU NOTICE IT You sleep with your mouth open because your nose is blocked, or you snore mostly during a cold or hay-fever season. WHAT IT MEANS A blocked or crooked nose forces you to breathe through your mouth, and only then does the palate start vibrating. The cause then lies a good deal earlier. WHAT WE DO We do not start here. This belongs with your GP or an ENT specialist, and they can often do more about it than we can.

- Your tongue NOT HERE HOW YOU NOTICE IT Only on your back, with a deeper and more irregular sound. On your side it is often gone. WHAT IT MEANS The tongue slides back in your sleep and narrows the airway. That is a different mechanism from a vibrating palate. WHAT WE DO Here we say honestly that a laser on the palate changes little. There are other solutions, and they lie outside this clinic.

- Your jaw position or teeth NOT HERE HOW YOU NOTICE IT Your lower jaw sits back, or you already wear a brace or an anti-snoring mouthguard. WHAT IT MEANS The space at the back of your throat is then smaller than average, however tight the palate is. WHAT WE DO This belongs with the dentist or orthodontist. Sometimes it does combine with NightLase, and then we discuss it together.

**Snoring is not the same as apnoea.**

Snoring is sound. With sleep apnoea your breathing briefly stops during sleep, and that is a medical problem with consequences for your heart and your blood pressure. They often occur together.

Making the sound quieter while breathing pauses sit underneath it is switching off the alarm and leaving the problem in place. So we always ask about it, and so this is here and not at the bottom.

> knop: Read on

DO YOU RECOGNISE ANY OF THIS?

- Your partner hears you stop breathing in your sleep

- You wake up feeling as though you are gasping for air

- You are unusually sleepy during the day, even after a full night

- You often have a headache in the morning

- You have high blood pressure or a heart condition

One yes is enough to start with your GP first. A sleep study belongs with that, and a doctor arranges it, not us. If nothing comes of it, you can always come back.

**How NightLase**

If the sound comes from your soft palate, this is what we can do. No cutting, no needles, and nothing you have to put in at night.

- STEP 1 Look first at where the sound sits Not every snoring sound comes from the soft palate. That decides whether this gives you anything.

- STEP 2 Pulses on the palate In a fixed pattern across the tissue, in about half an hour. You are sitting up and fully conscious.

- STEP 3 Three times, with weeks in between The tissue tightens between sessions. After the third you know what it does for you.

*HOW LONG IT TAKES YOU*

A series of three, with about three weeks in between. The effect builds across that series and is not permanent; repeating after a while belongs with it.

*WHAT YOU NOTICE AFTERWARDS*

After NightLase you can eat and talk normally. Some people feel a slight scratching in the throat for a while.

NIGHTLASE, ON THE SOFT PALATE

**We treat snoring with NightLase**

Laser against snoring. The soft palate becomes firmer, with no surgery and no mouthguard.

*PER SESSION*

On request

> knop: EVERYTHING ABOUT NIGHTLASE

**What helps and what we advise against**

With snoring the value sits mostly in what does not happen. Half the people who call about this hear from us that they should start somewhere else.

**THIS WORKS**

- Looking first at where the sound comes from, because that decides whether this gives you anything

- Referring to your GP if there is even one warning sign, even when you are already standing here

- NightLase as a series of three, with agreed moments beforehand to see whether it is working

- Saying honestly that the effect is not permanent and that repeating belongs with it

- Weighing what else plays a part: weight, alcohol before bed, sleeping position

**WE ADVISE AGAINST THIS**

- Starting without knowing where the sound sits. Then you are selling a series and not a solution

- Treating on a suspicion of sleep apnoea. A sleep study comes first there

- Promising the snoring disappears completely. Less is realistic, gone is not always

- Selling a nasal spray or a mouthguard alongside the treatment. That is not our trade

**Frequently asked questions**

Where does the sound actually come from?

From tissue vibrating with your breathing. In your sleep the muscles in your throat relax, so that the soft palate and the uvula flutter on the airflow. The narrower the passage, the louder the sound.

Is snoring the same as sleep apnoea?

No. Snoring is sound; sleep apnoea is your breathing briefly stopping during sleep. They often occur together, which is why we always ask about it. If there is a suspicion, a sleep study comes first and we do not start.

Do I need a general anaesthetic for NightLase?

No, and there is no cutting either. You are sitting up, fully conscious, and you walk out yourself afterwards.

How many sessions do I need?

Usually three, with about three weeks in between. The effect builds across that series; after the first session there is rarely anything to hear yet.

Does it stay away?

Not on its own. The tissue gives way again after a while, and then a repeat is needed. So we do not call it permanent, and you hear beforehand that a repeat belongs with it.

What does this cost?

The rate for NightLase is on the price page as soon as it is settled.

**Book a consultation at Diba Clinics**

In the first conversation we look at where the sound starts and ask about your nights. After that you know whether this gives you anything, and so do we.

### /en/team

**Tabbladtitel:** Our team | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** The 11 people who work at Diba Clinics, with each person's field and whether their title is protected by law.

**THE PEOPLE WHO TREAT YOUR SKIN**

With every device on this site stands the same sentence: two clinics with the same device do not give the same result, because what counts is the setting and the hand that holds it.

That is easily said. Here is whose hand that is.

*Skin therapists*

*Orthomolecular skin specialists*

*Laser specialists*

You do not choose who you see yourself. That follows from your question, and if you have a preference you can simply say so.

**The difference in training**

Who treats your skin and who looks at what plays a part from within are two different trainings. That way you know who stands beside you for which question.

- Skin therapist PROTECTED TITLE Works with the devices and the treatments: laser, light, needling, peels. Judges what your skin can take and tunes the settings to it. A bachelor's degree in skin therapy, at The Hague University of Applied Sciences or HU Utrecht. The title is protected in article 34 of the Individual Healthcare Professions Act, and our skin therapists are listed in the Dutch Quality Register for Paramedics.

- Orthomolecular skin specialist Looks at what plays a part from within: food, hormones, digestion. With acne and pigment that is often half the story. An additional training alongside skin therapy or beauty therapy, focused on food, hormones and digestion. The title is not in the Individual Healthcare Professions Act, so always ask about the training behind it.

- Laser specialist Works with the laser and light equipment: hair removal, and light aimed at colour or vessels. Chooses the setting per skin type and per area. A vocational training on the equipment itself, with certification per device. Not a protected title, so ask about the training behind it; our laser specialists work under the same protocols as the skin therapists.

- Andres SKIN THERAPIST

- Iris SKIN THERAPIST

- Griselle SKIN THERAPIST

- C PHOTO TO FOLLOW Cheyenne SKIN THERAPIST

- A PHOTO TO FOLLOW Anouk SKIN THERAPIST

- Rojda FOUNDER OF DIBA CLINICS B.V. AND ORTHOMOLECULAR SKIN SPECIALIST

- Demi ORTHOMOLECULAR SKIN SPECIALIST

- India SKIN THERAPIST IN TRAINING AND LASER SPECIALIST

- E PHOTO TO FOLLOW Elaf LASER SPECIALIST

- Y PHOTO TO FOLLOW Yasin IT AND MARKETING

- O PHOTO TO FOLLOW Okan PRACTICE MANAGER

A diploma is not an end point.

Skin therapists can register in the Dutch Quality Register for Paramedics. A voluntary register with a five-year cycle. Anyone who stays in it demonstrates at least 1600 working hours per period, spread over at least 36 months, and 160 points of continuing education.

The register is voluntary, so being in it says something and not being in it says little. Which of us is in it we will state as soon as we have checked it per person; a claim about that should be verified and not assumed.

### /en/terms

**Tabbladtitel:** Terms and conditions | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** What happens if you cancel, arrive late, or if a treatment cannot go ahead. Per situation what it costs and why the rule is there.

**TERMS AND CONDITIONS**

You are probably here because something is up. You have to cancel, you are late, or you have seen an amount you did not expect. So below are situations and not articles.

With every situation it says what it costs and why the rule is there. The latter is the difference between a condition and a fine.

> knop: Read on

Up to 48 hours beforehand, cancelling costs you nothing, and you do not have to give a reason.

After that a part of the rate is charged, because the slot can no longer be filled. Every other rule on this page is a variation on that one.

**What a treatment costs**

- You cancel or reschedule in time Up to 48 hours before your appointment you can cancel or reschedule, by phone or message. You do not have to give a reason. WHAT IT COSTS Nothing. Your deposit is not lost and moves to the new appointment. WHY THIS RULE Within 48 hours we can usually still give the slot to someone else. Beyond that we cannot, and that is the only difference between this rule and the next.

- You cancel too late or do not come If you cancel less than 48 hours before your appointment, or do not turn up without a message, your deposit is lost. For a new appointment we ask for a deposit again. WHAT IT COSTS Only the deposit. Not the full rate and not a percentage of the reserved treatment either. WHY THIS RULE The time was reserved and the therapist was ready. It stays at the deposit because the aim is that a slot does not stay empty, and not that money is made from someone who was not there.

- You are late If you are more than 15 minutes late, the treatment may no longer fit safely into the reserved time. If it can be done safely we shorten it; if not, we reschedule the appointment. WHAT IT COSTS If it is shortened the full treatment price applies, because the time was reserved for you. If the appointment has to be rescheduled, the deposit is lost. WHY THIS RULE Otherwise the next appointment shifts along, and then someone else pays for something they had no part in. Half-treating because the clock says so is the other option, and it is worse.

- We have to cancel If an appointment cannot go ahead from our side, you hear that as soon as we know ourselves and we find a new date together. WHAT IT COSTS Nothing. Your deposit stays for the new appointment or you get it back. WHY THIS RULE The same rule as above, but our way round. A condition that works in only one direction is not an agreement.

- You buy a programme in advance Prepaid sessions remain valid for 12 months from the date of purchase. WHAT IT COSTS Unused sessions can be booked within that period or refunded. WHY THIS RULE The intervals affect the result, so a programme is meant to be completed according to plan. The period supports that and is not there to make sessions expire.

- When you pay You pay in the clinic itself. The deposit you paid when booking is set off against the total. WHAT IT COSTS The amount that was on the site beforehand. Never more than that. WHY THIS RULE All rates are public, per session and per area. What you pay is what was stated, and nothing is added at the desk.

- You are not satisfied Let us know, preferably as soon as possible. We look together at what happened and what a fitting next step is. WHAT IT COSTS Nothing to discuss it. WHY THIS RULE Nobody can honestly guarantee a result. What we do is take our explanation, our agreements and our responsibility seriously. If something about what you were told beforehand is not right, that is our mistake and we handle it as such.

**Three things that never change.**

These are not provisions but commitments. They are here so that they count too when you take the conditions out.

- The price on the site is the price All rates are public, per session and per version. There are no discounts, promo codes or temporary offers, so there is never a moment when you were too early or too late.

- No result is guaranteed How your skin responds differs per person. What we do is measure beforehand, so that afterwards there is something to compare rather than something to feel.

- Saying no is allowed, from both sides If a treatment does not suit your skin or the moment, it does not go ahead. That can also become clear on the day itself, and then it costs you nothing.

**What is not here yet.**

A section on liability. That wording is legal work and should come from a lawyer, not from us. As long as it is not here, we make no half-statement about it either: then at least you know it is missing rather than reading something that is no use to you.

The periods and amounts on this page are still a proposal in this version too. What was agreed at your appointment and what is on your confirmation takes precedence over what is written here.

If you have a question about these conditions, just ask it. Diba Clinics can be reached on 010-2038423 and via WhatsApp.
