**Tabbladtitel:** Which skin treatment suits me? | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Not sure which skin treatment you need? Book a treatment on advice. For new clients with an intake and for existing clients without a new one.

**I WANT A TREATMENT ON ADVICE**

You know what you want to improve about your skin, but not whether a peel, a laser treatment, microneedling or something else fits. You do not have to work that out yourself.

Tell us what is bothering you. The therapist looks at your skin, discusses what is possible and gives clear advice. Only once you know which treatment is proposed, why and what it costs do you decide whether to have it done.

> knop: Read on

> knop: BOOK A TREATMENT ON ADVICE

> knop: NEW OR ALREADY A CLIENT?

THE CONVERSATION EVERY ADVICE APPOINTMENT STARTS WITH

**New to us or been here before**

Intake plus treatment on advice

120 MINUTES RESERVED

We reserve 120 minutes, so two hours. Of that, the intake takes 30 to 60 minutes, depending on what there is to discuss: your question, your medical background, your skincare products and earlier treatments. Then the therapist looks at your skin. At least an hour always remains to treat. We only do a skin measurement when it adds something.

AFTER THAT YOU HEAR

- which treatment we advise

- why it suits your skin

- what you can expect from it

- how many treatments may be needed

- which recovery time and aftercare belong with it

If treating is safe at that moment, fits within the time and you want to go ahead? Then it usually happens straight away.

You then pay only for the treatment; the intake fee is waived. If no treatment happens, the intake costs € 50. The appointment does not have to fill the 120 minutes.

> knop: BOOK AS A NEW CLIENT

Treatment on advice

60 MINUTES RESERVED

You do not have to book a new intake, so this appointment takes 60 minutes. The therapist takes out your file, discusses what has changed since your last appointment and assesses your skin as it is now.

Then you get a treatment recommendation. Beforehand you hear which treatment it will be and what it costs.

You pay only for the treatment actually carried out. No separate intake fee is charged.

Is it an entirely new question, or is further investigation needed? Then the therapist may advise scheduling the treatment for a later moment.

> knop: BOOK AS AN EXISTING CLIENT

**You do not have to know the name**

It is enough that you can say what bothers you, what you want to improve and how much recovery time is workable for you.

- acne, blackheads or unsettled skin

- pigment spots or an uneven complexion

- redness, rosacea or visible vessels

- scars, coarse pores or an irregular skin texture

- fine lines, skin laxity or general skin improvement

- unwanted hair growth or ingrown hairs

- hair loss or scalp complaints

- a combination of different skin concerns

- a skin wish where you do not know which treatment fits

Is your question not among them? Describe it briefly when booking, so that we know beforehand how much time and which room we need.

**Four steps from question to treatment**

- STEP 1 You say what you want to improve A few short questions beforehand. You do not have to choose a treatment: we want to know what is bothering you and what you have already tried.

- STEP 2 The therapist assesses your skin We look at your skin, your question and everything that touches a safe treatment: medication, skincare products, earlier reactions and sun.

- STEP 3 You get clear advice Which treatment fits best, why, and what the alternatives are. Sometimes the most honest advice is to wait or to do nothing.

- STEP 4 Treating when it is safe If it fits within the reserved time and you agree with the advice and the price, it can happen straight away. If not, we schedule it together.

**What people asked about this.**

**Do I have to choose a treatment beforehand?**

No. This appointment is meant precisely for people who do not know which treatment fits best. It is enough that you can say what bothers you.

**Am I always treated straight away?**

Not automatically. We only treat if it is safe at that moment, if it fits within the reserved time and if you agree with the advice and the price.

**Does a skin scanner decide which treatment I get?**

No. The therapist decides what is appropriate based on your skin, your question and your medical background. A skin measurement supports that judgement when it adds something.

**Can I say what I do and do not want?**

Yes. The advice comes from the therapist, but the choice is made together. Nothing is carried out without your consent.

**What do I pay?**

If you are new, you pay for the treatment that is carried out and the intake fee is waived. If no treatment happens, the intake costs € 50. If you are already a client, you pay only for the treatment carried out. You always hear the price before we start.

**Tell us what bothers you. We will work out the rest.**

The advice comes from the therapist, the choice is made together, and nothing happens without your knowing what it is and what it costs.

**Tabbladtitel:** Acne programme: a guided course for acne | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** A guided programme for acne: treatments at the clinic, products and check-ups at home. Rate € 570, 60 minutes. At Diba Clinics in Rotterdam.

**ACNE PROGRAMME**

ACNE PROGRAMME, BLEMIDERM

*HOW DEEP*

Epidermis

60 minutes

Varies per phase of the programme.

A guided programme for acne: treatments at the clinic, products and check-ups at home.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

**Where it lands**

A programme instead of separate treatments, because acne changes over weeks and does not arise at a moment. It starts with a measurement and a schedule for home; then treatments in the clinic follow with a check-up every four to six weeks in which the schedule is adjusted. It ends with tapering down to what you keep up yourself.

- Stratum corneum The outer layer of dead cells. What happens here shows quickly and heals quickly. IT WORKS HERE

- Epidermis Where your pigment sits and where new skin cells come from. IT WORKS HERE

- Upper dermis This is where the connective tissue starts. What you reach here heals by building. DOES NOT REACH HERE

- Deep dermis Hair roots, vessels and the firmness of your skin. Working this deep needs a reason. DOES NOT REACH HERE

**What happens, in order.**

Every treatment starts with cleansing, and that is done by hand. Make-up and sebum come off and the therapist checks that everything is gone, because a device or an active ingredient that works on a layer never reaches your skin.

- Measurement beforehand We look at where it sits, which type it is and how your skin is doing now.

- Treating and adjusting Sessions in the clinic with products at home, and at every check-up seeing whether the schedule holds.

- Afbouwen A programme ends with what you keep up yourself. Otherwise it comes back and everything starts again.

ACNE PROGRAMME, DURING THE TREATMENT

**What you notice in the chair**

The programme starts with a measurement and a conversation, not with a treatment. What comes out of that decides the order, and that order is the heart of it: inflammation first, scars later, never at the same time.

After that you see us at set intervals. Every appointment is part treatment and part check-up, and at every check-up a new measurement is taken under the same lighting.

Between appointments you care for your skin yourself, with the products and the schedule you are given. That decides a large part of the result.

**What this treatment is meant for**

On the left where this treatment works well, on the right when another treatment does more for you.

- Follows the course of acne rather than picking out one moment

- Combines treatments in the clinic with products and check-ups at home

- Records at every check-up what has changed, so that you do not compare from memory

- Acne has a course, so we do not agree an end date beforehand

- With severe or scarring acne a doctor looks first

- Most of it happens at home, so the products belong to the programme

Three to six months, with a check-up every four to six weeks. Where you fall within that range depends on the type of acne and on how your skin responds, and you hear that after the measurement.

The rate covers the treatments in the clinic, the check-ups and the products for home. What it does not cover is separate treatments you want in between, and those are simply listed on the price page.

A single treatment for skin with spots and blockages, without starting a programme. Every treatment starts with cleansing, and that is done by hand. Make-up and sebum come off and the therapist checks that everything is gone, because a device or an active ingredient that works on a layer never reaches your skin.

- Seeing what is there Blockages, inflammation or both. That decides what happens in that appointment.

- Cleansing and emptying Thorough cleansing and emptying the blocked pores sterilely and at the right pressure.

The therapist first looks at what is there: blockages, inflammation or both. That decides what happens in that appointment and what is left alone instead.

Afterwards your skin is calm and slightly red for a few hours. You go home with advice about what to put on your face in the days after, and what not.

- With severe, inflamed acne with lumps a doctor looks first

- Does nothing about scars that are already there; those come up once the skin is calm

COSMELAN, MESOESTETIC

Epidermis

A six-month programme against hyperpigmentation, with a mask at the clinic and products at home.

The difference from Dermamelan, when it is best to start and what the programme costs with us is on Cosmelan and Dermamelan in Rotterdam.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

**Where it lands**

Cosmelan starts with two weeks of preparation at home, then the mask goes on in the clinic and a fixed routine of months follows. It slows the production of pigment instead of only removing what is there, and that is why it runs so long. Sun, hormones and genes all help decide why pigment arises; so the work at home is not a side issue but the largest part of the programme.

This runs on Peel lines

- Stratum corneum to 0.02 mm Dead cells and lipids. The water barrier.

- Epidermis to 0.1 mm Pigment cells and the dividing layer that new skin comes from.

- Upper dermis to 0.5 mm Fine vessels, nerve endings and young collagen.

- Deep dermis to 2 mm Hair roots, sebaceous glands, larger vessels and the supporting collagen.

- Stratum corneumto 0.02 mmDead cells and lipids. The water barrier.

- Epidermisto 0.1 mmPigment cells and the dividing layer that new skin comes from.

- Upper dermisto 0.5 mmFine vessels, nerve endings and young collagen.

- Deep dermisto 2 mmHair roots, sebaceous glands, larger vessels and the supporting collagen.

The proportions are schematic; the depths beside them are not. Usual values for facial skin. The thickness differs per place on the body; on the back the dermis is a multiple of this. How deep we work in your case depends on the setting the therapist chooses.

WHAT HAPPENS

- 1 Choosing a strength Three levels. Which one fits depends on your skin today.

- 2 Working time The working time is measured against your skin. Leaving it on longer gives no better result.

- 3 Peeling The loosened layer comes away over days and is replaced faster.

The stratum corneum

- Deep dermis Hair roots, vessels and the firmness of your skin. Working this deep needs a reason. DOES NOT REACH HERE

Every treatment starts with cleansing, and that is done by hand. Make-up and sebum come off and the therapist checks that everything is gone, because a device or an active ingredient that works on a layer never reaches your skin.

**What you notice in the chair**

The first appointment is short. A mask goes on your face that you take home yourself and remove at home, after the number of hours you are given. That number is not a guideline but an agreement.

The weeks after, you do the work. You are given products with a schedule, and following that schedule decides the outcome more than what happens in the clinic does.

After a few days you start peeling. So we agree beforehand when you start, so that it does not coincide with a holiday or a busy week.

**What this treatment is meant for**

On the left where this treatment works well, on the right when another treatment does more for you.

- Carries on at home, because most of this programme happens outside the clinic

- The homework is part of it; without that part the programme stalls

- Sun brings pigment back, so protection stays part of the plan

- For melasma, Dermamelan is usually the heavier and fitter choice

A microneedling device that makes microscopically small channels in the skin with minute, vibrating needles to stimulate the natural healing process. That stimulates collagen production, making the skin firmer, smoother and more even. Works on fine lines, acne scars, coarse pores and dull skin.

This runs on Dermapen 4

- Upper dermis to 0.5 mm Fine vessels, nerve endings and young collagen.

- Deep dermis to 2 mm Hair roots, sebaceous glands, larger vessels and the supporting collagen.

WHAT HAPPENS

- 1 Depth per area Around the eyes the skin is thinner than on the cheek. The setting follows.

- 2 Vibrating needles The needles move vertically, which tears the tissue less than dragging.

Connective tissue

The scaffolding of your skin. What you prompt here repairs by building.

It runs on its own. Click a step to steer it yourself.

**What happens, in order.**

Every treatment starts with cleansing, and that is done by hand. Make-up and sebum come off and the therapist checks that everything is gone, because a device or an active ingredient that works on a layer never reaches your skin.

- Numbing cream It takes half an hour to work. Without it, it is too sharp; with it, it is manageable.

- The work itself Per area, at a fixed depth setting. You hear the device more than you feel it.

- Red on the way home One to three days, as though you had sat too long in the sun. No make-up on the first day.

DERMAPEN 4, DURING THE TREATMENT

**What you notice in the chair**

The same course as with the SkinPen: numbing cream, half an hour of waiting, and then the pen in strips across the area. The Dermapen works faster, so a section is finished sooner.

The depth is adjusted per area. Around your eyes and on your forehead it goes shallower than on your cheeks, and you notice that: the deeper it goes, the more pressure you feel.

Afterwards the same rules apply. One to three days red, leave it alone the first day, and do not skip sun protection after that.

**What this treatment is meant for**

On the left where this treatment works well, on the right when another treatment does more for you.

- Makes channels in the skin that get your own repair going

- Works on fine lines, acne scars, coarse pores, dull skin and pigment left behind after inflammation

- Passes through the skin more evenly with vibrating needles than with a rolling motion

- What you see after one time is swelling; the result comes across the series

- Deep or tethered scars need a combination with laser

- With active inflammation we treat the inflammation first and the texture after

### /en/treatments/electrolysis

**Tabbladtitel:** Electrolysis: grey and blond hair too | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Hair by hair, grey and blond included. For what the laser cannot see. We charge the treatment time per half hour. Rate € 60, 30 minutes.

**ELECTROLYSIS**

*HOW DEEP*

Upper dermis

*HOW LONG*

30 minutes

*RECOVERY*

The treated spots are red for a few hours and can swell slightly, much like after waxing.

*HOW OFTEN*

A series, with a few weeks in between.

Hair by hair, grey and blond included. For what the laser cannot see. We charge the treatment time per half hour.

What electrolysis costs with us, why the laser cannot see grey hair and how it works alongside laser is on Electrolysis in Rotterdam.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

**Where it lands**

The laser aims at the pigment in the hair root. If there is no pigment there, there is nothing to aim at; that is why grey, white and very light blond hair does not respond to laser. In electrolysis a thin needle goes into the hair canal alongside the hair and the root itself gets a short burst of current. Colour then does not matter. It goes hair by hair, so it is slower than laser and it is meant for small areas.

- Stratum corneum The outer layer of dead cells. What happens here shows quickly and heals quickly. PASSES THROUGH HERE

- Epidermis Where your pigment sits and where new skin cells come from. IT WORKS HERE

- Upper dermis This is where the connective tissue starts. What you reach here heals by building. IT WORKS HERE

- Deep dermis Hair roots, vessels and the firmness of your skin. Working this deep needs a reason. DOES NOT REACH HERE

**What happens, in order.**

Every treatment starts with cleansing, and that is done by hand. Make-up and sebum come off and the therapist checks that everything is gone, because a device or an active ingredient that works on a layer never reaches your skin.

- Checking first whether laser is possible If there is pigment in the hairs, laser is faster and cheaper. This is for what is left afterwards.

- Hair by hair A fine needle follows the follicle down to the root. Per hair you feel a short prick.

- In a series A hair only responds in its growth phase, so more appointments follow with weeks in between.

**What electrolysis is meant for**

On the left where this treatment works well, on the right when another treatment does more for you.

- Works whatever the hair colour, so on grey, white and very light blond hair too

- Suits the odd hairs left after a laser course

- Works on small areas where precision matters more than speed, such as chin, upper lip and around the eyebrow

- Is not meant for large areas such as legs or back; laser hair removal is faster and better value there

- Goes hair by hair, so a full area takes more sessions and more time than laser

- Asks for patience: the result builds across the series and is not visible after one appointment

> knop: Not sure whether this treatment suits you? Book a treatment on advice. The therapist looks at your skin and chooses, and you hear beforehand what it will be and what it costs. TO TREATMENT ON ADVICE

**The concerns this belongs to**

Every concern page says what the concern is, what can be done about it and when a different approach gives more.

- Ingrown hairs Bumps after shaving, with a hair that does not come out. READ ABOUT INGROWN HAIRS ›

**What connects to it**

- Laser hair removal € 20 Faster and better value as long as there is pigment in the hairs. Usually this first. WHAT IT INVOLVES

**Frequently asked questions**

Why does the laser not work on grey hair?

Because the laser seeks out the pigment in the hair root and the heat does its work there. Grey and white hair no longer has that pigment, so there is nothing to aim at. That is not down to the device or the setting.

Can I combine it with laser hair removal?

That is the usual order. First the laser course for everything with pigment, and then electrolysis for the hairs left standing. That way you do not pay per hair for what can be done faster.

What does this cost?

Sixty euros per half hour of treatment time, as it stands in the diary too. How much time you need depends on the area and on how many hairs there are; we establish that at the intake.

How long does an appointment take?

Allow 30 minutes at the clinic. That is the time reserved for you in the calendar, including the cleansing beforehand.

How much recovery time do I need?

The treated spots are red for a few hours and can swell slightly, much like after waxing. In most people that is gone the same day.

How often do I need to come?

A series, with a few weeks in between. How many depends on the number of hairs and on the area.

What does it cost?

60 euros per session. Every price is published on the price page.

The therapist looks at your skin, measures with the EVE-M and establishes what suits you. You hear straight away how many sessions it involves and what it costs. If you are treated in the same appointment, the intake fee is waived.

**Where it lands**

A scar is tissue built up differently from the skin around it: tighter, with fibres running in another direction. The laser brings controlled heat into that tissue, after which the healing orders the fibres anew. So the scar becomes flatter and less red, and blends better with the skin around it. Gone it does not go.

**Where it lands**

### /en/treatments/led-therapy/acne

**Tabbladtitel:** LED therapy for acne | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** LED light therapy for acne. What blue light does to the bacterium, why it is not a stand-alone treatment and how often it is needed.

**LED LIGHT THERAPY FOR ACNE**

LED does nothing about the blockage and nothing about the oil. It works on what comes after: the bacterium that thrives in a blocked pore and the inflammation that follows. So it almost never stands alone.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

**Why this here does about it**

In a blocked pore a bacterium grows that occurs naturally in the skin. That bacterium makes substances that react to blue light of a certain wavelength; in doing so oxygen is released that damages the bacterium itself.

Red light does something else: it penetrates deeper and calms the inflammatory response around it. With acne they are therefore often given one after the other, blue on the bacterium and red on the redness.

What LED does not do is clear the pore. Without a cleanse or a peel the blockage stays and the bacterium returns, and then you are treating the same thing over and over.

**What is goes differently than usual**

- Usually straight after, not on its own After a cleanse or a peel, once the pore is clear. Then the light tackles what is still in there rather than what lies on top.

- Blue and red, in that order Blue on the bacterium, red on the inflammation. Which of the two counts more depends on how red and how inflamed your skin is.

- Short but often A session takes twenty minutes and there is no recovery time. It works through repetition, so a series with a few days to a week in between.

**What it gives you**

Calmer skin with fewer inflamed spots, and less redness around the spots that are there. It is the quiet step in an acne programme: no recovery time, no irritation, and the effect comes from the repetition.

*HOW OFTEN*

Usually straight after another treatment.

*RECOVERY TIME*

None.

*FROM*

€ 30

**When you would choose something else**

- As a single treatment it does little; without tackling the blockage it comes back.

- With severe inflamed acne a doctor should take a look.

- Certain medication makes the skin light-sensitive; you should mention that before any light goes on.

**What people asked about this.**

**Can I have LED on its own?**

That is possible, but then you get little out of it. The light works on the bacterium and on the inflammation; if the pore stays blocked it keeps coming back. It is meant as a step within a programme.

**Does it hurt?**

No. You lie for twenty minutes with goggles on under the light and at most you feel some warmth. Afterwards you carry straight on with your day.

**Whether this suits you, your skin will show.**

Everything above applies to this concern in general. What is going on with you and whether this is the right route is established by the therapist at the skin consultation. If the answer is no, you hear that too.

> knop: OR LET US CHOOSE

- Upper dermis This is where the connective tissue starts. What you reach here heals by building. DOES NOT REACH HERE

- Deep dermis Hair roots, vessels and the firmness of your skin. Working this deep needs a reason. DOES NOT REACH HERE

**What happens, in order.**

Every treatment starts with cleansing, and that is done by hand. Make-up and sebum come off and the therapist checks that everything is gone, because a device or an active ingredient that works on a layer never reaches your skin.

- Look first at where the sound sits Not every snoring sound comes from the soft palate. That decides whether this gives you anything.

- Pulses on the palate In a fixed pattern across the tissue, in about half an hour. You are sitting up and fully conscious.

- Three times, with weeks in between The tissue tightens between sessions. After the third you know what it does for you.

NIGHTLASE, DURING THE TREATMENT

**What you notice in the chair**

This treatment works on your palate and not on your skin. Your mouth stays open with a retractor and the laser passes over it in three or four passes.

It is warm and takes getting used to, but it does not hurt. No blade and no anaesthetic is involved.

Afterwards you can eat and drink normally. Some people have a slightly dry throat for a day.

**What this treatment is meant for**

On the left where this treatment works well, on the right when another treatment does more for you.

- Works without cutting, without needles and without anything you have to wear at night

- You can eat, talk and work normally straight afterwards

- Can be repeated when the effect fades

- With breathing pauses, a sleep study through a doctor comes first

- The tissue gives way again after a while, so you repeat it

- If the sound comes from somewhere else, a doctor takes a look

Does it hurt?

You feel warmth at the back of your mouth. No anaesthetic is involved and nothing is cut.

Does it work for sleep apnoea too?

This is not a treatment for that. If pauses in breathing have been reported, or you are unusually sleepy during the day, then a sleep study through your GP comes first. Once you know what is going on, we look at what we can do.

How long does it last?

That differs per person and it is not permanent. We agree beforehand when we look again.

How long does an appointment take?

Allow 30 minutes at the clinic. That is the time reserved for you in the calendar, including the cleansing beforehand.

How much recovery time do I need?

After NightLase you can eat and talk normally. Some people feel a slight scratching in the throat for a while.

How often do I need to come?

A series of three, with about three weeks in between. The effect builds across that series and is not permanent; repeating after a while belongs with it.

### /en/treatments/nordlys-pigmentation/sun-spots

**Tabbladtitel:** Nordlys IPL for sun spots | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Nordlys IPL for sun spots and age spots. Why the spot goes darker first, how many sessions it takes and when it is not possible.

**NORDLYS IPL FOR SUN SPOTS AND AGE SPOTS**

A sun spot is a place where pigment cells have been making too much for years. Light can tackle that build-up precisely, because it seeks out the dark and skips the skin around it.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

**Why this here does about it**

The Nordlys light is absorbed by the pigment in the spot and not by the lighter skin beside it. So exactly the spot heats up and the rest stays cool; that is what sets an IPL apart from a peel, which takes off the whole top layer.

That heat makes the pigment grain break apart and work its way to the surface. In the days after, the spot first becomes darker and grainier, then it flakes away. That darkening is the sign that it has worked.

So this works well on sharply defined spots from the sun, and less on pigment that is diffuse or sits deeper.

**What is goes differently than usual**

- Only on untanned skin The light seeks colour. On tanned skin it hits more than the spot, and that risks discolouration. After the sun we wait.

- Spots separately or a whole area A few separate spots are treated precisely; with scattered sun damage the light goes across the whole cheek or the back of the hand.

- Three to six sessions With four weeks in between, so that there is time to see what has gone before work resumes.

**What it gives you**

Spots that lighten or disappear, with more even skin overall. In the first week after a session it looks worse than before; that belongs with it and is not a setback.

*HOW OFTEN*

A series of three to six, with four weeks in between.

*RECOVERY TIME*

Usually a few hours red.

*FROM*

€ 75

**When you would choose something else**

- With melasma this is often not the right choice: that pigment reacts to heat and can flare from it.

- A spot that changes shape or colour should be assessed by a doctor first, not treated by us.

- On tanned skin it does not go ahead.

**What people asked about this.**

**Why does the spot get darker first?**

Because the pigment has broken apart and is working its way to the surface. After about five to ten days it flakes away. Scratching or scrubbing in that period is the only way to turn it into a mark that stays.

**Do they come back?**

The treated spot does not, but the pigment cells that made it are still there. Without daily protection new ones appear, and then you have spent the same money twice.

**Whether this suits you, your skin will show.**

Everything above applies to this concern in general. What is going on with you and whether this is the right route is established by the therapist at the skin consultation. If the answer is no, you hear that too.

> knop: OR LET US CHOOSE

### /en/treatments/nordlys-redness/rosacea

**Tabbladtitel:** Nordlys IPL for rosacea | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Nordlys IPL for rosacea. What light does about the lasting redness, what it does not do about the flushing, and when a doctor belongs with it.

**NORDLYS IPL FOR ROSACEA**

Rosacea is more than redness: it is skin that overreacts, with flushes, sensitivity and sometimes bumps. Light tackles one part of that, and it is the part you see in the mirror.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

**Why this here does about it**

With rosacea the small blood vessels in the face stand open more often and for longer. Over time they no longer close fully, and then a red background stays even when you are not flushing.

The Nordlys light is absorbed by that blood and closes the vessels, after which the body clears them away. So the fixed redness subsides: the layer that was always there disappears.

What stays is the tendency to flush. That lies in how the vessels react to heat, alcohol, exertion or stress, and light does nothing about that. Anyone who knows beforehand is not disappointed afterwards.

**What is goes differently than usual**

- Starting gently Rosacea skin is easily provoked. The first session at a lower energy, and see what your skin does with it before anything is scaled up.

- Across the whole area, not per vessel With rosacea it is rarely one vein but an area that is structurally red. So the light goes across the whole area.

- Maintenance comes with it After the starting series, once or twice a year. Rosacea does not go away; with this you keep the visible redness in check.

**What it gives you**

Less lasting redness and a more even colour, built over three to six sessions. The sensitivity and the flushing stay; those call for knowing what triggers your skin, and that is not a treatment but knowledge.

*HOW OFTEN*

A series of three to six, with four weeks in between.

*RECOVERY TIME*

A few hours red, and the treated vessels are darker at first before they fade.

*FROM*

€ 75

**When you would choose something else**

- It does not cure rosacea. It removes the visible redness and that can come back.

- With the bumps and spots that come with rosacea, medication from a doctor is often needed; light does little about that.

- With a nose that is thickening and becoming bumpy, that belongs with a doctor and not with us.

**What people asked about this.**

**Will my flushes go away with this?**

No. The light closes vessels that stand permanently open; the tendency to flush lies in how your vessels react and that stays. What does change is the red background that was always there.

**Does this work alongside my doctor's treatment?**

Yes, and often that is the best route: the doctor tackles the bumps and the inflammation, we the visible redness. We agree what happens when.

**What we Nordlys IPL for redness and vessels use it for**

- Nordlys IPL for couperose A visible vessel is a blood vessel that has become wider than it should be and no longer closes on its own.

**Whether this suits you, your skin will show.**

Everything above applies to this concern in general. What is going on with you and whether this is the right route is established by the therapist at the skin consultation. If the answer is no, you hear that too.

### /en/treatments/nordlys-redness/thread-veins

**Tabbladtitel:** Nordlys IPL for couperose | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Nordlys IPL for thread veins and visible vessels. What happens to a vessel, how many sessions it takes and why new ones can appear.

**NORDLYS IPL FOR COUPEROSE**

A visible vessel is a blood vessel that has become wider than it should be and no longer closes on its own. Light can close it, and then your body clears it away. That is the whole mechanism.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

**Why this here does about it**

The Nordlys light is absorbed by the red in the blood, and not by the skin around it. So exactly the vessel heats up and the rest stays cool.

That heat makes the wall of the vessel collapse. Blood can no longer pass through and the body breaks it down in the weeks after. What you see after that is ordinary skin, because that vessel is gone.

Straight after the treatment a vessel can be darker instead. That belongs: it is the sign that it has been hit, and it fades in the days after.

**What is goes differently than usual**

- A filter for the thickness of the vessel A fine vein on the cheek asks for a different setting than a thicker vessel by the nostril. The therapist chooses the filter accordingly.

- Separate vessels precisely, redness across the area With a few visible veins the work is done vessel by vessel. With an area that is structurally red the light goes across the whole area.

- Three to six, with four weeks in between Not everything responds at once, and the time in between is needed to see what has gone.

**What it gives you**

Visibly fewer vessels and a calmer colour. What has gone does not come back: that vessel no longer exists. New ones can appear elsewhere, because the disposition that made them does not change.

*HOW OFTEN*

A series of three to six, with four weeks in between.

*RECOVERY TIME*

A few hours red, and the treated vessels are darker at first before they fade.

*FROM*

€ 75

**When you would choose something else**

- This does not cure the predisposition. Anyone who forms vessels easily keeps doing so; maintenance belongs with it.

- On tanned skin it is not possible: the light seeks colour, and then it hits the tanned skin too.

- With a red nose that is thickening and becoming bumpy, a doctor should take a look.

**What people asked about this.**

**Do the vessels come back?**

The treated vessels do not; they have been cleared away. New ones can appear, because what caused them does not change. For most people that means a session every year or two to keep it up.

**Does it hurt?**

Every flash feels like a short flick with an elastic band. A cool gel goes on and you are given goggles, because you see the light through your eyelids as well.

**What we Nordlys IPL for redness and vessels use it for**

- Nordlys IPL for rosacea Rosacea is more than redness: it is skin that overreacts, with flushes, sensitivity and sometimes bumps.

### /en/treatments/peels/acne

**Tabbladtitel:** Medical peel for acne | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Medical peels for acne in Rotterdam. Which acid works on what, why your skin can become more unsettled first, and how often.

**MEDICAL PEELS FOR ACNE**

A peel for acne is not a clean-up. The acid does two things at once: it clears the opening of the pore and it slows what builds up inside it. Which acid goes on your skin depends on which of those two is the problem for you.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

**Why this here does about it**

Acne starts with a blockage: the wall of the pore renews too quickly, the loose cells stick together and the oil can no longer get out. What follows in bacteria and inflammation sits behind that blockage.

Salicylic acid dissolves in oil and so gets into the pore itself; it loosens the plug where it sits. Glycolic acid works on the top layer and makes loose cells let go sooner. With oily skin and many blackheads the first is the obvious one, with dull skin with blockages the second.

So with acne it is less a question of stronger or weaker and more of which acid acts where. That is what is established at the intake.

**What is goes differently than usual**

- Building up, not full strength at once The first time at a lower strength and a shorter working time. How your skin responds decides the next one.

- Expect a dip In the first weeks the skin can become more unsettled as blockages come to the surface. That is not a worsening; it is what was already underneath.

- A series of four to six With two to four weeks in between, and then maintenance as long as the skin asks for it.

**What it gives you**

Fewer blockages and fewer new spots, usually noticeable from the third session. What a peel does not do is remove existing scars; those call for something else and that comes only once the acne is calm.

*HOW OFTEN*

Usually a series of four to six, with two to four weeks in between.

*RECOVERY TIME*

Two to five days dry and flaky, depending on the strength.

*FROM*

€ 140

**When you would choose something else**

- With severe, inflamed acne with lumps a doctor should take a look; a peel is not the first step then.

- While using isotretinoin no peel is done, and after stopping a waiting period applies.

- On freshly tanned skin a peel does not go ahead.

**What people asked about this.**

**Does my skin get worse first?**

That can happen, in the first weeks. What comes up then was already there; it simply becomes visible sooner. It is part of the course and it passes.

**How often do I need to come?**

Usually four to six times with two to four weeks in between. Then we look at whether maintenance is needed and how often.

**What we Medical peels use it for**

- Medical peel for pigmentation Pigment lies at different depths, and a peel reaches only one of them.

- Medical peel for skin rejuvenation Skin that looks tired is often not slack but dull: the top layer renews more slowly, lies less evenly and so reflects light unevenly.

**Whether this suits you, your skin will show.**

Everything above applies to this concern in general. What is going on with you and whether this is the right route is established by the therapist at the skin consultation. If the answer is no, you hear that too.

### /en/treatments/peels/pigmentation

**Tabbladtitel:** Medical peel for pigmentation | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Medical peels for pigment spots. Why the sun decides the result, when a peel does work and when a programme fits better.

**MEDICAL PEELS FOR PIGMENTATION**

Pigment lies at different depths, and a peel reaches only one of them. That is the whole trade-off: if the spot sits in the top layer, you can carry it off. If it sits deeper, you take the top off and it comes back.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

**Why this here does about it**

A pigment spot is a place where the pigment cells have made too much. With sun damage that pigment usually sits high, in the epidermis, and that layer renews itself continuously.

A peel speeds up that renewal. The cells with too much pigment are carried off sooner and the new ones beneath have less in them. That is why it works on superficial pigment and not on pigment that sits in the dermis.

Sun here is not a side issue but half the result. Every exposure sets the pigment cells working again, and then you are removing what comes straight back.

**What is goes differently than usual**

- Preparing with products at home Two to four weeks beforehand, slowing what the pigment cells do. Without that preparation the chance of a patchy result is higher.

- Preferably in autumn or winter Not because it cannot be done otherwise, but because the months after decide whether it lasts. Less sun means more result.

- Daily protection, not advice but part of it Without protection the pigment comes back, and then the series was money thrown away.

**What it gives you**

More even skin with lighter spots, built over a series. With stubborn or deeper pigment a programme of months is a more realistic route than separate peels; you hear that at the intake, not halfway through.

*HOW OFTEN*

Usually a series of four to six, with two to four weeks in between.

*RECOVERY TIME*

Two to five days dry and flaky, depending on the strength.

*FROM*

€ 140

**When you would choose something else**

- With melasma an ordinary peel is often not the right choice: that pigment reacts to heat and hormones and can flare from it.

- On pigment-rich skin there is a chance of discolouration after the peel; the strength is tuned to that and sometimes we advise against it.

- On tanned skin it does not go ahead.

**What people asked about this.**

**Do the spots come back?**

If you go into the sun unprotected, yes. The pigment cells are still there and they do again what they did. Daily protection here is not a tip but the difference between a result and no result.

**Which is better, a peel or Cosmelan?**

That depends on how deep the pigment sits and how stubborn it is. A peel is lighter and easier to do on its own; Cosmelan is a programme of months and tackles what separate peels founder on. At the intake the therapist establishes which of the two fits.

**What we Medical peels use it for**

- Medical peel for acne A peel for acne is not a clean-up.

- Medical peel for skin rejuvenation Skin that looks tired is often not slack but dull: the top layer renews more slowly, lies less evenly and so reflects light unevenly.

**Whether this suits you, your skin will show.**

Everything above applies to this concern in general. What is going on with you and whether this is the right route is established by the therapist at the skin consultation. If the answer is no, you hear that too.

### /en/treatments/peels/skin-rejuvenation

**Tabbladtitel:** Medical peel for skin rejuvenation | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Medical peels for skin rejuvenation. What a peel does for dull, uneven skin and where the limit lies.

**MEDICAL PEELS FOR SKIN REJUVENATION**

Skin that looks tired is often not slack but dull: the top layer renews more slowly, lies less evenly and so reflects light unevenly. That is exactly the layer a peel works on.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

**Why this here does about it**

From about thirty it takes longer for a skin cell to reach the surface from below. More dead cells are left lying, and they do not lie neatly. Light falling on them reflects in all directions, and that is what we see as dull.

A peel loosens that top layer in one go, so that the new layer beneath comes to lie more evenly. That is visible straight away and it is also why the effect is temporary: the skin simply carries on slowing down.

With repetition more happens. A series of peels also gets the production in the layer beneath going, and then it is not only about glow but about firmness too.

**What is goes differently than usual**

- Strength to what your skin can take From a superficial peel with no recovery time to a stronger one that peels for a few days. Which it becomes depends on your skin and on how many days you have.

- Combines well With needling in the same series: the peel on the top layer, the needling on the connective tissue beneath. Two layers, two kinds of result.

- Maintenance rather than a course Four to six to begin with, then every few months. It is a maintenance treatment and that is not a shortcoming.

**What it gives you**

Fresher, more even skin that reflects light more calmly, noticeable straight after the first session and firmer after a series. Deep lines and slackness fall outside this.

*HOW OFTEN*

Usually a series of four to six, with two to four weeks in between.

*RECOVERY TIME*

Two to five days dry and flaky, depending on the strength.

*FROM*

€ 140

**When you would choose something else**

- A fold formed by muscle movement does not go away with this.

- With real laxity, tightening with laser is what is called for; a peel does not reach that layer.

- With a sensitive or damaged barrier we start with repairing and not with taking away.

**What people asked about this.**

**How long does it last?**

The glow of one peel lasts weeks. The firmness a series builds lasts months, and after that it asks for maintenance. That is not a sales trick but how skin renewal works.

**Do I have to take time off for it?**

With a superficial peel, no; you are red for a few hours. With a stronger one you peel for a few days, and then we would rather not schedule it just before something important.

**What we Medical peels use it for**

- Medical peel for acne A peel for acne is not a clean-up.

- Medical peel for pigmentation Pigment lies at different depths, and a peel reaches only one of them.

**Whether this suits you, your skin will show.**

### /en/treatments/skinpen/acne-scarring

**Tabbladtitel:** SkinPen for acne scars | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Microneedling with the SkinPen or Dermapen 4 for acne scars in Rotterdam. What it does for pits, what it does not do for marks, and how many sessions it takes.

**MICRONEEDLING FOR ACNE SCARS**

Acne scars are not marks but shapes: the skin is missing connective tissue there, and so it catches the light differently. No cream helps against that and no peel; those work on colour and on the top layer. Microneedling works on the shape. We do the same treatment with the Dermapen 4 as well; which pen it becomes is chosen by the therapist per area.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

**Why this here does about it**

An acne scar forms because inflammation has cleared away connective tissue and too little has come back in its place. What is left is a pit in which light makes a shadow, and it is that shadow you see in the mirror.

The pen places hundreds of channels down into the upper dermis, exactly the layer where that connective tissue sits. The body repairs those channels with new collagen, and that fills up the floor of the pit. Not at once: the building carries on over weeks to months, and that is why you see nothing yet after the first session.

With acne scars that is the whole story. It is not about the colour but about the depth: the less difference in height, the less shadow, the less you see the scar.

**What is goes differently than usual**

- Deeper than in an ordinary session For texture the work goes deeper than for skin improvement. The therapist sets the depth per area; more is possible on the cheek than on the jawline.

- The acne first, then the scar As long as there is active inflammation, no work is done on scars. Prompting inflamed skin makes new scars more likely, not less.

- A series, not a session Four to six times with four to six weeks in between. That time in between is not waiting but the treatment: it is when the collagen is made.

**What it gives you**

Count on months and on improvement, not on disappearance. Pits become shallower and the skin looks more even; a scar that is no longer there is a promise nobody can keep. What still stands after the series we look at together before deciding whether more makes sense.

*HOW OFTEN*

A series of three to six, with four to six weeks in between.

*RECOVERY TIME*

One to three days red, like a strong sun flush.

*FROM*

€ 180

**When you would choose something else**

- With dark or red marks without a dent this is not the first choice: that is colour, and light or a peel works better on it.

- With deep, sharply bordered pits (ice-pick scars) needling often does not go far enough; then a fractional laser is a more realistic route.

- If you are prone to keloid, nothing is prompted before a doctor has taken a look.

**What people asked about this.**

**Is it possible if I still have acne?**

Not on the places where it is active. We start with the acne itself; once the skin is calm, there is something to work on that stays calm too.

**How many sessions do I need?**

Usually four to six, with four to six weeks in between. How many it becomes for you depends on how deep the scars sit and how your skin responds to the first.

**What we Microneedling with the SkinPen use it for**

- SkinPen for coarse pores A pore cannot close; oil has to get out.

- SkinPen for fine lines There are two kinds of line and they ask for different things.

- SkinPen for surgical scars A surgical scar is different tissue from the skin around it: the connective tissue lies in one direction instead of criss-cross.

- Microneedling for stretch marks Stretch marks are tears in the dermis formed from within because the skin was stretched faster than it could grow with.

**Whether this suits you, your skin will show.**

Everything above applies to this concern in general. What is going on with you and whether this is the right route is established by the therapist at the skin consultation. If the answer is no, you hear that too.

### /en/treatments/skinpen/fine-lines

**Tabbladtitel:** SkinPen for fine lines | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Microneedling for fine lines. Why it works on surface lines and not on a deep fold, and how long it takes.

**MICRONEEDLING FOR FINE WRINKLES**

There are two kinds of line and they ask for different things. A fine line is there even when you relax your face and comes from skin that has become thinner and drier. A fold forms because a muscle pulls the skin together. This works on the first kind; not on the second. We do the same treatment with the Dermapen 4 as well; which pen it becomes is chosen by the therapist per area.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

**Why this here does about it**

From about twenty-five the skin makes slightly less collagen every year. So the upper dermis becomes thinner and the top layer sits more loosely, and that is what you see as a fine network of lines.

Needling gets healing going in exactly that layer. The new collagen makes the skin slightly thicker and firmer, and thicker skin folds into small lines less easily.

That is not filling. Nothing is introduced; the skin makes it itself, which is why the effect builds over weeks and also fades again gradually.

**What is goes differently than usual**

- Carefully around the eyes The skin at the eye socket is thinner than the rest of the face. There the work is done at a lower setting, and sometimes not at all.

- Often with a booster alongside In the same appointment hyaluronic acid can go into the channels with it. That makes the skin feel fuller straight away while the building gets going.

- Three to six, and then maintenance With four weeks in between. Then once or twice a year to hold on to what has been built.

**What it gives you**

After the series, skin that feels smoother and in which the finest lines stand out less. The best moment to compare is three months after the last session, because then the building is finished.

*HOW OFTEN*

A series of three to six, with four to six weeks in between.

*RECOVERY TIME*

One to three days red, like a strong sun flush.

*FROM*

€ 180

**When you would choose something else**

- A fold between the eyebrows or a smile line formed by muscle movement does not go away with this. We do not work with injectables for that.

- With a drooping eyelid or genuinely slack skin this is too light; then tightening with laser is more to the point.

- On freshly tanned skin we wait, even at a light setting.

**What people asked about this.**

**Is this an alternative to botox?**

No, it works on something else. Botox relaxes a muscle and thereby removes a fold; needling changes the quality of the skin itself. On a muscle fold needling does little, on thin skin with fine lines botox does little.

**How soon do I see something?**

In the first days your skin looks fresher from the swelling; that is not yet a result. What lasts starts building after about four weeks and carries on for roughly three months.

**What we Microneedling with the SkinPen use it for**

- SkinPen for acne scars Acne scars are not marks but shapes: the skin is missing connective tissue there, and so it catches the light differently.

- SkinPen for coarse pores A pore cannot close; oil has to get out.

- SkinPen for surgical scars A surgical scar is different tissue from the skin around it: the connective tissue lies in one direction instead of criss-cross.

- Microneedling for stretch marks Stretch marks are tears in the dermis formed from within because the skin was stretched faster than it could grow with.

**Whether this suits you, your skin will show.**

Everything above applies to this concern in general. What is going on with you and whether this is the right route is established by the therapist at the skin consultation. If the answer is no, you hear that too.

### /en/treatments/skinpen/large-pores

**Tabbladtitel:** SkinPen for coarse pores | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Microneedling for coarse pores and uneven skin texture. What does change, what does not, and why pores do not get smaller.

**MICRONEEDLING FOR COARSE PORES**

A pore cannot close; oil has to get out. What can happen is that the rim around it becomes firmer, and that is exactly the difference between a pore that stands out and a pore you do not see. We do the same treatment with the Dermapen 4 as well; which pen it becomes is chosen by the therapist per area.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

**Why this here does about it**

Pores draw the eye when the skin around them is slack. The opening itself is about the same size in everyone; what differs is whether the rim stands taut or has sunk a little. With a sunken rim shadow falls in and then the opening looks bigger than it is.

Microneedling gets new collagen going in the upper dermis. That is the tissue holding that rim up, and when it tightens the opening becomes less deep and catches less shadow.

So this is a texture treatment and not a cleanse. Emptying a pore helps for a few days; firming the rim lasts longer.

**What is goes differently than usual**

- Shallower and across a larger area For texture, coverage counts more than depth. The work goes across the whole area rather than on separate spots, at a setting lighter than for scars.

- Often combined with cleansing A HydraFacial beforehand removes what is in the pores. Needling on a full pore is the wrong order.

- Maintenance comes with it After the starting series, a session per quarter holds the result. Collagen breaks down again; that is not failure but how skin works.

**What it gives you**

Skin that looks more even and reflects light more evenly, usually visible from the third session. What does not happen is that pores disappear: if anyone promises that, they are promising something about anatomy that is not true.

*HOW OFTEN*

A series of three to six, with four to six weeks in between.

*RECOVERY TIME*

One to three days red, like a strong sun flush.

*FROM*

€ 180

**When you would choose something else**

- With oily skin and many blackheads, cleansing and oil control is the first step; needling does little about that.

- With active inflammation nothing is prompted.

- Anyone looking for an immediately visible difference will be disappointed here: this works over months.

**What people asked about this.**

**Do my pores get smaller?**

No. The opening stays; what changes is the firmness of the skin around it, so that less shadow falls into it and it stands out less.

**What is the difference from a HydraFacial for this?**

A HydraFacial takes out what is in there and you see that straight away; it lasts days to weeks. Needling changes the skin around it and that takes months. The two do not clash, they work on different things.

**What we Microneedling with the SkinPen use it for**

- SkinPen for acne scars Acne scars are not marks but shapes: the skin is missing connective tissue there, and so it catches the light differently.

- SkinPen for fine lines There are two kinds of line and they ask for different things.

- SkinPen for surgical scars A surgical scar is different tissue from the skin around it: the connective tissue lies in one direction instead of criss-cross.

- Microneedling for stretch marks Stretch marks are tears in the dermis formed from within because the skin was stretched faster than it could grow with.

**Whether this suits you, your skin will show.**

### /en/treatments/skinpen/stretch-marks

**Tabbladtitel:** Microneedling for stretch marks | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Microneedling for stretch marks. Why red stretch marks respond better than white ones, and what does and does not change.

**MICRONEEDLING FOR STRETCH MARKS**

Stretch marks are tears in the dermis formed from within because the skin was stretched faster than it could grow with. The colour tells you how old they are, and that age decides what there is left to gain. We do the same treatment with the Dermapen 4 as well; which pen it becomes is chosen by the therapist per area.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

**Why this here does about it**

Fresh stretch marks are red or purple: vessels still run through them and the tissue is still at work. In that phase the skin responds best to a prompt, because the healing is still going and you push it one way.

White stretch marks have run their course. The tissue is thinner by then and there is little pigment in it, and that does not come back. What can happen is that the texture improves: the marks become less deep and the edge less sharp, so that they stand out less.

In both cases needling gets new collagen going in the layer where the tear sits. With red stretch marks that yields more than with white ones, and you ought to know that difference before starting a series.

**What is goes differently than usual**

- Deeper than on the face The skin on the stomach, hips and thighs is thicker. The depth is tuned to that and differs per area.

- Large areas, a longer appointment Stretch marks are rarely in one place. Count on a longer session than a facial treatment.

- Six to eight sessions With four to six weeks in between. On the body, healing goes more slowly than on the face.

**What it gives you**

Less deep stretch marks with a more even surface. With red stretch marks, often less colour difference too. What does not happen is that they disappear: the scar stays, it draws the eye less.

*HOW OFTEN*

A series of three to six, with four to six weeks in between.

*RECOVERY TIME*

One to three days red, like a strong sun flush.

*FROM*

€ 180

**When you would choose something else**

- White stretch marks respond less than red ones. That is not a setting that can be changed; it is what there is left to repair.

- During pregnancy and breastfeeding we do not treat.

- On freshly tanned skin we wait, on the body too.

**What people asked about this.**

**Does it work on old, white stretch marks too?**

Less well than on red ones. The texture can improve so that they stand out less, but the colour does not come back. At the intake we look at which of the two you have, because that decides whether it is worth it.

**Is it possible during pregnancy?**

No. We do not treat during pregnancy or breastfeeding, not on the body either.

**What we Microneedling with the SkinPen use it for**

- SkinPen for acne scars Acne scars are not marks but shapes: the skin is missing connective tissue there, and so it catches the light differently.

- SkinPen for coarse pores A pore cannot close; oil has to get out.

- SkinPen for fine lines There are two kinds of line and they ask for different things.

- SkinPen for surgical scars A surgical scar is different tissue from the skin around it: the connective tissue lies in one direction instead of criss-cross.

**Whether this suits you, your skin will show.**

### /en/treatments/skinpen/surgical-scars

**Tabbladtitel:** SkinPen for surgical scars | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Microneedling for scars after surgery or a caesarean. When you can start, what changes and when a doctor looks first.

**MICRONEEDLING FOR SURGICAL SCARS**

A surgical scar is different tissue from the skin around it: the connective tissue lies in one direction instead of criss-cross. So it is tighter, shinier and often somewhat raised or, conversely, drawn in. Needling reorders that tissue. We do the same treatment with the Dermapen 4 as well; which pen it becomes is chosen by the therapist per area.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

**Why this here does about it**

In normal skin the collagen fibres lie criss-cross, and that makes the skin supple in every direction. In a scar they lie parallel, because that is how the wound was pulled shut. That tissue is strong but stiff, and it reflects light differently.

Microneedling makes thousands of tiny wounds in that stiff tissue that heal again. In that second healing the new collagen lies less tightly in one direction, and the scar becomes more supple and less sharply bordered.

That works best once the scar has matured and is no longer changing: usually from six months after the operation, sometimes later.

**What is goes differently than usual**

- Not before it is ready A scar that is still red is changing on its own, and prompting it can disturb that. We wait until at least six months after the procedure.

- Only on and just beside the scar Work is done on the tissue itself and a little around it, so that the transition to ordinary skin becomes smoother.

- More sessions than on ordinary skin Scar tissue responds more slowly. Count on six to eight sessions, with four to six weeks in between.

**What it gives you**

A scar that feels more supple, shines less and stands out less sharply against the skin around it. The line stays visible; what changes is how much it draws the eye.

*HOW OFTEN*

A series of three to six, with four to six weeks in between.

*RECOVERY TIME*

One to three days red, like a strong sun flush.

*FROM*

€ 180

**When you would choose something else**

- With a keloid or a tendency towards one, nothing is prompted before a doctor or dermatologist has taken a look: too strong a prompt makes a keloid bigger.

- With a scar less than six months old we wait.

- With a scar that opens, itches or changes colour, a doctor should look first.

**What people asked about this.**

**Is it possible on a caesarean scar?**

Often yes, if the scar has matured and is calm. The therapist assesses it first; if there is doubt about the type of scar we consult your doctor.

**When can I start after my operation?**

Usually not before six months. Before that the scar is still changing on its own and there is nothing to gain by prompting it.

**What we Microneedling with the SkinPen use it for**

- SkinPen for acne scars Acne scars are not marks but shapes: the skin is missing connective tissue there, and so it catches the light differently.

- SkinPen for coarse pores A pore cannot close; oil has to get out.

- SkinPen for fine lines There are two kinds of line and they ask for different things.

- Microneedling for stretch marks Stretch marks are tears in the dermis formed from within because the skin was stretched faster than it could grow with.

**Whether this suits you, your skin will show.**

Everything above applies to this concern in general. What is going on with you and whether this is the right route is established by the therapist at the skin consultation. If the answer is no, you hear that too.

### /en/treatments/smootheye

**Tabbladtitel:** SmoothEye: laser around the eye contour | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Laser around the eye contour, for crow's feet and fine lines. From € 150, 60 minutes. At Diba Clinics in Rotterdam.

**SMOOTHEYE**

*HOW DEEP*

Upper dermis

*HOW LONG*

60 minutes

*RECOVERY*

A few hours slightly red around the eyes.

*HOW OFTEN*

A series of three to four, with a few weeks in between.

> knop: Single treatment € 150

> knop: Course of three € 395

> knop: With RRS Eyes € 280

> knop: With RRS Eyes, course of three € 600

Laser around the eye contour, for crow's feet and fine lines.

> knop: BOOK A CONSULTATION

**Where it lands**

The skin around your eyes is the thinnest on your face and so slackens first. SmoothEye heats that area with a long, slow pulse in which the top layer stays cool. Existing collagen contracts and new production gets going, which makes the fine lines less sharp and the eyelid a little firmer.

This runs on Fotona TimeWalker

- Stratum corneum to 0.02 mm Dead cells and lipids. The water barrier.

- Epidermis to 0.1 mm Pigment cells and the dividing layer that new skin comes from.

- Upper dermis to 0.5 mm Fine vessels, nerve endings and young collagen.

- Deep dermis to 2 mm Hair roots, sebaceous glands, larger vessels and the supporting collagen.

- Stratum corneumto 0.02 mmDead cells and lipids. The water barrier.

- Epidermisto 0.1 mmPigment cells and the dividing layer that new skin comes from.

- Upper dermisto 0.5 mmFine vessels, nerve endings and young collagen.

- Deep dermisto 2 mmHair roots, sebaceous glands, larger vessels and the supporting collagen.

The proportions are schematic; the depths beside them are not. Usual values for facial skin. The thickness differs per place on the body; on the back the dermis is a multiple of this. How deep we work in your case depends on the setting the therapist chooses.

WHAT HAPPENS

- 1 Pulse down The light aims at water in the tissue and not at colour. So it works where nothing is brown too.

- 2 Heat at depth The tissue warms in a controlled way, exactly as deep as the setting allows.

- 3 Weeks of repair The building comes after. What you see that day is swelling, not a result.

ACTS ON

Water

Every skin cell is largely water. Aim at that and you hit tissue and not colour.

It runs on its own. Click a step to steer it yourself.

- Stratum corneum The outer layer of dead cells. What happens here shows quickly and heals quickly. PASSES THROUGH HERE

- Epidermis Where your pigment sits and where new skin cells come from. IT WORKS HERE

- Upper dermis This is where the connective tissue starts. What you reach here heals by building. IT WORKS HERE

- Deep dermis Hair roots, vessels and the firmness of your skin. Working this deep needs a reason. DOES NOT REACH HERE

**What happens, in order.**

Every treatment starts with cleansing, and that is done by hand. Make-up and sebum come off and the therapist checks that everything is gone, because a device or an active ingredient that works on a layer never reaches your skin.

- Eyes protected Metal eye shields go under your eyelids. They stay in for the whole treatment.

- Heat around the eye The handpiece passes in calm strips across the eye contour. The warmth rises and lingers there a while.

- Straight on The skin is slightly pink for a few hours. Make-up is usually fine again the same day.

**What you notice in the chair**

The eye shields take getting used to and feel cool. Once they are in you see nothing, and that lasts the whole treatment.

What you feel is a warmth rising around your eye. The therapist asks along the way how warm it is and adjusts accordingly.

**What this treatment is meant for**

On the left where this treatment works well, on the right when another treatment does more for you.

- Works on the thin skin around the eyes, where many treatments are not allowed

- Softens crow's feet and fine lines

- Needs no needles and no recovery time

- For dark circles from pigment or vessels you choose a different treatment

- For a real excess of eyelid skin this is too light; that is surgery

- This is a series; from a single session you see little

> knop: Not sure whether this treatment suits you? Book a treatment on advice. The therapist looks at your skin and chooses, and you hear beforehand what it will be and what it costs. TO TREATMENT ON ADVICE

- Under-eye bags Volume under your eyes: fluid, fat or a shadow. READ ABOUT UNDER-EYE BAGS ›

**What connects to it**

- VectorLift € 150 Works above the eyebrow, where SmoothEye works below it. WHAT IT INVOLVES

- Fotona 4D € 370 The complete facial treatment on the same device. WHAT IT INVOLVES

**Frequently asked questions**

Is it safe that close to your eyes?

Yes, with the metal eye shields that go underneath. They screen the eye completely and stay in for the whole treatment.

Does this help against dark circles?

Usually not. Circles come from pigment, from vessels showing through or from shadow, and that calls for a different approach. Which it is for you we establish at the intake.

How many sessions do I need?

Usually three to four, with a few weeks in between. Then you keep it up with an occasional session.

How long does an appointment take?

Allow 60 minutes at the clinic. That is the time reserved for you in the calendar, including the cleansing beforehand.

How much recovery time do I need?

A few hours slightly red around the eyes. Usually you walk straight out with it.

How often do I need to come?

What does it cost?

From 150 euros; the amount depends on the option you choose. Every option is on the price page.

The therapist looks at your skin, measures with the EVE-M and establishes what suits you. You hear straight away how many sessions it involves and what it costs. If you are treated in the same appointment, the intake fee is waived.

What is the difference from a chemical peel?

With a chemical peel an agent does the work and the working time decides the depth. Here light does the work and the therapist sets the depth per pulse.

Is this possible just before an occasion?

Count on a few hours of redness. The day before is usually manageable; the same day is tight.

What does it cost?

That depends on the area and on whether you have it separately or as part of 4D. We establish that at the intake.

How long does an appointment take?

Allow 60 minutes at the clinic. That is the time reserved for you in the calendar, including the cleansing beforehand.

How much recovery time do I need?

A few hours slightly red. Make-up is usually fine again the next day.

How often do I need to come?

As a one-off refresher or as a series. Also the last step of Fotona 4D.

**Where it lands**

VectorLift heats the tissue of your forehead and the area above your eyebrow in set strips. Because collagen contracts and new production gets going, the eyebrow comes to sit a little higher and the forehead becomes firmer. It is a matter of millimetres and of your own tissue, not of a surgical lift.

This runs on Fotona TimeWalker

### /en/vacancies/skin-therapist

**Tabbladtitel:** Skin therapist vacancy Rotterdam | Diba Clinics

**Google-omschrijving:** Skin therapist vacancy at Diba Clinics in Rotterdam. Working with the EVE-M, Fotona, Nordlys, SkinPen and peels, in a team of eleven. Part-time or full-time.

**SKIN THERAPIST VACANCY IN ROTTERDAM**

Diba Clinics is a skin clinic in Rotterdam North. We treat acne, pigmentation, scars, skin improvement and unwanted hair growth, and since 2017 we have worked with a fixed team of eleven.

We are looking for a skin therapist who runs a clinic independently: measuring, drawing up a treatment plan and carrying that plan out themselves on the equipment we have.

> knop: APPLY FOR THIS POSITION

> knop: ASK A QUESTION FIRST

Prefer to call? You can, on 010-2038423.

*CONTRACT*

Part-time or full-time

*HOURS*

24 to 38 hours, by arrangement

*LOCATION*

Weissenbruchlaan 166, 3054 LS Rotterdam. Posted on 4 September 2026.

**What you do**

You run a clinic of your own: you measure, you draw up the plan and you carry it out yourself. Four parts that come back every week.

- Measuring and assessing Every programme starts with a skin analysis on the EVE-M. You assess what you see, record it under fixed lighting and discuss the outcome with the client.

- A plan that holds You establish which treatment fits, in which order and over how many sessions. You assess contraindications yourself and explain why something is or is not possible.

- Treating yourself Laser, IPL, microneedling, peels and mesotherapy. You set the equipment to the skin type and the area, and adjust on what the skin does in between.

- Watching the programme At every check-up you put the images side by side. If an approach gives too little, you change it rather than sitting it out.

BETWEEN TWO APPOINTMENTS

**What we ask and offer**

On the left the requirements that really matter, on the right what stands against them at Diba. Both lists are the same length, deliberately.

- A completed bachelor's degree in Skin Therapy (The Hague University of Applied Sciences or HU Utrecht)

- Listed in the Dutch Quality Register for Paramedics, or able to meet that shortly

- Experience with laser, IPL or microneedling, or willingness to be trained in them

- You can explain what you do in plain language, including when the answer disappoints

- Available at least two evenings a month, because Wednesday and Thursday run until 21:00

- A permanent place in a team of eleven, with skin therapists and orthomolecular skin specialists side by side

- Equipment that is there and works: Fotona TimeWalker, Nordlys IPL, GentleMax Pro, SkinPen, Dermapen 4, U225 and the EVE-M

- Time for an hour-long intake, because that is where every programme starts

- Room for continuing education, partly because the Quality Register asks for those points

- A clinic in Rotterdam North with parking in the street

**From email to a day alongside us**

Three steps, and you know beforehand what is coming. There is no assessment in it and no round with five people at a table.

- You send something An email to info@dibaclinics.nl with your CV. A cover letter is not needed; a few lines about where you work now and what you are looking for is enough.

- We call You hear something within a week. That conversation takes a quarter of an hour and is about what you do now and what you would want to do here.

- You spend a day with us You work alongside us in the clinic, see the equipment and meet the team. After that you both know enough to form a view.

**Frequently asked questions**

Can I apply as a graduate?

Yes. A skin therapy degree is the requirement; experience with specific equipment is not. You are trained on the devices you do not yet know.

Do I work with my own calendar?

You run a clinic of your own and see your own clients again at the check-ups. The calendar is scheduled by the practice manager.

How many hours are available?

24 to 38 hours, by arrangement. Wednesday and Thursday run until 21:00 and Saturday until 18:00, so evenings and Saturdays are part of the rota.

Is there a salary indication?

We discuss that in the first conversation, along with the hours and the start date.

Where exactly is the clinic?

At Weissenbruchlaan 166, 3054 LS Rotterdam, in Rotterdam North. By car you park in the street and by public transport you are inside in a little under half an hour from Rotterdam Centraal.

**Send your CV, we will discuss the rest**

A cover letter is not needed. A few lines about where you work now and what you are looking for is enough, and you hear something within a week.

**Lo que la gente pregunta más**

Estas son las preguntas que más se hacen antes de pedir cita. Si la tuya no está, llámanos o escríbenos por WhatsApp.

¿Tengo que saber ya qué tratamiento quiero?

No. Vienes justamente para que te asesoremos. Vemos juntos qué encaja con tu piel y con tu objetivo.

¿Cuánto cuesta una primera cita?

Una consulta previa sola con consejo de tratamiento cuesta 50 euros y dura treinta minutos. Si reservas un tratamiento con asesoramiento, reservamos dos horas si es tu primera vez y una hora si ya eres cliente; el importe de la consulta previa no se cobra en cuanto tratamos.

¿Puedo reservar solo la primera consulta?

Sí, y es una de las dos formas de empezar cuando todavía no sabes qué necesitas. La consulta de la piel dura treinta minutos: medir, explicación y un plan que te llevas a casa. La otra forma es un tratamiento con asesoramiento, en el que en la misma cita también tratamos si se puede. Tú decides cuál de las dos.

¿Siempre hace falta un análisis de piel?

No siempre. Cuando un escáner de la piel aporta algo, te explicamos qué medimos y por qué.

**Pide una primera consulta con nosotros en Róterdam.**

Si solo quieres consejo, la cita dura treinta minutos y cuesta 50 euros. Si reservas un tratamiento con asesoramiento, reservamos dos horas si es tu primera vez y una hora si ya eres cliente; el importe de la consulta previa no se cobra en cuanto tratamos.
